author: tamird
body:
git_repository checks add_prefix containment with a raw string prefix.
A normalized path can therefore select a sibling whose name shares the
checkout-root prefix, and the worker deletes that sibling before
fetching.

Require a path-component boundary (or the root itself) and cover the
destructive sibling case with a sentinel regression.

Follow-up to #29453.

author: antawatec
body:
## Qué hace

Habilita el eslabón que faltaba para el login de técnicos: el **alta y revocación de la cuenta**. La vista `/tecnico`, el rol y todo el RLS (0020–0022, 0027) ya estaban en prod; lo que no existía era una forma de crear el `auth.user` + `profiles(role='technician')` + enlazar `technicians.profile_id` (todo requiere service_role).

- **Edge Function `technician-access`** con `action: invite | create | revoke`:
  - `invite`: `inviteUserByEmail` — al técnico le llega el correo con link (`token_hash` + `type=invite` → `/auth/callback` del FE) y define su clave al entrar.
  - `create`: `createUser` con contraseña temporal que el dueño comparte en mano.
  - `revoke`: `deleteUser` — la cascada borra el profile, el FK deja `technicians.profile_id` NULL, la RLS deniega **al instante** aunque el JWT siga vivo, y el historial queda intacto (referencia `technicians.id`). Delete y no ban: re-otorgar = volver a invitar.
- **Auth in-code** (mismo patrón que bank-transfer-approval): JWT contra GoTrue + rol `shop_owner` + el técnico debe ser de SU taller (404 uniforme, no filtra existencia cross-shop). Backstop en revoke: jamás borra un usuario que no sea technician de ese shop.
- **Re-entrante**: el usuario nace con marker en `user_metadata` (`invited_as`/`technician_id`/`shop_id`). Un huérfano de una corrida a medias se **borra y recrea** en el retry (adoptarlo dejaba la contraseña sin setear o el invite sin re-enviar — hallazgo de revisión adversarial). Cuentas sin nuestro marker jamás se tocan.
- **Carreras cubiertas** (2ª ronda de revisión): relectura del link antes de limpiar un huérfano (doble submit no destruye un acceso recién creado) y revoke concurrente → `alreadyRevoked` en vez de un 500 con log falso de corrupción.
- `findAuthUserByEmail`/`isAlreadyRegistered` extraídos a `_shared/authAdmin.ts` (move puro; provisionTenant los importa).
- Template de invite con **copy neutro** (GoTrue tiene UN template y ahora lo comparten el onboarding del dueño y el alta de técnicos).
- **SIN migración SQL**: todo corre con service_role sobre el esquema existente.

## Verificación

- `deno check` verde en los 5 entrypoints.
- E2E contra el stack local (27 checks): alta por ambos métodos, login del técnico, RLS deny-by-default (ve solo SUS órdenes, cero inventario), 400/403/404/409, email de invitación en Mailpit con subject y link correctos, `already_linked`/`alreadyRevoked` idempotentes, revocación inmediata con JWT vivo, historial intacto, huérfano con marker recreado con la clave nueva funcionando.
- Revisión adversarial multi-agente: 3 hallazgos confirmados en el BE, los 3 arreglados en este PR.
- Quirk local (no afecta prod): el file-server de templates de la CLI muere tras `supabase db reset` → emails salen stock hasta `supabase stop && start`.

## Deploy (manual, tras merge)

1. `supabase functions deploy technician-access` (el config.toml ya trae su entry `verify_jwt = false` documentado).
2. **Dashboard hosted → Auth → Email Templates → "Invite user"**: pegar el subject/body nuevos (copy neutro) — mismo día, porque el template lo comparten dueños y técnicos.
3. Confirmar que el secret `ONBOARDING_REDIRECT_URL` sigue seteado.

FE hermano: AntawaTec/AntawaTec-FE (UI de Equipo + `/tecnico/clave` + redirect del callback) — mergear este primero.

body:
## Что сделано
Перенос админ-режима gtport (страница Dictionaries + кнопка перезагрузки словарей) — в универсальной манере проекта.

### Backend
- **Миграция 000033**: реестр редактируемых таблиц `dpport.list_tables` (эталонный приём gtport: редактор работает только с перечисленными таблицами; сейчас `marka` и `stations` — новый справочник в редакторе добавляется одной INSERT-строкой, без правки кода) + суррогатный `marka.id` bigserial (естественный ключ marka составной, универсальному CRUD нужен одноколоночный; в старом GTport id был).
- **Универсальный CRUD** `/api/v1/admin/tables[/{table}[/{id}]]` (list / data / create / update / delete). Безопасность: имена таблиц строго из реестра, имена колонок из information_schema, всё квотируется, значения — параметрами (канон GORM-гибрида для динамического SQL). Доступ — только роль **administrator** (`RequireRole` из шаблона).
- Сервис `AdminTables`: валидация таблицы по реестру, отбрасывание неизвестных полей, приведение JSON-типов к типам колонок (целые float64 → int64 для bigint), контроль обязательных полей.
- Правки в БД кэш не перечитывают — применение к снимку отдельной явной кнопкой (`dict_reload`, как в эталоне: правки → «Обновить справочники»).

### Frontend
- Раздел **«Админ»** в меню (виден только administrator): селектор справочника из реестра, таблица с поиском по всем полям, «Добавить»/правка в модальной динамической форме (число/текст/переключатель по типам колонок, обязательные помечены), удаление с подтверждением; уведомления тостами.
- Кнопка **«Обновить справочники» перенесена** со страницы «Дислокация» сюда — весь цикл правки словарей на одной странице.

## Проверка
`go build/vet/test ./...` и typecheck фронта зелёные; миграция применена к dev; владелец проверил редактор вживую (роль administrator).

author: sean-starlabs
body:
## Summary

- connect only eligible active storage boot paths when capsule-on-disk lookup
  needs the filesystem behind a disk-only boot option
- repeat targeted lookup on the flash-update boot while retaining the S4 and
  pre-ReadyToLock security guards
- preserve capsule-associated BootNext across a one-boot deferred error retry
- keep malformed-only cleanup, fallback ambiguity rejection, allocation retry,
  and CoDGetAll error propagation intact

## Root cause

Byte Cezanne Y1 boots from a disk-only NVMe Boot0001. The early capsule scan
did not connect that boot path, so no `DiskCapsulesBoot` request reached
coreboot. coreboot therefore set `has_capsules=0` and disabled the capsule
update SMI handler. Later FMP raw reads used command `0x85`; without capsule
mode, the raw-read bit reached the default SMMSTORE handler and returned
`SMMSTORE_RET_UNSUPPORTED`, which EDK2 reported as `EFI_UNSUPPORTED`.

The fix connects the active storage path under an explicit default-off feature
PCD and requires a platform image-dispatch policy. It rejects positively
identified network-only paths, retains SAN and storage paths, classifies
InfiniBand from its storage/network resource flags, and retries short-form HD
expansion. File-path-only options are never bound to an arbitrary ESP in
capsule-in-RAM mode.

The update boot performs the same targeted lookup. S4 resume does not change
the handle graph or consume the request. Security and resource errors preserve
OsIndications and BootNext; a one-boot retry marker exits full-flash mode before
retrying. BDS preserves the capsule-associated BootNext during that deferred
OS boot, while still honoring platform cancellation or replacement.

## Validation

- exact base: `13b5f238b5d7acf4e57c4a3bd3cdf5a2156b7369`
- exact head: `10e3bd80fa64a12f9a83db3d4dc27dd787f08a3b`
- exactly three focused commits; PatchCheck passes for all three and in the
  pre-push hook
- focused deferred-BootNext host test: 4/4 pass under ASAN
- pre-push and post-push Codex CLI reviews of the exact full delta: no
  actionable correctness issues
- full capsule-enabled Byte Cezanne Y1 coreboot/EDK2 build: pass
- exact final review ROM SHA256:
  `4a464ab1e5dc2d435991bfdc6c02f7c48df4e348233180095d3df7e08ba1969d`
- exact final review COREBOOT region SHA256:
  `77a4feb99d29e5a947811b2b51c47298580c51d3e59a8fe0dc4e69275879b6a0`

Y1 normal-path hardware proof used ancestor `27622fb3f840`: two matching SPI
backups, a verified COREBOOT-only 26.07 baseline, then the retained signed
26.08 capsule through fwupd and a normal reboot. Final DMI is `26.08`; ESRT
current/last/status is `1703944/1703944/0`; fwupd reports `cod` success; signed
EC/COREBOOT regions match; BootOrder is preserved; capsule state is clean.

The later changes are limited to deferred-error BootNext preservation and
non-Y1 InfiniBand transport classification. They do not change Y1's proven
normal NVMe path, so the invasive hardware cycle was not repeated.

Software artifacts are under `validation-artifacts/final-10e3bd80fa` and the
hardware evidence is under
`validation-artifacts/y1-final-27622fb3f8-hardware` in the retained validation
workspace. Y1 remains reachable and released on signed 26.08.

author: checkupauto
body:
## Summary

Settles the audit's "orphan transformer-inference island" finding (`attention`/`transformer`/`model`/`kv_cache`/`qkv_cache`/`norm`/`quant`, plus `qtransformer`/`amx` which build on them).

An investigation confirmed: **zero consumers** anywhere in the workspace (not even internally, beyond their own tests/examples), ~4k LoC / ~15% of this crate's public API, unconditionally compiled into every one of the ~54 workspace crates that depend on `scirust-core` (which re-exports `scirust-simd`'s public API via `pub use scirust_simd::*`) for no benefit to any of them today. But the code itself is real: well-tested (41 tests), documented, actively maintained — not abandoned work. Real cost + zero current benefit + not dead is exactly what an opt-in feature is for, rather than either deleting working code or leaving the cost unconditional.

### What moved behind `transformer-inference` (off by default)

`attention`, `kv_cache`, `model`, `norm`, `qkv_cache`, `quant`, `transformer`. `activations`, `complex`, `dispatch`, `gemm`, `grad`, and `matrix` stay unconditional — they either have real external consumers (`scirust-learning` uses three `grad::` functions) or, in `complex.rs`'s/`x86_ext.rs`'s case, are unrelated general-purpose code the original audit conflated with the cluster (`x86_ext.rs`'s only mention of `quant` is a doc comment, not an actual dependency — verified before excluding it from the gate).

`grad.rs` needed a scalpel rather than an all-or-nothing gate: only `attention_backward` (and its gradcheck test) depends on `crate::attention`; the other seven backward functions don't, so only `attention_backward` moved behind the feature, keeping `grad.rs`'s real consumer (`scirust-learning`) working unconditionally.

`amx`/`qtransformer`'s existing `nightly-simd` gate gained `transformer-inference` alongside it (both depend on the now-gated modules). Added a `qkv_bench` `[[example]]` entry (previously undeclared, so unconditionally built) with `required-features`, and added `transformer-inference` to `amx_bench`/`qtransformer_bench`'s. `scirust-core` got a passthrough feature mirroring the existing `portable-simd` one.

### CI

The existing `nightly-simd` job and the aarch64 cross-check job both exercised `amx`/`qtransformer`/`quant.rs`'s aarch64 paths *implicitly* (they were unconditional) — both needed `transformer-inference` added to their feature list or that coverage would have silently disappeared without any test failure to flag it. Added a new stable job testing the base `transformer-inference` feature on its own, since the default workspace build/test no longer exercises it at all.

## Test plan

- [x] `RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo +stable check --workspace --all-targets --locked` — whole workspace compiles with default (off) features
- [x] `cargo test -p scirust-simd --locked` (feature off) — 58 tests pass (down from 88, the cluster's tests excluded as expected)
- [x] `cargo test -p scirust-simd --all-targets --features transformer-inference --locked` (stable) — 88 tests pass
- [x] `cargo +nightly-2026-07-02 test -p scirust-simd --all-targets --features "nightly-simd,transformer-inference" --locked` — 95 tests pass, covers `amx`/`qtransformer`
- [x] `cargo clippy` clean in all three configurations (default, `transformer-inference`, `nightly-simd,transformer-inference` on the nightly toolchain matching CI's clippy job)
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` — clean
- [x] `cargo check -p scirust-core --features transformer-inference --locked` — the passthrough feature forwards correctly
- [x] Verified zero external consumers of the gated modules before gating (not just the original audit's claim — re-checked directly), and specifically verified `x86_ext.rs` and `complex.rs` don't actually belong in the gate despite the audit grouping them with the cluster

author: bhanunuthakki
body:
## Problem

The daily FMP budget file (`.tmp/cacher/budget_<date>.json`) counted every HTTP attempt — including 429-rejected retries that never consumed provider quota. On 2026-07-16 the 03:00 `refresh_cache` cron ran into a dead provider quota, logged 252 all-429 attempts into `calls_made`, and when FMP's window reset at ~12:15 PT the same day's real drain fast-exited on "budget exhausted" without pulling a single endpoint. A poisoned ledger costs a full day of freshness on the free tier.

## Fix

Split the counters in `save_fmp_data.py`:
- `_CALL_COUNTER` — raw attempts, unchanged consumers (per-run `--max-calls` caps, printouts)
- `_SERVED_COUNTER` (new) — attempts FMP actually served: any non-429 response **including 4xx** (matches FMP's billing model), plus network errors conservatively (they may have reached FMP; overcounting is safe, undercounting re-breaches the provider cap)

Only served attempts feed `calls_made`; raw attempts land in a new `attempts` key for forensics. `refresh_cache.py`'s reader is untouched (same key).

## Verification

- New `tests/test_fmp_budget_ledger.py`: all-429 → 3 attempts / 0 served; 429→200 → 2/1; served 403 spends; network error spends conservatively
- Full FMP suites green: 33 passed (`test_fmp_budget_ledger`, `test_fmp_tier_ladder`, `test_save_fmp_data_empty_classification`, `test_save_fmp_data_validation_gate`)

### Motivation

- Implement the Exam Simulator v2 Phase 1 blueprint: replace ad-hoc randomization with Fisher–Yates and produce balanced, repeatable exam attempts. 
- Ensure answer letters and multi-select combinations are balanced across an attempt, preserve option order during navigation, provide multiple exam lengths, and surface a comprehensive review summary after submission.

### Description

- Added a reusable exam engine in `js/exam-engine.js` exposing `fisherYates`, `balanceQuestionOptions`, `remapQuestion`, `generateExam`, and `isPbq` to perform Fisher–Yates shuffles, balanced single-letter distribution, balanced multi-select selection, answer/explanation remapping, and exam generation with PBQ placement. 
- Integrated the engine into the app by updating `js/app.js` to use `ExamEngine` for preparing attempts, to add exam lengths (`10`, `25`, `50`, `85`), to keep option order stable for the duration of an attempt, and to hide running score, domain, difficulty, explanations, and correct-answer indicators during an active exam; the `finish()` flow now renders a detailed exam summary with overall, domain, objective, missed, flagged, and correct-answer-letter distribution. 
- Added `tests/exam-engine.test.js` to assert balanced distribution, correct remapping of answers and `why_wrong` entries, stable navigation ordering, and PBQ-first placement for full exams. 
- Wired the engine into the UI by loading `js/exam-engine.js` from `index.html` and updated `service-worker.js` cache assets to include the new engine file.

author: always1ov
body:
## Summary
Two fixes for the positions experience (backend + frontend):

### 1. Trade ledger (new capability)
Positions were snapshot-only — one row per stock per account with cost/quantity and no history, so 建仓/加仓/止盈/清仓 had no first-class representation (only edit/delete).

- New `PositionTrade` table recording open/add/reduce/close with price, quantity, realized pnl, post-trade snapshot, and note
- `POST /positions/{id}/trades`: **add** uses weighted-average cost; **reduce** keeps cost and records realized pnl `(price − cost) × qty`; **close** (or reduce-to-zero) removes the position row while keeping the ledger; optional `sync_funds` adjusts the account's available funds by trade value (default on)
- `GET /positions/trades/list`: per-stock timeline, queryable even after the position is closed
- `create_position` also records an `open` trade so timelines are complete from day one
- Frontend: a 交易 button on each position row opens a dialog with 加仓/减仓/清仓 tabs, live preview of the new weighted cost or realized pnl, a funds-sync toggle, and the stock's own operation timeline; 编辑/删除 stay as manual-correction fallbacks
- New table is auto-created by the existing `Base.metadata.create_all` startup path — no manual migration needed

### 2. Batch report leakage (bug fix)
收盘复盘/盘前分析/新闻速递 analyze the whole watchlist in one AI call but stored the **entire multi-stock report** into every stock's `ai_response` (and the whole batch prompt into `prompt_context`) — opening any stock's suggestion detail showed all other stocks' content. Batch agents now store only the stock's own structured excerpt (new `format_stock_excerpt` / `format_batch_prompt_note` helpers in `suggestion_pool.py`); the full report remains available in the History page. Existing pool entries refresh on the next agent run.

## Test plan
- [x] New `tests/test_position_trades.py` (8 tests): open auto-record, weighted-average cost on add, realized pnl + funds sync on reduce, close deletes position but keeps ledger, reduce-to-zero becomes close, oversell rejected, invalid action/price rejected, sync_funds=false leaves funds untouched
- [x] Full backend suite: 303 passed (only pre-existing sandbox-environment failures: missing `_cffi_backend`/`weasyprint`/`tradingagents` wheels — unrelated to this diff; CI runs the full suite with complete deps before the image build)
- [x] `tsc` + `pnpm build` pass; headless-browser test of the trade dialog with mocked API: reduce 40 @ 900 on a 100-share 858.377-cost position previews 剩余 60 股 / 实现盈亏 +1664.92 (hand-verified), submission appends to the timeline, zero page errors

body:
Plan: plans/PR-Receivables-Ledger.md
Slice phase: Vertical slice
Ownership lane: eom-receivables

Atlas previously stored invoice applications as unrelated payment rows, so one mailed check covering two or three invoices had no authoritative receipt identity, allocation ledger, unapplied balance, or transactional lifecycle. This vertical slice adds that money-safe path while preserving legacy callers. The latest repair closes four exact-head findings at their authoritative boundaries: trusted secret-scan history, standalone MCP readiness, singular idempotency-key size, and oldest-due-first allocation ordering.

## Intentional

- `customer_payments` owns a physical or electronic receipt; invoice applications are explicit allocations and may leave unapplied customer credit.
- Checks start in `received` and follow deposit/clear lifecycle; ACH and Square compatibility receipts start cleared so they never enter the physical-check deposit queue.
- Legacy invoice-payment rows remain readable and are conservatively adopted one-to-one. `invoice_payments.payment_id` remains nullable for one rollout so old data is not hidden.
- New receivables HTTP writes are feature-gated and bearer-authenticated; the retired unauthenticated quick-pay route remains a non-writing 410 tombstone.
- The standalone invoicing MCP applies migrations and proves full receivables readiness before exposing tools.
- No root `.gitleaksignore` is added. The final PR range is one clean commit without the flagged test-code fixture occurrence, while the future trusted-base guard rejects every first or later ignore addition unless a labeled security-only rotation authorizes it.

## Deferred

- Make `invoice_payments.payment_id` non-null only after all finance writers and legacy rows have rolled forward.
- Provider webhooks, bank-file matching, payer-account modeling, and check-image storage remain separate operator-approved slices.
- The EOM backend and portal consumers remain coordinated companion-repository deployments.

## Parked hardening

None. Authentication, idempotency, atomic allocation, lifecycle audit, migration ordering, complete readiness, and secret-ignore governance are required in this money-write slice rather than waived.

## Cold diff reconstruction

Ground truth is the exact-head code, not earlier findings or plan prose.

- Confirmed before repair, now fixed: the initial-ignore exception was PR-controlled because the trusted workflow checks out and executes the base checker (`.github/workflows/gitleaks_baseline_growth_guard.yml:21-40`), while the base checker did not protect `.gitleaksignore`. The published tree contains no root ignore, and `scripts/check_gitleaks_baseline_rotation.py:55-101,221-239` now treats every first or later ignore addition as rotation-gated. `tests/test_check_gitleaks_baseline_rotation.py:119-186` covers unapproved initial/later growth and the labeled security-only path restriction.
- Confirmed before repair, now fixed: standalone MCP startup ran migrations but could serve after a partially applied schema. `atlas_brain/mcp/invoicing_server.py:72-114` now requires `ReceivablesService.is_ready()` before yielding and always closes the pool. `tests/test_receivables.py:495-599` proves success order, migration abort, and incomplete-schema abort.
- Confirmed before repair, now fixed: singular `record_payment` accepted an unbounded key before inserting into a 128-character column. `atlas_brain/mcp/invoicing_server.py:598-616,668-699` publishes the 1-to-128 schema and rejects an invalid helper call before repository access; `atlas_brain/services/receivables.py:540-558` repeats the invariant at the authoritative write boundary. `tests/test_receivables.py:229-246,1690-1717,2004-2023` covers service, repository-access, and real FastMCP schema boundaries.
- Confirmed before repair, now fixed: the greedy allocation loop consumed a customer-name-first invoice feed. `atlas_brain/services/receivables.py:429-486` orders by due date, issue date, customer name, and invoice number before suggesting allocations. `tests/test_receivables.py:249-269,1753-1794` proves the query contract and real PostgreSQL behavior for one contact whose newer invoice alphabetically sorts first.
- Confirmed before repair, still fixed: readiness validates every migration-added column and all 16 explicit or constraint-backed indexes; the API maps only concrete live database-unavailability states to 503; singular retries do not repeat CRM history; inactive receipts expose no available credit; and only physical checks enter the deposit queue.
- Contradicted during earlier cold review and corrected before publication: claims that a PR-owned initial ignore was trusted, that migrations alone proved standalone MCP readiness, and that the prior customer-name-first query implemented oldest-due-first suggestions were overstated. No waiver remains.
- Could not determine from code: production token provisioning, maintenance-window execution, deployed process versions, and companion-repository rollout state. Those remain release-time operational prerequisites and are not claimed here.

## Verification

- Ephemeral PostgreSQL 16: `python -m pytest tests/test_receivables.py tests/test_invoice_repository.py -q` with `ATLAS_RECEIVABLES_TEST_DATABASE_URL` — 62 passed, including oldest-due-first allocation across differing customer-name snapshots, removal of every required index, and live backend termination during a transaction.
- Focused receivables/repository/Gitleaks-rotation suite — 72 passed, 6 expected PostgreSQL-environment skips.
- Python compile and `git diff --check` — passed.
- Plan synchronization — passed.
- Invoicing MCP/OAuth surface — 43 passed; monthly invoice approval blockers — 2 passed, 41 deselected.
- Gitleaks clean PR range — 1 commit, 221,096 bytes, no leaks.
- Maturity ratchets and repository pre-push review are rerun or revalidated by the publication wrapper and GitHub checks.

## Diff size

- 18 files changed; 5,438 insertions and 203 deletions (5,641 total changed lines).
- Diff-budget override: The ledger schema, atomic receipt/allocation service, authenticated HTTP and MCP entrypoints, compatibility bridge, readiness contract, secret-ignore governance, and real PostgreSQL regression proofs must ship together so no deployment can expose a partial money-write path.
- The plan's explicit 18-file override covers the money-write boundaries and their regression proofs. No maturity or secret baseline is enlarged.

## AI reconciliation

- Initial `.gitleaksignore` trust finding: fixed by removing the ignore and republishing one clean commit; future ignore growth is rotation-gated.
- Standalone MCP schema-readiness finding: fixed with readiness-gated lifespan and failure cleanup proof.
- Singular MCP idempotency-key bound finding: fixed at registered transport, helper pre-repository, and service boundaries.
- Oldest-due-first suggestion finding: fixed in the authoritative query and proven against real PostgreSQL.
- All earlier recorded automated-review findings remain fixed; none are waived.

author: jaimeferreira2002
body:
A large batch — the app becomes **meetro**, gains Portuguese, adopts the real brand assets, and the iOS project is finally sane.

## Brand
- **Name swept everywhere**: `appName`, the in-app Privacy/Terms text (interpolated), the hosted docs, MaterialApp title, and the iOS display name. It was still calling itself the placeholder "Lisbon Metro Live" *inside its own legal documents*.
- **meetro logo splash** — fade in / hold / fade out (2s, replacing the 3.4s train animation). The logo carries the four-line motif itself, so the separate stripe and caption went.
- **Palette repointed to the official pictogram colours** (`#F7A800 / #2F7DE1 / #00A19B / #EA1D76`). Our values were approximations that disagreed with both the line SVGs *and* the meetro logo's own stripe. Map, pictograms and brand now match.
- **Bundle id → `com.jaimeferreira.meetro`** (was `pt.metrolisboa.metroLisboaAr` — the reverse-DNS of Metro Lisboa's domain, which contradicted our own "not affiliated" Terms). Tile User-Agent fixed for the same reason.
- Real `logo_metro.png` + official line pictograms (adds `flutter_svg`; the marks ship as SVG). Pictograms used where they have room; dense rows keep colour dots since the marks need ~16px+.

## Portuguese
- `strings.dart` — `tr(en, pt)` with a Language selector in Settings, persisted, defaulting to the device locale. Deliberately lightweight rather than gen-l10n (EN/PT only, no plurals/dates); every call site funnels through one function if we outgrow it.

## UI
- HUD stripe removed; Nearby icon is now a compass (the old arrow duplicated the my-location button).
- **Collapsible panels removed** — tapping the active tab now deselects to the map. Same outcome, ~80 fewer lines.

## iOS project (the painful part)
- **`ios/` is now tracked.** It wasn't, so the Xcode project persisted across branches while the widget's files didn't — every branch but one was unbuildable.
- Fixed **"Multiple commands produce appex/Info.plist"**: Xcode 16 made `MetroWidget/` a *file-system synchronized group*, so the folder's `Info.plist` was copied as a resource *and* processed via `INFOPLIST_FILE`. Moved it out of the synced folder.
- `flutter_launcher_icons` configured (the icon was still Flutter's blue F — it's a native asset catalog, unrelated to Flutter's asset bundle).

## Known / deliberate
- Legal texts stay English pending review.
- App icon is the wordmark; it needs a square mark to read at 60pt.
- Metro Lisboa's logo/pictograms are still shown — narrowed, not resolved, in `docs/APP_STORE.md`.

## What changed

For Square offline payments, use `offline_payment_details.client_created_at` as the effective transaction timestamp when present. Keep the original upload/server timestamp in the stored raw payload and fall back to `created_at` when client time is absent or blank.

## Why

Offline POS payments can reach Square hours after the register took them. Using the later server `created_at` pointed the thumbnail and Protect timeline link at the upload time instead of the customer transaction.

## Impact

New offline sales display and request footage at the device-recorded checkout time. Malformed nonempty timestamps are rejected by the existing malformed-payment path instead of producing a wrong link.

## Validation

- Added client-time normalization and raw timestamp retention coverage
- Added blank/missing fallback cases
- Added malformed timestamp handling
- Added sync/store/snapshot timestamp regression
- `pytest -q` — 98 passed

## Note

Existing offline rows retain their old timestamp until versioned upserts are merged and Square reconciles those payments again.

author: ihb2032
body:
`Pipeline.fingerprint` was computed once in `__post_init__` and covered configuration names only. Two in-process runtime changes could then make caches silently serve wrong output:

- **Runtime re-registration**: registries allow replacing an implementation under a live name, and the frontend re-resolves names per run — after a swap, behaviour changed while `fingerprint` / `source_hash` stayed put. `Registry` now carries a monotonic `generation` counter, and the fingerprint folds a snapshot of every compilation-relevant registry's generation, so a swap advances the fingerprint, flips `source_hash`, and invalidates `frontend_fingerprint` stamps on populated IR. Steady state is a few atomic int reads; lazy adapter loading is preserved.
- **Asset-resolver identity**: an `image` fence inlines resolver-returned bytes into the parsed tree, but neither the tree-cache key nor the fingerprint knew the resolver — two documents referencing the same `media/image1.png` name through different resolvers could share one document's pixels over a shared `tree_subcache`. Tree-cache keys are now `(domain, source, surface, salt)` 4-tuples (salt = resolver identity for graphics, `""` for math/music), and the fingerprint folds the same identity (three tiers: none / declared `cache_identity` / per-instance weakref-retired token).

Also fixes a wiring defect this exposed: assigning `asset_resolver` to an already-built Pipeline never took effect (the frontend driver kept its constructor-time `None` snapshot), so in-document images silently soft-failed to blank rasters. `CompilationSession.begin` now syncs the driver snapshots at run start.

body:
<!--Read comments, before committing pull request read checklist again

# Checklist:

- I have performed a self-review of my own code,
- I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas,
- I have made corresponding changes to the documentation,
- I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works,
- New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes ("bundle exec rake"),
- Title include "WIP" if work is in progress.
- I acknowledge that I will *not* force push my branch once reviews have started.

-->

Resolves #5632

### Description
Clicking "New Quantity Request" opens a Bootstrap modal, but the button itself gets stuck showing "Please wait..." after the modal is dismissed.

The cause is `rails-ujs`. Its `data-disable-with` behavior disables a link on click and only re-enables it once the next page load or AJAX request completes. A modal-toggle button never does either of those: it just opens a modal client-side. So the button disables on click and never gets re-enabled.

`modal_button_to` builds on the shared `_link_to` helper, which sets `data-disable-with: "Please wait..."` as a default for every button unless the caller opts out. That default makes sense for buttons that navigate or submit a form, but a modal toggle never does either, so the fix is to opt `modal_button_to` out of it entirely rather than trying to reset the state after the fact with more JavaScript.

I considered listening for the modal's `hidden.bs.modal` event and manually resetting the button's text and disabled state instead. That would work, but it's more code for a problem that doesn't need it: `disable_with` isn't relevant to a button that never navigates, so it's cleaner to just not apply it in the first place.

### Type of change
* Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

* New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
* Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)

* Documentation update

### How Has This Been Tested?
Added helper specs for `modal_button_to` covering the default case and the case where the caller passes their own `data` options, confirming `data-disable-with` is omitted in both.

Added a system spec that opens the new request modal, dismisses it, and confirms the trigger button still reads "New Quantity Request" instead of "Please wait...".

author: oblinger
body:
## What changed

Adds **M28.4**, a single seed-deterministic `transport_complexity` dial on the generator entry point — a sibling of the M28.1 network-size dial (`9997782`). Where M28.1 scales world *size*, M28.4 scales world *structure*: the number of compartments and their branching.

- **Seam:** `src/alienbio/build/pipeline.py` — `instantiate(..., transport_complexity=...)` resolves the dial (new `TRANSPORT_LEVELS` + `_resolve_transport_complexity`) and threads a numeric factor into `_process_containers`, which scales `parameters.containers.regions.count` (compartment count) and `populations.per_species_per_region` (per-compartment branching) via the existing shared `_scale_count` helper. Also reachable through `Bio.build(..., transport_complexity=...)` in `spec_lang/bio.py`. `TRANSPORT_LEVELS` exported from `alienbio.build`.
- **No new RNG:** reuses the existing seeded region/population generation; the region and organism loops append by index, so lower factors truncate and higher factors extend the same deterministic sequence.

## Guarantees (all tested)

- **Default = byte-identical:** `transport_complexity` unset / `1.0` / `"simple"` reproduces today's world exactly (`_scale_count(x, 1.0) == x`). Verified against full `_ground_truth_`, `regions`, `molecules`, `reactions`.
- **Monotone:** higher dial → `>=` compartments and `>=` populations, checked across 6 seeds.
- **Seed-deterministic:** same `(value, seed)` → identical topology.
- **Raises on bad input:** unknown named level or negative number raises `ValueError` (no silent clamp/fallback).
- **Domain-neutral:** levels `sparse`/`simple`/`branched`/`dense`; opaque container/region vocabulary only.

## Named levels

| Level | Multiplier |
| --- | --- |
| `sparse` | 0.5 |
| `simple` | 1.0 (identity) |
| `branched` | 2.0 |
| `dense` | 4.0 |

## Tests

New `tests/integration/test_transport_dial.py` (15 tests: determinism, default byte-identity, monotonicity, named levels, spec-level default, validation, Bio.build path). Doc section added to `docs/Guide/Generator Spec.md`.

- `uv run pytest tests/` → **1880 passed, 32 skipped** (baseline 1865+15 new; JAX not installed → skips).
- `uv run pyright src/` → **147 errors**, unchanged from baseline; zero new errors in touched files.

author: jason-easyazz
body:
## ⚠️ Merge order: this must land AFTER #1401

`down_revision = "0021"`, and **0021 only exists in #1401** (panel-config). If this merges first, alembic boots looking for a revision that isn't there. **Auto-merge deliberately NOT armed** until #1401 lands.

## The bug (mine)

`_DEFAULT_DISPLAY_PREFS` has advertised `sleep_enabled` + `sleep_seconds` since the dimmed-sleep work, and `home.html` reads both at boot to size its idle-sleep window. But:

1. `display_preferences` **has no such columns** — live schema is `device_id, enabled, day_brightness, night_enabled, night_start, night_end, night_brightness, idle_enabled, idle_seconds, idle_brightness, off_enabled, off_seconds, pi_host, updated_at`
2. the PUT's INSERT **enumerates columns explicitly** and omitted both → every write silently dropped them
3. the table has **zero rows** in production

**Net effect: the operator's sleep choice could never be saved.** The panel always used the hardcoded 180s.

It hid because a **GET looks correct** — `_row_to_prefs` falls back to the defaults, which is exactly what the caller expects to see. I added the defaults and the panel read, and gave them nowhere to live. `off_enabled`/`off_seconds` have columns and work; this brings sleep to parity.

## The fix

**`0022_display_prefs_sleep.py`** — `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS sleep_enabled/sleep_seconds`, dialect-aware per 0018/0020, with a `PRAGMA table_info` probe on the SQLite branch (which has no `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, so a rerun would error). Nullable, no server default **on purpose**: NULL means "never set", which `_row_to_prefs` already skips, so existing rows behave exactly as they do today.

**The PUT** — both added to the column list, `VALUES`, the params tuple **and the `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` set-list**. That last one matters: the INSERT is an upsert, so a column that's inserted but missing from the set-list persists the *first* write and silently ignores every later edit — a nastier version of the same bug. Column/placeholder counts verified aligned (16/16); a mismatch writes values into the wrong columns silently.

## The test asserts the invariant, not the columns

An enumerated column list cannot be kept in sync with a defaults dict by hand — that's *how this shipped*. So rather than checking two names:

> **everything in `_DEFAULT_DISPLAY_PREFS` must be written by the PUT**

which fails the day someone adds the next pref without a column. Plus a second guard that anything inserted is also in the `ON CONFLICT` set-list.

Mutation-verified: restoring the pre-fix INSERT makes `test_every_advertised_pref_is_persisted_by_the_put` fail. Marker-based (`ci_safe`), no `validate.yml` edit.

## Live round-trip: pending deploy

Deliberately not claimed as done. The columns only exist once the migration runs, and zoe-data only writes them after a restart — **merge ≠ deploy**. I'll verify the real round-trip (PUT → GET → row actually persists) as part of the authorized restart, and report the result.

author: pentiminax
body:
## Summary

Fixes #242. `ArrayDataProvider::fetchData()` mapped every row twice whenever a global search was active — once inside the `array_filter` predicate (for **every** element, including out-of-page rows) and again in the output generator for the paginated slice. Row mapping (Twig column rendering + action resolution) is expensive.

## Changes
- **Search active:** each element is mapped exactly once, filtered on the mapped row, and the surviving mapped rows are sliced and yielded as-is — no remapping. `recordsFiltered` = number of matches.
- **No search:** the items are sliced first, then only the paginated slice is mapped, so out-of-page rows are never mapped. `recordsFiltered` = `recordsTotal`.
- Logic split into small, single-responsibility private helpers (`filterBySearch`, `rowMatches`, `slice`, `mapRows`, `yieldRows`, `normalize`).

## Behavior preserved
`recordsTotal` = total element count, `data` remains a generator, `length <= 0` means "no limit", object and array items both supported.

## Tests
Added a spy `RowMapper` counting `map()` invocations, asserting: (1) no-search + pagination maps once per returned row and never for out-of-page rows; (2) search active maps once per element with correct results. Verified the new test fails against the old double-mapping implementation.

`vendor/bin/phpunit` → **OK (838 tests)**.

With **no search** (including the default empty `Search('', false)` from unfiltered loads), it **paginates first** and maps only the current page. With an **active search**, each item is mapped **once**, filtered on that mapped row, then the matches are sliced—eliminating the old pattern of mapping every row for filtering and again for output.

body:
Prep for making the repo public. Removes the two places the author's macOS
username (`jonathang`) was baked into tracked files.

## Findings from the pre-public review

Scanned every tracked file and the full commit history (diff content of all 14
commits, plus every historical blob). **No security issues found:**

| Checked | Result |
|---|---|
| API keys / secrets (any blob, any commit) | ✅ none — `config.toml` was never committed |
| Transcript data (`data/`, `index.db`) | ✅ never committed |
| Other people's names (from the live index) | ✅ none in tracked files |
| Transcript content (meetings, interviews) | ✅ none in tracked files |
| Author's macOS username | ⚠️ 3 occurrences → **this PR** |

## Changes

**`config.example.toml`** — `/Users/jonathang/Documents/Obsidian Vault` → `~/Documents/Obsidian Vault`.
`config.py:119` already calls `.expanduser()`, so this resolves identically. Verified
end-to-end: the real `load_config()` parses the example file and yields the same path.

**`scripts/install_launchd.sh`** — labels become `com.transcript-analyzer.{sync,dashboard}`.
Previously anyone installing this got launchd agents named after *someone else's* account.

## The non-obvious part

Renaming the label orphans agents from an existing install — they stay loaded under the
old name, and `uninstall` (which used the new labels) would never find them. On the
author's machine both were live:

```
com.jonathang.transcript-sync
com.jonathang.transcript-dashboard   (running, PID 86830)
```

So both `install` and `uninstall` now tear down the legacy labels first. Those are derived
from `$USER` rather than hardcoded — which reproduces the old name on an affected machine
(`com.jonathang.*`) while matching nothing on a fresh one (unload is a silent no-op), and
keeps the username out of the repo. Hardcoding the legacy names would have reintroduced
exactly what this PR removes.

## Verification

- `bash -n scripts/install_launchd.sh` — parses clean
- `git grep -E "/Users/|jonathang|jagong"` — zero occurrences
- TOML parses; `~` expands to the correct path via the real loader
- Legacy labels resolve to exactly the two currently-loaded agents

## Not addressed here

The username remains in **git history** (this PR only changes HEAD). Removing it entirely
needs a history rewrite + force-push, which changes all SHAs — not done unilaterally.
Given the account is `jagong-cmu` and commits already carry `jagong@andrew.cmu.edu`, the
username adds no exposure beyond what's already public.

author: mingruizhang
body:
## What

Hardens the XHS search flow for consecutive searches — the common case where the model emits several `search` tool calls in one LLM step (validated on Axiom: up to 8 per step across many users), or searches back-to-back across steps on the same tab.

- **`search_notes`**: navigate back to `/explore` before submitting whenever the tab is parked anywhere else on XHS, so every search starts from a fresh document instead of the previous query's leftover SPA state.
- **`search_transition_ok`**: fail on a URL-keyword mismatch even when the input box already matches the query (previously the URL check was skipped in that case), and require the exact `/search_result` path for `page_state` (previously `includes('/search_result')` also matched `/search_result_ai` and `/search_result/<id>` detail routes).
- **`submit_search`**: new last-resort `navigate_search_url` strategy — when the typed submit derails, load the classic results route directly (`search_result?keyword=…`). Attempts hijacked onto the AI route exit the transition poll early and skip the now-stale submit-button click.
- `percent-encoding` added as a direct dependency (already in the tree via reqwest) for the keyword encoding.

## Why

Prod traces show two failure modes for consecutive searches on the shared tab:

1. **Stale-transition race**: for the 2nd+ search, the box shows the new query (we just typed it) and the old grid still satisfies `card_count > 0`, so the transition wait could pass on the previous query's page and silently return its cards as the new query's results.
2. **SPA-debris grind**: search sessions that never leave the SPA degrade into multi-minute searches and dead tabs. Reference timeline in trace `dd321c39c5c74555259d665740803f0c`: a 5-search step ground 5m47s + 7m7s ending in `Current page is not Xiaohongshu: about:blank`, then recovered to 35s searches the moment a fresh navigation happened; later the browser wedged permanently (`Input.dispatchMouseEvent` / `Runtime.evaluate` CDP timeouts for the rest of the conversation).

While verifying live, a third issue surfaced: since ~2026-07 XHS can hijack home-box submits onto the new **`/search_result_ai`** route (with a double-encoded keyword). The old page-state check accepted that page's cards as regular search results. This is already visible in 4 prod traces from the last 14 days, so the fallback is load-bearing today, not speculative.

## Verification

- Live end-to-end on managed Chrome (CLI daemon built from this branch): two back-to-back searches (`上海 咖啡店` → `露营 装备`) both landed on the classic results route with correct, non-bleeding cards. On this machine the typed submit is AI-hijacked, so both healed via the new `navigate_search_url` strategy — without this fix every search here would return AI-page results or fail.
- `cargo check --workspace` clean; all 91 existing socai-core tests pass (no new tests per repo rules).

## Notes for review

- The `submit.strategy` field in run artifacts now reports `navigate_search_url` when the fallback fires — useful for gauging how often the typed path derails in the field.
- Douyin has the same weak transition check (no keyword validation at all); being handled separately.
- The `sort=最多点赞` per-note grind is the known stale-note-cascade issue and is out of scope here.

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>pnpm/pnpm (pnpm)</summary>

### [`v11.11.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/HEAD/pnpm11/pnpm/CHANGELOG.md#11110)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.10.0...v11.11.0)

##### Minor Changes

- [`508b8c2`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/commit/508b8c2): Added the `pnpm access` command for managing package access and visibility on the registry, supporting listing packages and collaborators, getting and setting package status and MFA requirements, and granting or revoking team access.

##### Patch Changes

- [`c70e33e`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/commit/c70e33e): Allow `allowBuilds` entries for git-hosted packages to match by repository URL without pinning the resolved commit hash. This lets trusted git repositories keep running their build scripts after branch updates without approving each new commit, while package-name-only rules still do not approve git-hosted artifacts.
- [`3067e4f`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/commit/3067e4f): Reduced peak memory usage during cold-cache dependency resolution. The metadata fetch is memoized for the whole resolution phase, and it was retaining each package's raw registry response body (used only to mirror the response to disk) for that entire time. The memoized cache now holds a body-less copy, so the raw body only lives as long as the call that writes the disk mirror. On large graphs that fetch full metadata (e.g. with `minimumReleaseAge` or `trustPolicy` enabled) this cuts peak RSS by roughly 30%, back in line with pnpm 10. The resolved lockfile is unchanged.
- [`51300fd`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/commit/51300fd): Prevent a crafted `pnpm-lock.yaml` from writing package content outside the virtual store. A dependency path key whose name reconstructs to a path-traversal sequence (e.g. `../../../tmp/x@1.0.0`) is now rejected by the isolated (virtual-store) linker and the Plug'n'Play resolver map, matching the containment already applied to the hoisted linker. Under the global virtual store, a traversal in the version-derived path segment (e.g. a snapshot `version: "../../x"`) is now rejected at `formatGlobalVirtualStorePath`, the single point every global-virtual-store slot path funnels through — closing the same escape in the isolated linker, the resolver's dependency-graph builder, and the config-dependency installer.
- [`f8058eb`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/commit/f8058eb): Reject symlinked `pnpm-lock.yaml` files when reading or writing the env lockfile document.
- [`9318a11`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/commit/9318a11): Allow `registries` and `namedRegistries` to be configured in the global `config.yaml` file.
- [`51300fd`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/commit/51300fd): Fixed a path traversal vulnerability where a dependency whose manifest `name` was a scoped path traversal (e.g. `@x/../../../<path>`) could be written outside `node_modules` to an attacker-controlled location during `pnpm install`, even with `--ignore-scripts`. The isolated linker now validates the package name before using it as a directory name, matching the existing protection in the hoisted linker.
- [`14332f0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/commit/14332f0): Fail instead of silently removing an optional dependency's locked entries from `pnpm-lock.yaml` when the registry cannot resolve it. Previously, when registry metadata lacked a version that the lockfile already pinned (for example, a mirror that had not synced a recent release yet), `pnpm install` and `pnpm dedupe` silently dropped the optional dependency's entries — emptying maps such as the platform binaries of `@napi-rs/canvas` — so the lockfile differed between machines and frozen installs on other hosts had nothing to link [#​12853](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/12853).
- [`fecfe83`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/commit/fecfe83): Fixed peer dependency resolution with `autoInstallPeers` when a workspace package depends on a version of a package that a transitive dependency's self-contained closure also provides for itself. The peer providers that are attached to the root project for reuse are no longer peer-resolved a second time in the root context, so packages inside such a closure no longer get their peers bound to the root project's incompatible version [#​4993](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/4993).
- [`5a4daec`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/commit/5a4daec): `${...}` environment-variable placeholders in the `httpProxy`, `httpsProxy`, `noProxy`, `proxy`, and `noproxy` settings are no longer expanded when these settings come from a project's `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. They now receive the same protection already applied to `registry`, `namedRegistries`, and `pnprServer`.
- [`d1da02e`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/commit/d1da02e): `pnpm publish` no longer prints credentials when the target registry is configured with inline `user:pass@` credentials (e.g. `registry=https://user:pass@example.com/`). They are now redacted both from the "publishing to registry" line and from the OIDC (trusted publishing) failure messages.
- [`dcfc611`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/commit/dcfc611): `pnpm self-update` now honors `trustPolicy=no-downgrade`. It resolves the target pnpm version against full registry metadata, so it refuses to switch to a version whose supply-chain trust evidence is weaker than an earlier-published one, the same way a regular install does.
- [`a8ad82d`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/commit/a8ad82d): Register the `pn` alias in generated shell completion scripts.
- [`25bd5c3`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/commit/25bd5c3): Fixed standalone installer downgrades from pnpm v12 to v11.
- [`23996e9`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/commit/23996e9): `pnpm runtime set <name> <version>` now validates its arguments: the name must be `node`, `deno`, or `bun`, and the version must not contain a comma. Previously these were interpolated straight into a `pnpm add` selector, where an unsupported name or a comma (e.g. `node 22,is-positive`) could be misread as a list of packages or a local directory and install unintended packages or bins.

author: majiayu000
body:
## What / Why

The intake layer was source-pluggable but destination-hardwired: uncovered issues always entered the built-in `github_issue_pr` workflow. This PR adds optional declarative intake bindings so normalized incoming issues can route directly to project workflow definitions.

Closes #1656. The governing spec landed in #1657.

## Behavior

- Adds an optional `definition.intake` policy with source, required labels, excluded labels, and `max_active_instances`.
- Validates bindings fail-closed against sources that were actually registered for declarative polling.
- Routes matching issues exclusively to the selected declarative definition; unmatched issues retain the existing path.
- Uses deterministic definition tie-breaking, store-backed live dedupe, active-instance caps, and audited routing outcomes.
- Keeps source matching normalized and source-agnostic.

## Review fixes

The follow-up commit `303d6228` addresses every unresolved review thread:

- validates against actual poll-tick sources, excluding webhook-only GitHub and Feishu paths that do not invoke declarative routing;
- persists `author_trust_class` so non-collaborator isolation cannot default to Trusted;
- separates raw `external_id` from a repository-namespaced workflow `subject_key`, preventing collisions for equal issue numbers across repositories while preserving source callbacks;
- persists the repository identity and maps terminal declarative instances into the intake completion callback, restoring cancellation and transient-failure retry behavior.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo check -p harness-server --all-targets`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- 9 intake binding tests
- 3 declarative identity tests
- trust persistence regression test
- declarative completion callback regression test
- repository pre-push DB-less matrix passed, including 482 `harness-workflow` tests
- 6 PostgreSQL lease tests and the DB-backed `harness-server` suite were deferred to configured CI because `HARNESS_DATABASE_URL` is not set locally

## Risk and rollback

Risk is concentrated in startup binding validation, declarative submission identity/data, and terminal intake callbacks. Regression tests cover each review finding. Squash-revert this PR to restore the previous built-in-only intake path.

author: ibanner56
body:
## A11c — Publish the update manifest to GitHub Pages

Makes the Stage-1 update client's fixed URLs live by publishing each channel's manifest to GitHub Pages on every tagged release:

```
https://ibanner56.github.io/CallersCompendium/stable.json
https://ibanner56.github.io/CallersCompendium/beta.json
```

These are read by `kUpdateManifestBaseUrl` in `app/lib/src/update/update_config.dart` and 404 gracefully today (silent no-op by design).

### Mechanism: persistent `gh-pages` branch (not `actions/deploy-pages`)
`deploy-pages` replaces the **whole site** each deploy, so a stable release would clobber `beta.json` (and vice-versa). Instead, `tools/release/publish_pages_manifest.sh` starts from the existing `gh-pages` content and overwrites **only** the current channel's file, so **the other channel is preserved by construction**. A fetch-and-retry loop handles a concurrent stable+beta push. No new third-party action is introduced (reuses the already-SHA-pinned `checkout`/`upload-artifact`/`download-artifact`), so there is nothing new to SHA-pin.

Path math: for a project Pages site, the `gh-pages` root maps 1:1 to the base URL (root `stable.json` → `…/CallersCompendium/stable.json`).

### Wiring (surgical)
- `publish` job: uploads `dist/<channel>.json` as the `channel-manifest` artifact (one new step; draft-release/SBOM/attestation/build-matrix behavior otherwise untouched).
- New `pages` job: `needs: [meta, publish]`, **identical** canonical-repo + `push` + tag guard as `publish`, `permissions: contents: write` **only** (no `id-token`/`attestations`). Downloads the artifact and runs the script. Forks/PRs/manual dispatch can never publish.

### Cross-channel preservation — proven offline
`tools/release/test_publish_pages_manifest.py` drives the real script against local bare git repos (no network) and asserts: first publish creates `gh-pages` with only `stable.json` (+ `.nojekyll`, no source tree); a later `beta.json` publish keeps `stable.json`; a later `stable.json` publish keeps `beta.json`; `.nojekyll` survives republishes; unchanged content is a no-op; bad args fail loudly.

### One-time maintainer step (documented)
`docs/dev/releasing.md` gains a new section covering the mechanism, path math, preservation guarantee, and the one-time **Settings → Pages → Deploy from a branch → `gh-pages` → `/ (root)`** step. Shipping this before Pages is enabled is safe (client 404s gracefully). Light notes added to ADR-002 §1 and ROADMAP 7.1.

### Validation
- `actionlint .github/workflows/release.yml` — clean
- `shellcheck tools/release/publish_pages_manifest.sh` — clean
- `python3 tools/release/test_publish_pages_manifest.py` + existing `test_gen_release_metadata.py` / `_notes` / `_sbom` — all pass

No real tags pushed; no public release created.

author: jcasimir
body:
## What

A writing team for the CE plugin: **Perkins** (a phased orchestrator) and a **seven-voice reviewer panel** that draft and review prose so it sounds, reads, and looks like Jeff wrote it — and get *better* at it over time.

## Perkins — five gated phases

`develop → outline → draft → seven-voice review + iterate → compound`

Mirrors Erin's phased march, but for writing. Composes `ce:write` and `ce:prose-review` (companion PR: [compound-engineering-plugin#10](https://github.com/JumpstartLab/compound-engineering-plugin/pull/10)) plus `ce:compound`. The compound phase's **enforcement artifact is a voice-guide rule** — every correction Jeff makes teaches the guide, so the next draft starts closer to his voice. `/ce:run perkins "<what to write>"`.

## The panel

| Reviewer | Lens |
|---|---|
| Stephen King | Voice & tone — does it sound like Jeff? |
| Gary Provost | Rhythm & cadence — the read-aloud test |
| George Orwell | Concision & AI-slop — cut filler, kill machine tells |
| Barbara Minto | Structure & flow — answer-first (docs) / narrative arc (prose) |
| Jakob Nielsen | Formatting — scannability, the "looks" |
| Ann Handley | Audience — will it land with the reader? |
| Bryan Garner | Vocabulary — the right term of art |

Tagged `category: writing` so `ce:prose-review` selects exactly this set. Each owns specific voice-guide sections with explicit deferral lanes.

## Voice guide (re-grounded — see commit history)

`voice/voice-guide.md` is the **living** record of how Jeff writes. The first cut was accidentally derived partly from a machine-generated doc; it has been **re-grounded on provenance-verified writing**:

- `Career/lint-rules.md` — Jeff's own codified rules (formal register)
- three cover letters that pass that lint (Anthropic, OW COO, Posit)
- the two "With Intention" Medium essays — pure, pre-AI Jeff (expressive register)

**Two-register model:** *formal* (cover letters, client docs — restrained, no exclamation/profanity, lint-rules governs) vs *expressive* (blog/opinion — raw, funny, profane, direct address, italics-for-voice). The reviewers are register-aware so an expressive piece isn't flattened into a memo.

Live copy read/written at `~/.config/compound-engineering/voice-guide.md`; project override at `docs/writing/voice-guide.md`. The private source corpus is **not** committed.

## Try it

1. Merge this + the plugin PR.
2. Seed the guide: `cp voice/voice-guide.md ~/.config/compound-engineering/voice-guide.md` (already done on tractor).
3. `/ce:refresh`, then `/ce:run perkins "draft the X"`.

## Known gaps (v1)

- **Email voice is under-sampled** — flagged in §6 for the compound loop to fill.
- Further pre-AI grounding available in the `Turing Archive/Projects-writing/` curriculum if we want to deepen the teaching register.

author: m4n5ter
body:
English ## Summary Part of #853. Introduces the M1 foundation for one Runtime Host per canonical interactive root: - `@maka/storage/root-authority` resolves a root, establishes its durable identity, and mints the only capabilities that can acquire or observe Host ownership. - `@maka/runtime-host` adds the transport-independent bootstrap protocol, local client, single-owner Host kernel, and connect-or-spawn election path. - Real-process and static dependency gates cover the ownership, lifecycle, protocol, and package-boundary contracts. This is deliberately a non-serving kernel: it does not open Runtime Stores, compose `@maka/runtime`, recover Sessions, start schedulers, expose domain operations, migrate any surface, or switch the production owner. Those remain later slices of #853. ## Design decisions - **One authority per root.** A random root id is durably bound to the initialized filesystem identity. Path aliases and root moves converge on the same control namespace; a copied initialized root fails closed instead of creating a second owner. - **The OS lock is the authority.** Registration, PID, endpoint, and health data are discovery evidence only. There is no stale-lock stealing or PID-based ownership recovery. - **Ownership is capability-scoped.** Root authority alone mints branded owner and observer handles; the Host authenticates the complete owner aggregate before using it. - **The Host outlives its launcher and clients.** Candidate launch is detached, client disconnect only drops that connection, and idle exit is committed by the Host's residency gate. - **Incompatible Host replacement is residency-aware.** Protocol compatibility is determined by the protocol range and required feature contract. Residency is any accepted connection or work that requires the Host to stay alive; this non-serving M1 kernel currently counts accepted connections and active bootstrap/status operations. An incompatible Host with residency blocks replacement, while a truly idle incompatible Host exits through the normal idle lifecycle so the same bounded election can launch a compatible Host without overlapping owners. - **Election has one deadline.** Registration reads, connect, handshake, candidate launch, and retry backoff consume one monotonic budget; a timed-out client cannot start a late detached Candidate. - **The bootstrap surface stays small.** V1 uses a bounded 64 KiB newline-delimited JSON protocol for hello, handshake, and status only. Export-aware TypeScript AST gates use explicit external-import allowlists and fail closed on dynamic loader capabilities, preventing protocol/client code from reaching server internals, Runtime composition, or Store factories. - **Local transport is private by construction on POSIX.** Each Host epoch uses a randomized UDS inside a current-user directory. Windows named-pipe support is best effort in M1; its stronger ACL and packaging guarantees remain explicit follow-up work rather than inferred from POSIX behavior. ## Verification - Root `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test -- --serial`, `npm run build`, and `npm run check:stale` pass. - `@maka/storage`: 314 passing, 1 existing Windows-only skip. - `@maka/runtime-host`: 29 passing. - Real Node and Electron processes cover concurrent cold start in both directions, normal/crash/force-kill release, launcher exit with Host survival, stale discovery artifacts, compatibility replacement, bounded election, private endpoint permissions, malformed and oversized frame isolation, root identity drift, and shutdown under transport backpressure. - TypeScript AST dependency gates enforce both the M1 package boundary and the root-authority leaf boundary. ## Review focus - Whether root identity and the native lock establish one unambiguous ownership authority. - Whether Host residency, draining, shutdown, and incompatible replacement can ever overlap owners or strand the lock. - Whether connect-or-spawn preserves one total deadline without post-timeout side effects. - Whether the package graph keeps M1 independent of Runtime/Store composition and leaves a clean boundary for the next slice.
简体中文 ## 概要 属于 #853 的一部分。 本 PR 引入“每个 canonical interactive root 只有一个 Runtime Host”的 M1 基础： - `@maka/storage/root-authority` 负责解析 root、建立持久 identity，并签发唯一可取得或观察 Host ownership 的 capability。 - `@maka/runtime-host` 提供与 transport 无关的 bootstrap 协议、本地 Client、single-owner Host kernel，以及 connect-or-spawn 选主路径。 - 真实进程测试和静态依赖门覆盖 ownership、lifecycle、protocol 与 package boundary 契约。 这仍是一个刻意收窄的 non-serving kernel：它不会打开 Runtime Store、组装 `@maka/runtime`、恢复 Session、启动 scheduler、暴露 domain operation、迁移任何交互界面，也不会切换 production owner。这些属于 #853 的后续切片。 ## 设计决策 - **每个 root 只有一个 authority。** 随机 root id 会与首次初始化时的 filesystem identity 持久绑定。路径别名和 root 移动仍会收敛到同一 control namespace；复制已经初始化的 root 会 fail closed，而不会产生第二个 owner。 - **OS lock 是唯一 authority。** Registration、PID、endpoint 与 health 只提供 discovery evidence，不参与所有权判断；不存在 stale-lock stealing 或基于 PID 的 ownership recovery。 - **Ownership 受 capability 约束。** 只有 root authority 可以签发 branded owner/observer handle；Host 在使用前会认证完整 owner aggregate。 - **Host 独立于 launcher 和 Client 生命周期。** Candidate 以 detached 方式启动；Client 断开只释放该连接；idle exit 只能由 Host 自己的 residency gate 提交。 - **不兼容 Host 的替换由 residency 决定。** 协议兼容性由 protocol range 与必要 feature contract 判断。Residency 指任何要求 Host 继续存活的已接纳连接或工作；当前 non-serving M1 kernel 实际只统计 accepted connection 与 active bootstrap/status operation。不兼容且仍有 residency 的 Host 会阻止替换；真正 idle 的不兼容 Host 会通过正常 idle lifecycle 退出，让同一次有界 election 在不重叠 owner 的前提下启动兼容 Host。 - **Election 只有一个 deadline。** Registration 读取、connect、handshake、Candidate launch 与 retry backoff 共用一个 monotonic budget；已经超时的 Client 不会再启动迟到的 detached Candidate。 - **Bootstrap surface 保持最小。** V1 只使用有 64 KiB 上限的 newline-delimited JSON 承载 hello、handshake 与 status。基于真实 exports 的 TypeScript AST gate 使用精确 external-import allowlist，并对动态 loader capability fail closed，禁止 protocol/client 到达 server internals、Runtime composition 或 Store factory。 - **POSIX 本地 transport 默认私有。** 每个 Host epoch 在 current-user directory 下使用随机 UDS。M1 的 Windows named pipe 为 best effort；更强的 ACL 与 packaging 保证会作为明确的后续工作处理，不从 POSIX 行为中推断。 ## 验证 - 根级 `npm run lint`、`npm run typecheck`、`npm test -- --serial`、`npm run build` 与 `npm run check:stale` 均通过。 - `@maka/storage`：314 项通过，1 项既有 Windows-only skip。 - `@maka/runtime-host`：29 项通过。 - 真实 Node/Electron 进程覆盖双向并发 cold start、normal/crash/force-kill 释放、launcher 退出后 Host 存活、stale discovery artifact、compatibility replacement、bounded election、private endpoint permission、malformed/oversized frame 隔离、root identity drift，以及 transport backpressure 下的 shutdown。 - TypeScript AST dependency gate 同时约束 M1 package boundary 与 root-authority leaf boundary。 ## 建议审查重点 - root identity 与 native lock 是否建立了唯一且没有歧义的 ownership authority。 - Host residency、draining、shutdown 与 incompatible replacement 是否可能造成 owner 重叠或 lock 无法释放。 - author: tamird
body:
CPU-load scheduling rejects the first action when CPU capacity is zero because the action cap evaluates 0 >= 3 * 0. The request is then queued on a latch that no running action can release.

Check the hard action cap before sampling machine load, allow only the first local action past a zero-capacity cap, and distinguish tracked CPU usage from effective machine load when applying the allow-one policy. Enforce the cap on subsequent zero- and positive-CPU requests.

Cover loaded positive, zero, and negative CPU capacity; explicit zero-CPU requests; non-CPU resource use; and the action cap.

Fixes #28713.

author: daniel3303
body:
## Summary

The two query shapes behind the "funds holding this stock" lookup were unplannable at production scale and dominated every consumer's latency (~9.5s per cold stock-summary render on the commercial portal; same cost in the MCP/REST GetFundsHoldingStock tools and the fund-series directory rebuild):

1. **`GetHoldingsByStockCusip`** — `Cusip = $1 OR Cusip IN (subquery)` defeats the CUSIP index (Postgres cannot index an OR between a constant and an uncorrelated subquery) and degrades to a full scan of the 25M-row holdings table (~5s). The current CUSIP now rides inside the alias subquery via `UNION`, and explicit not-null filters keep EF's null compensation from reintroducing the OR. Plans as an index semi-join: **0.3ms** measured on production data.

2. **`GetLatestPerSeries`** — the anti-join's identity condition OR-ed the registrant populations together, leaving no hashable key → O(N²) nested loop (10,342² = 85M join-filter evaluations, ~8s). A filing only ever competes with filings of its own population (the identity legs are mutually exclusive), so the dedup is now three partition-scoped branches concatenated with UNION ALL, each leading with a plain hashable equality: **~18ms** measured, with an identical result set (7,621 = 7,621 rows on production data).

## Code changes

- `src/Equibles.Sec.Repositories/NportFilingRepository.cs` — both query rewrites, with comments explaining why the shapes matter (incl. the redundant in-lambda not-null guard that keeps EF from null-compensating the RegistrantCik equality).
- `tests/Equibles.UnitTests/Sec/NportFilingRepositoryQueryTranslationTests.cs` — new ToQueryString translation tests pinning both shapes (no OR in the CUSIP lookup; two UNION ALLs + a bare RegistrantCik equality in the dedup), so a regression fails offline instead of on every stock page.

## Verification

- Semantics: existing `NportFilingRepositoryTests` + `NportFundHoldingsToolTests` (19 tests) pass; both rewrites produce identical row sets on production data (raw-SQL A/B).
- Plans: EXPLAIN ANALYZE on production — 0.335ms (was ~5s) and 17.8ms (was ~8s).
- Full unit suite: 3488/3488 green. Integration suite: 2060/2065 — the 5 failures are the `YahooPriceImportServiceCompanyProfile*` tests, already red on main (introduced by #4155), unrelated to this diff.

author: pentiminax
body:
## Summary

Fixes #243. The filtered count in `DoctrineDataProvider::fetchData()` clones the `QueryBuilder` **after** the user's `configureQueryBuilder` filters run. Those filters can add `leftJoin`s for relation search; when a join traverses a **to-many** association, `COUNT(e)` is inflated by row multiplication, corrupting `recordsFiltered` and breaking pagination.

## Changes
- Filtered count now uses `COUNT(DISTINCT e)` so it counts distinct root entities regardless of to-many joins. A code comment documents the rationale.
- The unfiltered `recordsTotal` count has no joins, so it deliberately keeps `COUNT(e)` — the change stays minimal.

## Tests
Added a regression test (in-memory SQLite EM, `OneToMany` fixtures) where `configureQueryBuilder` adds `leftJoin('e.tags', 't')`, producing row multiplication, and asserts `recordsFiltered` equals the distinct-customer count. Verified it fails on the old `COUNT(e)` code and passes with the fix.

`vendor/bin/phpunit` → **OK (837 tests)**.

## The bug

A peer community post could show an **"Open GDP →"** (or LightHouse / ServiceCredits / Directory) action button that neither the author nor an admin attached — members can't attach plugin links to posts at all. In the reported case a welcome message containing "join the economy" got an "Open GDP" button.

The legacy `getActionForText()` keyword inference inside `buildChatMessage` (`use-home-chat.ts`) ran on **every stored message** and matched substrings like `economy`/`gdp`, `housing`/`lighthouse`, etc., attaching an action button. Since any post not authored by the viewer is treated as `from: 'hub'`, this decorated real peer posts — making it look as if the poster had linked a plugin.

Removed the `getActionForText()` inference entirely (it was already flagged in this plugin's build checklist as superseded by the Feed AI Q&A pipeline). Action buttons now come only from an **explicit** source — the local concierge reply sets its own `actionLabel`/`actionSlug`. A peer community post never carries an inferred action.

- **Web only** — the Android Hub never had this inference (verified).
- The action was **client-side only and never persisted** (community posts store no action), so there's nothing to clean up — the button just stops rendering on next load.

author: oblinger
body:
## What

Adds the **M32.4 environmental-pressure injection dial** — a single, seed-deterministic scenario-level perturbation on the simulator seam. A pressure is an **opaque NAMED perturbation** carried with an **INTENSITY** and a **PERSISTENCE** (an intensity/persistence ladder), surfaced to the simulator as a **removable** displacement overlay so that recovery / resilience can be measured.

## Seam

`suite.verify.simulate(world, sim_cfg, seed, pressure=None)` — the existing WorldSimulator entry point in the `suite` subsystem. The natural (unperturbed) integration is computed **exactly as before**; when a `pressure` is supplied, a per-step displacement overlay `exp(coef * p_t)` is applied on top of the sampled states. New library module `src/alienbio/suite/pressure.py` holds the named registries + `make_pressure(...)` resolver + `EnvironmentalPressure` (with its overlay trajectory).

## The removable-recovery guarantee

`p_t` **builds up** toward `intensity` while the pressure is active and **decays geometrically toward zero** after `remove_at`. Because the overlay relaxes to zero once the pressure is lifted, the reported state **provably returns toward the unperturbed trajectory regardless of the base world's own stability** — recovery is a property of the dial, not of the world. This is the defining property; `remove_at=None` keeps the pressure active for the whole run (no recovery).

## Requirements (all mandatory) — met

- **Absent == identity**: `pressure=None` → byte-identical trace (test asserts `np.array_equal`).
- **Monotone intensity**: overlay plateau scales with intensity → strictly larger perturbation (tested across the `low/moderate/high/severe` ladder + numeric).
- **Removable → recovers**: lift halfway, assert final deviation `<< peak` and `~0`.
- **Seed-deterministic**: optional `jitter>0` draws bounded per-step noise from the framework's seeded RNG (`Seed.rng()`); identical `(pressure, seed)` → identical trace; jitter=0 is fully deterministic.
- **Raises on bad input**: unknown pressure name / out-of-range level / negative `remove_at` / negative `jitter` → `ValueError`, no silent fallback.
- **Domain-neutral**: pressures + intensity/persistence levels are opaque named ordinals, no biology semantics.

## Tests

New `tests/suite/test_pressure.py` — **19 tests** covering absent=identity, monotone intensity, removable-and-recovers, seed reproducibility, bad-input raises, and overlay build/decay mechanics.

- `uv run pytest tests/` → **1884 passed, 32 skipped** (was 1865 passed baseline; +19 new).
- `uv run pyright src/` → **147 errors, unchanged from baseline**; **0 errors** in the touched files (`pressure.py`, `verify.py`).

body:
## Summary

Fixes the Baseball Scoreboard's Live/Recent/Upcoming Display Mode setting being ignored when set to "Scroll" outside of Vegas mode. Games kept flipping/switching one at a time instead of scrolling, even though the config was set to scroll.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix in an existing plugin

## Plugin(s) affected

baseball-scoreboard

## Related issues

N/A — reported directly by a user, no linked issue.

## Root cause

`display()` routes every granular per-league mode (`mlb_live`, `mlb_recent`, `mlb_upcoming`, `milb_*`, `ncaa_baseball_*` — the only modes registered in `manifest.json`) straight to `_display_league_mode()`. That method never checked the `live_display_mode`/`recent_display_mode`/`upcoming_display_mode` config and always fell through to the switch/flip behavior via `_try_manager_display()`.

The existing scroll machinery (`_should_use_scroll_mode`, `_display_scroll_mode`) was only reachable from `_display_external_mode()`'s "combined mode" branch — a code path `display()` never actually calls for granular modes (there's even a self-aware log line admitting this in the code). Vegas mode worked because it bypasses `display()` entirely and calls the scroll manager directly and unconditionally via `get_vegas_content()` → `_collect_games_for_scroll(mode_type=None, ...)`.

## Fix

Added `_display_league_scroll_mode()`, called from `_display_league_mode()` whenever the league/mode's configured display mode is `'scroll'`. It mirrors `_display_scroll_mode()`'s prepare/display-frame/is-complete flow but is scoped to a single league. Since the underlying `ScrollDisplayManager` keeps one active scroll session per `mode_type` (shared across leagues), it also tracks which league's content is currently prepared and forces a re-prepare when that changes (e.g. rotation switches from `mlb_live` to `milb_live` and both are set to scroll), so leagues don't stomp on each other's scroll state.

## Test plan

- [ ] Loaded the plugin in LEDMatrix on real hardware
- [ ] Loaded the plugin in LEDMatrix emulator mode (`EMULATOR=true python3 run.py`)
- [ ] Rendered the plugin in the dev preview server (`scripts/dev_server.py`)

Runtime verification (setting MLB Display Mode to Scroll and observing on-device/emulator behavior) was not performed in this environment — please verify on hardware/emulator before merge.

## Required for plugin changes
