body:
Closes #65, #66, #67, #68, #69, #70, #71, #72.

Batch fix for the 8 tickets filed from the Nexus build, released as **v0.29.0** (changelog + upgrade registry + SECURITY.md rolled in this PR). Two of the fixes are **BREAKING** and carry migration notes in `cmd/gofastr/upgrades.yml`.

## Tickets

| # | Fix |
|---|---|
| **#65** | **BREAKING** — generated CRUD + entity MCP tools require an authenticated session by default; `EntityConfig.Public` / blueprint `public: true` is the explicit opt-out. SSE stays stricter (only `Public` opens an anonymous stream). `gofastr generate` warns on every public entity. |
| **#66** | Eager-load `BelongsTo` tolerates NULL foreign keys (scans through `sql.NullString`) instead of failing the whole `?include=`. |
| **#67** | Fresh-Postgres first boot: `BOOLEAN` DDL for bool columns (+ lossless legacy `INTEGER` upgrade), and the bootstrap-admin seed moved to `WithSeed` (post-migrate, errors surfaced). |
| **#68** | Generated `e2e_test.go` is Windows- (`.exe`) and Postgres-portable (driver-aware DB bootstrap, `t.Skip` when PG unreachable). |
| **#69** | Documented the audit pre-image casing contract; added `AuditPreImageAs[T]` + `AuditPreImageSnakeFromContext`, reusing the existing casing machinery. |
| **#70** | **BREAKING** — `PATCH /<entity>/{id}` for sparse updates, and a unified `{"data":{...}}` envelope for all single-record responses; every in-repo client migrated. |
| **#71** | Configurable `SecurityHeaders`; core-ui router accepts both `:param` and `{param}`; dev-mode relaxes the per-IP login limiter (per-account brute-force gate stays on). |
| **#72** | `gofastr audit a11y` drives login to audit authenticated pages with honest coverage; admin audit log now actually records (the admin handler was bypassing hooks with a nil-hook handler). |

## Process

Each ticket was fixed TDD (repro-first, since they were filed against v0.26.1 and the repo is at v0.28.0), with docs shipped in the same change. The batch then went through **two independent adversarial reviews** (correctness/security + breadth/docs): no gate bypass was found, but 5 P1 integration defects were — admin audit-redaction casing bypass, admin audit metadata, generated PATCH client zero-values, `pack` dropping `Public`, and owner-seed-before-admin ordering — all fixed with proving tests in a follow-up commit.

Also fixes two pre-existing worktree-hermeticity test bugs (`TestStart_BindFailureRunsShutdown` — the `/tmp` vs `/private/tmp` bind-isolation flake — and the generator `go run` module-path failures) so CI is green on every checkout, not just plain clones.

## Verification

Full CI mirror run locally and green: deterministic packages (160, `-p 2`), gofmt-tracked-clean, vet, `coverage-floors.sh`, repolint, and every browser-e2e suite serialized (site, axe, kiln, meridian, core-ui/runtime, core-ui/widget).

## The feature

Game code reorders vector lanes constantly — `pos.xz` for a ground plane, `.yx` to flip, `.xxyy` to expand. This adds GLSL-style swizzles to the existing first-class SIMD vectors: **2-4 lane letters read the named lanes into a new vector, in letter order.** Duplicates and re-broadening a narrower vector are allowed; single-letter reads stay scalar exactly as before.

```bet
lowkey a: vec4 = vec4(1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0)
lowkey r: vec2 = a.yx        // [2,1]
lowkey d: vec4 = a.xxww      // [1,1,4,4]
lowkey e: vec4 = vec2(5.0, 6.0).yxyx
```

## Design: pure lowering sugar

`v.yx` emits the exact lane-extract + `simd[...]` aggregate MIR that `vec2(v.y, v.x)` does. Consequences:

- **No grammar change** (member access already parses), **no new midir ops, no backend or runtime work** — LLVM's O2 pipeline folds extract+build into shufflevector on its own.
- **betfe parity is tractable**: `fieldAccessStr` mirrors the same desugar with identical emission order (lane temps, then the aggregate temp), so `.mir` output stays byte-identical — gated by `selfhost.yml` as usual.
- Every letter is validated (xyzw + in-range for the source arity) before any code is emitted, in all three implementations (lower_field, interp, betfe).

## Tests

New corpus program `15-simd/simd-swizzle` (interp = pass, compiled = pass): reverse, narrow+reorder (`.wzy`), duplicate lanes (`.xxww` through `.dot`), broadening a vec2 (`.yxyx`), and an integer-vector case (`i32x4 → .wy`). MANIFEST gains the `simd.swizzle` feature key. The three-way differential (interp == compiled == .expected, at O0 and O2) plus the selfhost byte-parity gate are the correctness argument.

## Caveat

Authored without a local toolchain (no cargo/LLVM on this machine) — this PR's own CI is the build/test run. If a leg is red I'll iterate here.

author: mac8o
body:
## What & why

Adds a **per-IP login throttle** to close a password-spraying gap.

The existing account lockout (`failed_login_attempts` + `locked_until`) stops someone brute-forcing **one** account, but does nothing against **spraying** — one failed attempt each across many accounts from a single IP, which never trips any individual account's lockout threshold. This adds a per-IP failed-attempt budget as defense-in-depth.

## How it works

- New `SecurityPolicy::loginThrottlePerIp()` — max failed sign-ins per minute from one IP (default **20**, tunable via the `login_throttle_ip_per_min` system setting, consistent with the other configurable policy thresholds).
- Enforced in `AuthController::login()`: over-limit requests are rejected **before the DB lookup**, with the same friendly on-form error the account lockout already uses.
- **Only failures are counted** (`RateLimiter::hit` fires solely on a failed `Auth::attempt`), so many staff signing in successfully behind one shared campus NAT IP are never throttled.

## Tests

`tests/Feature/AuthTest.php` — new `test_login_is_ip_throttled_against_password_spraying`: sprays failures across several different accounts (none reaching its own lockout) and asserts the IP is then refused, even for a correct credential. All 8 auth tests pass, including the existing account-lockout tests (no interference between the two mechanisms).

## Not included (from the security discussion)

SQL injection was reviewed and is **already prevented** (Eloquent/PDO prepared statements throughout; raw fragments are constants or `?`-bound). Security-headers middleware, audit-record enrichment, and read-access logging were discussed but deferred.

author: ns-ctw
body:
## Problem

A single web turn can span multiple `agent_start`/`agent_end` pairs: each **subagent** run fires its own pair on the same emitter. The bridge treated the *first* `agent_end` as the whole turn's end — sent `done`, cleared `ourTurnActive` — so the rest of the main turn stopped streaming (斷更) and `isBusy` was left toggled (stuck 'busy').

Confirmed on session 019f6d80 with the new lifecycle logging (#81): `agent_start(ourTurnActive=true)` → `agent_end` → `done` → a **second** `agent_start(ourTurnActive=false)` running orphaned.

## Fix

Guard `agent_start`/`agent_end` with `isForeignAgentEvent(ctx)`: skip when the firing session is positively different from, or more ephemeral than, the bridge's own persisted session (mirrors the existing `session_start` `isPersisted()` skip at line ~911). Conservative — when the session can't be identified it falls through, so the **main session's events are never skipped** (no regression on normal turns).

## Verification

- Extension 162/162, biome clean.
- Isolated bridge, real agent, normal turn: main events log `foreign=false / persisted=true`, turn streams and completes (busy→done) unchanged.
- The subagent leg can't be triggered under `--no-extensions` (no subagent tool), but the `ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId()/isPersisted()` discriminator is proven to return the main session's real id/persisted=true, so a subagent's ephemeral session will read `foreign=true` and be skipped. The sid/persisted logging is kept to confirm `foreign=true` on subagent events in production.

author: hassanhabib
body:
Scaffolds the solution so every later issue has a home.

## Projects

| Project | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `Standard.Agents` | the library (net10.0) |
| `Standard.Agents.Tests.Unit` | xUnit, mirroring the service tree |

`Standard.Agents.Demo` and `Standard.Agents.Conformance` are created by their own issues (#38, #39) rather than scaffolded here as empty placeholders — a console project needs a `Program.cs`, and that code belongs to the issue that owns it.

## Packages

The library previously carried **zero package references**. Two enter, deliberately:

- **`Xeption`** — required by The Standard's exception model (`UpsertDataList`, `ThrowIfContainsErrors`)
- **`RESTFulSense`** — gives `GeneratorBroker` the typed HTTP exception ladder that `BrainService` maps against, replacing `EnsureSuccessStatusCode()` + null-forgiving `response!`

All-In/All-Out: partial adoption is not standardization.

⚖️ **`FluentAssertions` is pinned to 7.2.2**, the last Apache-2.0 release. Version 8+ ships under a commercial Xceed license — pinning keeps the repo free of any paid-license obligation.

## Layout

```
Standard.Agents
  |-- Brokers/{Data,Decision,Direction,Loggings}
  |-- Models/Foundations/{Skills,Memories,Knowledges,Gates,Brains,Judges,
  |                       InternalTools,ExternalTools,Returns}/Exceptions
  |-- Models/Orchestrations/Agents      AgentContext, AgentStatus
  |-- Services/{Foundations,Orchestrations,Coordinations}/{Data,Decision,Direction}
  |-- Tools
```

`AgentContext` lives under `Models/Orchestrations/Agents` — a **deliberate shared model**. The Standard forbids models shared across independent flows (horizontal entanglement), but the three natures are one loop, not independent flows, and SPEC.md §3 mandates a single context record.

## Verification

```
dotnet build   → Build succeeded. 0 Error(s)
dotnet test    → runner wired; no tests yet (first lands with #7)
```

Closes #6

## Feature 029 — Sense Pictures

Reproduce a copied sense's pictures — the `CmPicture` owned object graph
(caption/description multistrings + layout scalars, in order) **and** the
backing image asset copied into the target `LinkedFiles` area — under 024's
never-silent guarantee. Closes the 024-census `DROP_REPORTED` gap for
`LexSense.PicturesOS`.

> **Draft — held pending a flexicon fix.** The offline gate is green and the
> code runs live, but the attended live proof (T020) is blocked by a flexicon
> `AddPicture`/`CopyToProject` `NullReferenceException` (see below). Do not
> merge until T020 passes on a fixed flexicon build.

### What's here

New `src/gramtrans/Lib/pictures.py` — a Move leg (`reproduce_sense_pictures`)
and its read-only Preview twin (`plan_sense_picture_decisions`), mirroring the
028 `reproduce_moaffix_msenv_data` / `_plan_moaffix_msenv_decisions` pair —
wired into `categories._walk_lex_entry_closure` (Move) and
`_plan_entry_reference_decisions` (Preview). `PicturesOS` removed from
`categories._SENSE_SCOPE_GAP_FIELDS` (Appendixes/Thesaurus stay, routed to 030).

| Story | Delivered |
|---|---|
| US1 | `CmPicture` deep-copy — Caption/Description ws-mapped (024 helper) + 5 layout scalars, `PicturesOS` order; Preview emits one CREATE per picture |
| US2 | Backing image copied via `AddPicture` seam; per-run content-hash dedup cache; Preview CREATE-vs-LINK |
| US3 | Non-destructive collision handling — identical reused, same-name/different-content copied under a de-duplicated name (never clobbers) + reported |
| US4 | Never-silent filesystem failures — missing binary → `CmPicture`+`CmFile` wired at intended path (no bytes) + drop; unreadable/unwritable → reported, no partial write; identical Preview/Move drop set |
| US5 | Idempotency by structural fingerprint (image identity + caption); non-destructive empty source |
| Census | `("LexSense","PicturesOS")` flipped `DROP_REPORTED → COPIED`, never-silent guard preserved |

### Test status (offline — green)

- `tests/unit tests/verification`: **1791 passed**, 34 skipped; only the 7
  documented environment-baseline failures (6 `test_013_apply_syncable_signature`
  flexicon-tree-absent + 1 `test_wizard_pos_grammar_wiring`).

  files**, so hashing/dedup/collision/missing-binary run for real). See
  `specs/029-sense-pictures/verification-log.md`.

The attended live proof was run on **disposable project copies**. The worktree
code imports and runs live, but flexicon's `AddPicture` →
`MediaOperations.CopyToProject` → `CmFile.set_InternalPath` throws a .NET
`NullReferenceException` in this runtime — an environment/flexicon defect,

(two defects: `Create` sets `InternalPath` on an unowned `CmFile`;

`LangProject`). That seam is the Move-leg happy path, so live asset copy can't
be demonstrated until flexicon is fixed. The module degrades gracefully
(contract G7 — catches and reports, never crashes).

body:
### Motivation

- Provide a Phase 1 prototype of a private Android container (Valcrono VirtualSpace) that can import APKs, validate/store them, and run a minimal cooperative runtime via a `ProxyActivity`.
- Add modular runtime APIs and infrastructure for virtual storage, package import/compatibility scanning, file management, process/launch tokens and a small UI host to exercise the platform.
- Enable CI to build, test and publish debug APK artifacts automatically.

### Description

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

The container crashed on startup because run_migrations.py failed with psycopg2.errors.DuplicateObject: type "authprovider" already exists. The initial Alembic migration (001_initial.py) unconditionally ran CREATE TYPE statements for five enums, which fails when the types already exist in the target database. Since run_migrations.py re-raises on failure, uvicorn never started, causing the /health healthcheck to fail all retries.

## Solution

Wrapped each CREATE TYPE statement in a DO $$ ... EXCEPTION WHEN duplicate_object THEN null END $$ block so the statement becomes a no-op when the type already exists. The migration now completes successfully even against a database that already has these enums, allowing run_migrations.py to exit 0 and uvicorn to start.

author: linkmodo
body:
## Summary

Three related changes to the crop-ratio picker and auto-detection:

**1. Consolidated the ratio picker, added common print/screen sizes.** The dropdown listed every ratio in both orientations (3:2 *and* 2:3, 4:3 *and* 3:4, …) even though the crop tool already auto-orients to match the drag — the reversed entries never did anything a single canonical entry couldn't. Now one entry per shape, plus 7:5, 16:9, 16:10 and 8.5:11 which were missing entirely. The full `AspectRatio` enum keeps every reciprocal, because the Export "Paper ratio" picker doesn't auto-orient and genuinely needs both. `canonical_crop_ratio()` maps legacy/portrait stored values onto the visible entry.

**2. The crop box now reshapes when you pick a new ratio.** Previously it stayed visually stale until you redragged it. New `AppController.set_crop_ratio()` reshapes in place around the box's existing center, reusing `enforce_roi_aspect_ratio` (the same centered-reshape auto-crop uses). The math runs in real pixel space and accounts for 90° rotation, since a normalized "square" isn't square on a non-square image.

**3. Fixed auto-detect misclassifying 35mm scans as 7:5.** `_closest_standard_ratio` matched against the whole `AspectRatio` enum, which after change 1 included print/screen output sizes. 7:5 (1.4) and 16:10 (1.6) sit close enough to 3:2 (1.5) in log-ratio space that ordinary contour noise — sprocket holes, margin trimming — tipped a genuine 3:2 frame onto them. Detection now uses a dedicated `FILM_FORMAT_RATIOS` list of formats a camera/scanner can actually produce; the picker keeps the full list.

**4. Fixed a colour shift on ratio change.** Changing the ratio visibly shifted colour on the canvas. `set_crop_ratio` was clearing the per-file metering bounds, and since normalization meters *within* the crop ROI (`resolve_analysis_region`), re-analyzing over the new smaller ROI landed on different per-channel floors/ceils. On a real scan going 3:2 → 4:3 the red floor moved `+0.0058` while blue moved `-0.0056` — opposite directions, a cast shift rather than a brightness change. The other crop paths clear the bounds because the crop decides whether the film rebate is inside the metered region; a ratio change can't pull rebate in, since both the reshape and autocrop's `_enforce_ratio_by_occupancy` only ever shrink within a footprint that already excludes it. So the invalidation there could only ever drift. **This predates the branch** — with auto crop on, the ratio has always fed `get_autocrop_coords` and re-metered; change 2 extended the same fault to the manual-crop path.

## Test plan
- [x] **Colour shift**, verified against the real app on both the manual-crop and auto-crop paths: rendered floors/ceils are now bit-identical across a ratio change, and the shift reproduces when the invalidation is put back
- [x] **Reshape**, verified against the real app: a 0.6×0.7 box at (0.4, 0.55) becomes a true 747×747 pixel square on a 1600×1067 preview, center preserved
- [x] **Detection**: regression test sweeps ROIs measuring 1.42–1.58 (a real 3:2 frame plus plausible detection noise) and confirms none flip to 7:5/16:10
- [x] **Picker**, verified against the real app: dropdown matches `CROP_RATIO_CHOICES` with no reciprocal duplicates, and a legacy `"2:3"` stored value displays as `"3:2"`
- [x] 8 new unit tests across `test_controller.py` and `test_geometry_logic.py`, including a guard that the reshape never grows the box (the invariant change 4 depends on)
- [x] Full suite: 1963 passed. The one failure, `test_export_presets.py::test_output_dir_subfolder_of_source`, is a pre-existing Windows path-separator issue that reproduces on a clean `main`
- [x] `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean

author: adityathebe
body:
## Summary

Addresses the two open **CodeQL** code-scanning alerts on `master`:

| Alert | Location | Resolution |
|-------|----------|------------|
| #41 — Clear-text logging of sensitive information | `http/middlewares/logger.go` | **Fixed** in code |
| #43 — Use of a broken or weak cryptographic hashing algorithm | `http/digest.go` | **Documented** — protocol-mandated, dismiss as *Won't fix* |

## #41 — Clear-text logging (fixed)

The HTTP logging middleware wrote request URLs and transport errors verbatim. When a URL carries userinfo (`https://user:pass@host`) — or a transport error wraps such a URL — the embedded password was written to the logs in clear text.

- Log `req.URL` via `URL.Redacted()`, which masks the userinfo password, at every log sink in `jsonLogger`.
- `accessURL()` now returns `URL.Redacted()` too (it previously only stripped the query/fragment, leaving userinfo intact).
- Transport error strings are passed through `logger.StripSecrets(...)` before logging, so credentials embedded in a wrapped `url.Error` are redacted.

The header/body/query/form values reaching these log calls were already sanitized (`SanitizeHeaders`, `StripSecretsFromMap`, `IsSensitiveKey`); the URL and error paths were the remaining gap.

## #43 — MD5 in Digest auth (won't fix)

The flagged `md5.New()` is HTTP **Digest Authentication** (RFC 7616), where MD5 is the protocol-mandated default and the algorithm is chosen by the **server**, not the client. Many servers only offer MD5, so removing it would break authentication against them. SHA-256 is already used whenever the server advertises it.

This is a known false positive for digest auth. Rather than change behavior, this PR adds a doc comment on `hashStr` explaining why MD5 is retained. The alert should be dismissed in the Security tab as *Won't fix / used as required by protocol*.

## Testing

- `go build ./...` and `go vet ./http/...` pass.
- Offline digest tests (`TestDigestTransport`, `TestParseWWWAuthenticate`, `TestDigestAuthString`, …) and the full `logger` package tests pass. The remaining `TestHTTP` failures are unrelated — they require outbound network access to external hosts, which is blocked in the CI sandbox.

## Note (out of scope)

`http/middlewares/trace.go:254` also sets `req.URL.String()` as an OpenTelemetry span attribute, which has the same userinfo-leak shape but was not flagged by CodeQL. Happy to redact it in a follow-up if desired.

Specialized errors such as `PluginSetupError` were therefore created and immediately discarded for every published bundle. ## Example A plugin registered before initialization throws from `registerPlugin()`. React Grab removes that failed queued plugin and continues, but production users receive no warning or error object explaining why the plugin disappeared. ## Changes - Report specialized recoverable errors in production as well as development. - Add an artifact-level regression test against the built CommonJS production bundle. - Preserve the existing recovery behavior; failures still do not crash the host app. ## Validation - `nr build` - `nr test` — 1,067 passed, 24 skipped - `pnpm --filter react-grab exec playwright test e2e/ssr.spec.ts` — 16 passed - `nr lint` - `nr typecheck` - `nr format` - `git diff --check` --- ## Summary by cubic Keep recoverable error diagnostics in production for `react-grab`. author: kdwevedi
body:
Fixes #1276.

## RCA summary — the answer to "which failure point"

Full trace with file:line evidence in [the RCA comment on #1276](https://github.com/egovernments/Citizen-Complaint-Resolution-System/issues/1276#issuecomment-4999321700). Short version — three real failure points plus one misread, all silent:

1. **Attach fails on the drag path (primary).** The Add-KPI picker items have been HTML5 drag *sources* since they landed (draggable, `dataTransfer` kpiId payload, panel hides during drag) — but the grid was never made a drop *target*: `onDragWidgetStart/End` were `() => {}` no-ops and the RGL grid had no `isDroppable`/`onDrop`. Drag → drop → nothing; panel closes on dragend. Reads exactly as "selected a KPI, nothing appeared". (Click on the small `+` did work.)
2. **Adds vanish on reload for roles with an empty pack seed.** `useCatalogLayout` gated hydration on `seed.length` — but `/v2/analytics/packs` legitimately returns `defaultLayout: []` when no `DashboardPack` matches the caller's roles (`AnalyticsController.java:104`). For those employees the saved layout was never read back: picker adds worked in-session, then disappeared on every reload.
3. **Adds clobbered across personas.** The layout persisted under ONE global localStorage key (`ccrs.dashboard.catalog-layout.v1`) — not per user/tenant. Bug-bash pattern (GRO + supervisor on one browser): the second login reconciles the first user's layout against its own catalog and the next persist rewrites the shared slot — the first user's additions are gone. Plus a narrow variant: the 300 ms debounced drag-persist captured stale layout and could overwrite a just-persisted add/remove.
4. **Not-a-bug that reads as one:** the picker lists the role catalog *minus placed tiles*, so an employee with everything placed sees an empty picker — and a role with an empty catalog saw the *same* message.

## What this PR does

- **Drag-and-drop placement** (react-grid-layout's native external-drop): `isDroppable` is enabled only while a picker drag is live (foreign drags never conjure a placeholder), `droppingItem` is sized from the tile's real default size so the hover placeholder and landing cell are honest, and `onDrop` funnels into the **same** `addKpiToLayout(kpiId, {x, y})` used by picker clicks — one code path for attach + persist + batch refetch. Click-to-append is unchanged as the fallback; `draggableCancel` selectors untouched. RGL's synthetic `__dropping-elem__` is filtered before state/storage.
- **Hydration fix:** gate on catalog readiness, not seed length — empty-seed roles now restore saved additions on reload.
- **Storage key scoped per user + tenant** (`<base>.<tenantId>.<userUuid>`); the legacy global key is read once as a migration and never written again.
- **Stale-debounce guard:** structural persists (add/remove/reset) cancel any pending debounced write.
- **Picker empty-states split** with localized copy in both en_IN and pt_PT packs: `DASHBOARD_HEADER_ALL_KPIS_ON_DASHBOARD` → "All available KPIs are already on your dashboard" / "Todos os KPIs disponíveis já estão no seu painel"; new `DASHBOARD_HEADER_NO_KPIS_FOR_ROLE` → "No KPIs available for your role" / "Nenhum KPI disponível para a sua função".
- **Testability:** the pure half of `useCatalogLayout` (constraints, seed/saved reconciliation, add placement, storage IO with injected Storage, RGL-echo merge) moved to `utils/layoutStore.js`; the hook keeps only React state.

## Tests / validation

- New `node --test` suite `products/dashboard/src/utils/layoutStore.test.js` (16 tests): the empty-seed rehydrate regression, per-user key isolation + legacy migration, click-add placement, duplicate/unknown no-ops, drop-position honour + grid clamping, drop-onto-occupied compaction (no drop-out), `__dropping-elem__` stripping, constraint re-attachment.
- All pre-existing node tests pass (`hierLevelGrouping`, `applyTheme`, `transform-css` — 57 tests).
- `npm run build` (esbuild production) green.

## Interplay with in-flight dashboard PRs

Merge-checked against the `integration/dashboard-212` branch (develop + #1268 metrics client + #1285 tree type-filter, which both touch `AdminDashboard.jsx`): **two trivial textual conflicts only** — adjacent import lines in `AdminDashboard.jsx` (keep both) and one comment line in `dashboard-l10n-seed.ts` (l10n pack code-count phrase; both packs stay 1:1, 316 codes). On the resolved merge: all 64 node tests pass and the esbuild build is green; the drop wiring, metrics instrumentation, and filter changes don't interact semantically. #1283 (Group-by control) is already merged in the base of this branch.

Note: a second, older copy of the dashboard lives at `frontend/micro-ui/web/src/dashboard/` (pre-esbuild-migration, not mounted by the esbuild app); this PR intentionally fixes only the live `digit-ui-esbuild/products/dashboard/` module.


## Live-repro follow-up (2026-07-17): cancelled drags wedged the grid

Owner repro on bomet — drop "does not attach", console flooding `Error: <g> attribute transform: Expected number, "translate(NaN, 0)"` — was **reproduced against the deployed integration build and root-caused by reading react-grid-layout's internal state off the React fiber**:

**Root cause.** RGL 1.3.4 has **no cancel path for external drags**. Its dropping state (`droppingDOMNode`, the `__dropping-elem__` entry in `state.layout`, `dragEnterCounter`, and — once the synthetic GridItem drag engages — `activeDrag`) is only cleaned by a drop **on the grid** or by dragleave events balancing the counter back to 0. Two routes leave it stranded: releasing the drag anywhere off the grid (header, picker, ESC), and **leaked dragenters** — a hovered child DOM node that gets replaced mid-drag (chart redraws do this constantly) never fires its dragleave, so the counter can't reach 0 even on a clean exit. After one such drag, `activeDrag` stays non-null **forever**; `getDerivedStateFromProps` then returns `null` on every prop change, so each later add (drop *or* click) persists to storage but never renders — "does not attach". Observed downstream in the same stuck session: the grid rendered collapsed, chart re-measure thrash produced the apexcharts y-axis `translate(NaN, 0)` flood, and the renderer eventually hard-froze (~45 s hang).

**Fix (two halves, `f3f21a20` + `f94551d2`):**
- *Prevention:* while a picker drag is live, `.dashboard-grid-layout--dropping` disables `pointer-events` on grid items so dragenter/leave only ever target the grid container — the counter stays balanced, and `layerX/layerY` (which RGL reads relative to the event target) become grid-relative, fixing placeholder jumpiness over tiles.
- *Recovery:* a pure `pickerDragLifecycle` tracker (dragstart → `onDropDragOver` = engaged → `onDrop` = cleaned) decides at dragend whether RGL was left holding dropping state; if so a synthetic `drop` is dispatched at the grid **before** `isDroppable` flips false, driving RGL's own onDrop cleanup. `droppingKpiIdRef` is nulled first so the synthetic drop can never become an add.
- *Hardening:* drop coordinates are rounded + NaN-clamped before persisting; `defaultSizeForKpi` is pinned to always return finite `w/h` (the placeholder can never hand RGL an undefined size — `dataTransfer.getData` is empty during dragover in Chrome, so sizing relies on state set at dragstart).

**Validation on the deployed bomet build:** the exact wedge recipe (engage grid → leaked dragenter → exit → dragend, no drop) now leaves RGL fully clean (`activeDrag: null`, counter 0, no `__dropping-elem__`, all tiles rendered), and an immediately following drag-drop attaches and persists integer-only coordinates. New `node --test` suite `pickerDragLifecycle.test.js` pins the cleanup decision table; layout suite extended with NaN/fraction drop-coordinate regressions (110 node tests green on the integration merge, esbuild build green).

author: hyperpolymath
body:
## Summary

Makes the flagship **"compile-time shape verification"** claim *true*. Previously the `@axiom` macro parsed `input::`/`output::` type annotations but never used them — shape checks were runtime-only, and the README's `BrokenModel` "Compile error" example could not actually fire (it also used an aspirational API that doesn't match the code).

This wires genuine verification into the macro. `_verify_axiom_shapes` runs **during macro expansion** — i.e. at compile time, before the model is ever constructed or run — tracking the tensor shape from the `input::` declaration through the layer chain. A provable mismatch raises an error at expansion:

```
@axiom BrokenModel: compile-time shape mismatch in `output`.
  Dense layer expects 128 input feature(s), but the incoming tensor has 256.
  Running shape entering this layer: (:batch, 256).
```

## Design — sound but incomplete (by intent)

It rejects **only** mismatches provable from the declared shapes and literal layer sizes:
- each `Dense`'s declared `in_features` vs the running feature dim along the chain;
- the computed `output` vs the `output::` declaration.

Anything it cannot statically resolve — `Conv`/pool output geometry, non-literal layer arguments, unrecognised layers — collapses the running shape to *unknown* and passes through unchecked. So a **valid model never receives a false compile error**; only definite, literal-provable contradictions are rejected.

## Changes

- **`src/dsl/axiom_macro.jl`** — `_verify_axiom_shapes` + helpers (`_extract_shape_dims`, `_shape_after_layer`, `_flatten_pipeline`, a shape-preserving-layer whitelist); called at the top of `generate_axiom_code`.
- **`test/runtests.jl`** — new **"Compile-Time Shape Verification"** testset. The DSL previously had **zero** `@axiom` tests; this covers valid chains, the three mismatch types (Dense in-features, first-layer input, output declaration), the Conv/Flatten soundness case, and the no-input case.
- **`README.adoc`** — the flagship example rewritten to the **real API** (`Dense(in,out)`, `(:batch,N)`) showing the actual compile error, with an explicit soundness caveat.

## Verification

- Full suite: **732/732 passing** (`Pkg.test()`, 5m03s) — includes the new testset; no regressions.
- The real `@axiom` macro path accepts the `mnist.jl`/`simple_classifier.jl`-style chains unchanged and rejects the mismatch cases.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

The audit's other Tier-1 item — the **PyTorch `.pt`/`.pth` bridge** claimed as shipped (`scripts/pytorch_to_axiom_descriptor.py` is absent) — is **not** addressed here: `.pt` files are Python-pickle and importing them needs PyTorch (Python), which is banned estate-wide. That claim needs a separate honest correction (the JSON-descriptor path is what actually ships) or a non-Python reader.

author: neoxelox
body:
Implements `specs/flaggers/improvements.md` (all three phases in one PR, as agreed): flaggers move from per-trace to per-session, run after moments, and gain a hint catalog that routes suspicious sessions to the LLM pass without sampling.

## why

LLM flagger recall was structurally capped: a strategy only reached the classifier through its private `ambiguous` pre-filter or the 10% sample of `no-match` traces — `forgetting` had no pre-filter at all, so its recall was literally the sampling %. Meanwhile the platform already computes strong per-session suspicion signals for 100% of sessions (span/tool errors, cohort percentiles, moment labels) that flagging never saw. Running per trace also re-scanned the same accumulated conversation on every trace of a session.

## the two passes

Flagging is now two named passes, each a use-case + Temporal workflow:

- **Screening** (`screenSessionFlaggersUseCase` / `flaggerScreeningWorkflow`) — deterministic, free, 100% of sessions. Triggered by the moments persist activity publishing `flagger-screening` per recorded generation (including `skipped_*`/`failed` analyses — short sessions still deserve tool-error/jailbreak checks; not for `hash_current` or backfills). Loads the session, gathers hints, runs every strategy's deterministic detection (`matched`/`unmatched` — `ambiguous` is gone), writes matched scores directly, and routes the rest.
- **Classification** (`classifySessionFlaggerUseCase` / `flaggerClassificationWorkflow`) — the LLM pass, started as detached child workflows per session×slug. Classify (screening hints rendered into the prompt as leads-not-proof) → adversarial review → draft (dedup **before** billing) → save.

The BullMQ dedupe key for screening embeds the `analysisHash`: a bare per-session jobId would shadow every later generation after the first completes.

## hints

Cheap deterministic session evidence, gathered once per pass and visible to all strategies (`<entity>:<hint>` kinds): `span:error`, `tool:error`, `tool:loop`, four `outlier:*` (project p90 via the existing cohort baseline, Redis-cached 15 min), `moment:*` (generation-pinned labels), and six `pattern:*` gatherers — five are the old per-strategy ambiguous pre-filters relocated, plus a new PII one. A negative hint mapped in a strategy's `hintKinds` escalates it to `hinted`: rate-limited (30/min/org/slug) but **never sampled**. Unhinted strategies keep the 10% sample with their own buckets (25/min, 5/min when the session carries positive `user_satisfaction`/`resolution` hints). `forgetting` gets its first pre-LLM signal.

## anchor dedup

Sessions re-screen on every settle, and score deletion is off the table, so writes dedup on `metadata.anchorHash` — a content hash of the flagged message. Content survives compaction renumbering (indices don't) and LLM feedback re-wording (feedback text doesn't), while still letting one flagger flag several distinct parts of a long conversation. The check runs before billing authorization, and the billing idempotency key is anchor-scoped, so a re-detected issue never re-bills. Score rows keep `sessionId` plus the session's latest output trace as `traceId`, so trace surfaces stay coherent; `messageIndex` now shares the session drawer / moment-pill index space.

## new verticals

- `bluffing` — assistant proceeds past a failed tool call as if it succeeded (rides the `tool:error` hint).
- `pii-leakage` — assistant output exposes personal data it shouldn't have (rides `pattern:pii`).
- `tool-call-errors` also flags calls to tools missing from the session's declared toolset (`definedTools`, already in the sessions MV, now exposed on the entity).
- Moment kinds `user_correction` and `stalling` in conversation-intelligence (detector bumped to `ci-v7`, so sessions re-analyze on their next trace). The flagger hint union derives from `MOMENT_KINDS`, so new kinds flow in via typecheck.

A custom migration backfills `bluffing`/`pii-leakage` rows for every existing project — plus `low-cache-hit-rate`, which shipped in June without one. TS/Python SDKs bump to 9.3.0 and the CLI to 7.3.0 for the two new public slugs (artifacts regenerated).

## rollout and follow-ups

`trace-end` stops publishing `deterministic-flaggers` in this PR. The old per-trace pipeline (`deterministic-flaggers` + `start-flagger-workflow` workers, `flaggerWorkflow`, trimmed `processFlaggersUseCase`) stays registered drain-only; a cleanup PR deletes it ≥1 day after deploy (spec P1-j). Deterministic flags now land ~5 min after session quiet instead of ~90 s after trace end — accepted, flaggers feed signals/incidents. Known accepted risk: anchor dedup is select-then-insert without a DB unique index, so a narrow race across overlapping generations can double-publish an anchor; a partial unique index is the follow-up if dogfood shows duplicates.

## validation

No offline benchmarks by design (no datasets for 11 of 13 strategies); the screening activity logs a summary per pass (decision counts, fired hint kinds, started classifications) so hinted-vs-sampled match rates are readable off plain logs. 287 flagger tests (screening routing, anchor dedup across growth/compaction, every gatherer, suppression parity, the new strategies) plus workers/workflows/conversation-intelligence suites; full workspace typecheck and knip clean. Pre-existing OTLP test failures in `@domain/spans` on `development` are unrelated.

author: randomparity
body:
Closes #1250.

## Problem

`systems.check_ssh_reachable` is a banner-only, auth-free probe: `reachable=true` means the guest's sshd is answering, not that the caller's key is authorized. It returned a bare job handle whose only suggested next actions were the generic job-lifecycle set (`jobs.wait`/`jobs.cancel`), so an agent read `reachable=true` as "I can log in" and only discovered `Permission denied (publickey)` on the first real SSH attempt, then had to find `systems.authorize_ssh_key` on its own. The sibling `systems.ssh_info` already surfaces `authorize_ssh_key` as a next action, making the probe the inconsistent one.

## Change

- Extend the shared `ToolResponse.from_job` builder with an optional keyword-only `extra_next_actions`, appended after the job state's lifecycle actions (default `None` leaves every existing caller and `_common.job_envelope` byte-for-byte unchanged).
- `check_ssh_reachable` passes the RBAC-gated `visible_next_actions(["systems.authorize_ssh_key"], ctx, system.project)` — the same project-scoped filter `ssh_info` uses. A viewer-only caller sees only lifecycle actions; a contributor also sees the authorize pointer.
- The `check_ssh_reachable` wrapper docstring (agent-visible, serialized into the generated tool reference) and the `systems.md` toolset guide state that reachable confirms transport, not authorization.

No migration — pure response-shaping and documentation. ADR-0377.

## Tests

- `from_job` appends `extra_next_actions` after the lifecycle set; omitting the kwarg is unchanged (backward compat).
- `check_ssh_reachable` suggests `authorize_ssh_key` for a contributor and omits it for a viewer-only caller (RBAC gating), lifecycle actions present in both.

`just ci` green locally (lint, format, ty, 8354 tests, doc/guard stages).

author: zorkian
body:
## What changed

- classify low-risk plans for quick layered validation while retaining full validation for medium/high-risk work
- run formatter-write, typecheck, and Vitest related tests for ordinary low-risk code
- promote quick validation to the full suite when the actual patch crosses repository risk boundaries
- use actual changed paths, not advisory planned paths, for automatic publication and merge eligibility
- stop issuing a separate predicted-path digest for new plans while retaining historical schema compatibility

## Why

ADR 0009 makes path predictions advisory and Git commit identity authoritative. This removes expensive full-suite work from ordinary low-risk attempts without weakening repository policy, actual-patch risk classification, or exact-head GitHub CI.

## Impact

Low-risk attempts get faster feedback. Medium/high-risk and policy-sensitive changes still run the full local suite. Required GitHub checks on the published exact head remain authoritative.

body:
Milestone **M11** (`plans/m11-hi-mapping.md`): the "can I make images with the dish?" answer — turn a set of pointed captures into a coarse 2-D **map** of extended emission (galactic HI intensity / peak v_LSR / total power). Honest about the ceiling: the 0.7 m dish is a single **~21° beam**, so these are beam-limited maps of large-scale structure, **not resolved images** — the renderer stamps the resolution on every figure and never fills a cell it didn't observe.

## What's in it
- **Schema `user_version` 14** (`_migration_14_sky_map`): `sky_map` table + `capture.sky_map_id`/`map_az_deg`/`map_el_deg` (additive, guarded).
- **Reduction** (`confirm/mapping.py`, pure numpy): `cell_value` (hi_intensity / peak_vlsr / total_power) + `grid_map` (beam-weighted Gaussian binning; **NaN gaps never interpolated**). `export/figures.py::sky_map_figure` renders the heatmap with a mandatory HPBW circle + resolution caption and hatched unobserved cells.
- **Acquire two ways** (`server/mapping.py`): an **az/el raster runner** (lifespan loop) that slews the grid **only through M9's guarded `slew` primitive** and drives the daemon over the existing control channel — no new device path, **no new mutating MCP verb**, bias-tee untouched; **galactic maps ingest a drift-scan campaign's passes** (no hardware). `next_map_cell` is a pure, tested decision.
- **UI + API**: `/maps` index + `/maps/{id}` detail (heatmap, coverage, metric view toggle, raster start/stop or campaign-ingest) + "Maps" nav; read-only `GET /api/maps[/{id}]` + `/image.png`.
- **MCP (read-only)**: `list_sky_maps` + `get_sky_map` → **23 → 25 tools**.
- **Provenance**: bundle manifest (M8) gains a `sky_maps` block.

## Verification
- `/verify` green: lint, typecheck, `ruff format --check`, coverage **95.5%** (floor 85), and the end-to-end synthetic smoke. New tests: `test_mapping.py`, `test_maps.py`, plus migration/bundle/MCP coverage.
- **No `install.sh`/`OS_IMAGE` change ⇒ no QEMU gate.** The SDR/capture path and bias-tee invariant are untouched.

## Scope notes
- The quantitative rotation-curve fit stays downstream in jansky-research/ezRA; maps are in **relative** units (K-calibration waits on Tsys/flux-cal).
- Per-observation PDF embedding of a (cross-observation) map was deferred in favour of the bundle `sky_maps` provenance + the map's own page/image.

author: venomdrmsupport
body:
## Summary

Integrates native Windows System Tray lifecycle controls on top of Phase 3.
Bare invocation launches the tray; `venom serve` stays console-only. The tray
menu exposes explicit server lifecycle controls with hardened graceful
shutdown, single-instance enforcement, and an Error state for unexpected
server death.

- **Phase 3 base SHA:** `31e4fc29dabb5f3531432b3ae7eb0a6aca9ec6cb` (`codex/phase3-models-offerings-catalog`)
- **Head SHA:** `eb8381c423c996b3fbb814516de45a5319816a0a`
- **Commits over base:** 19

## Tray lifecycle behavior

Final menu contract:

```
Open Dashboard
Status: Running on :8300 / Stopped / Error
────────────
Start Server
Stop Server
Restart Server
────────────
Quit
```

- Initial auto-start on bare invocation; a second live instance is rejected by
  the single-instance lock (dialog + quit, no dead second icon).
- `Open Dashboard` opens `http://localhost:8300` only while Running; never
  implicitly starts the server.
- Start / Stop / Restart run off the UI thread with a `busy` guard so the event
  loop never freezes; unexpected server death flips state to Error and refreshes
  the menu.
- Quit / `ctx.Done()` / SIGINT / SIGTERM / console-close all perform a single
  idempotent graceful shutdown (`sync.Once`), release the port and SQLite
  resources, remove the tray icon, and exit 0. No hard-kill in the normal path.
- `serve` never invokes the tray runner.

## Port 8300 policy

`127.0.0.1:8300` is the only operational runtime bind; dashboard is
`http://localhost:8300`. No `:8200` references remain in runtime, active tests,
scripts, config, or current docs. A regression test asserts the default listen
address and dashboard URL.

## Windows executable icon

`build.ps1` generates a Windows resource (`cmd/venom/rsrc_windows_amd64.syso`,
gitignored) from `internal/tray/assets/icon.ico`, so `venom.exe` shows the Venom
icon in File Explorer/taskbar. Windows-only by filename suffix; no effect on
Linux/CI builds.

## Test counts (local, Windows)

- Web: `bun run typecheck` clean, `bun run test` 48/48 passed, `bun run build` ok.
- Go: `go vet ./...` clean, `gofmt -l cmd internal` clean, `go test ./...` all
  packages pass (incl. `internal/tray`, `internal/cli`, `internal/config`).
- `scripts/build.ps1` exit 0; `git diff --check` clean.

## Canonical binary

- Path: `bin/venom.exe`
- `version` commit: `eb8381c` (matches HEAD)
- SHA256 (worktree build): `7F855B638E1F9D27F6BECA1DF649035819B2620638B1F3705A7765071C32E5A8`
- No `*.exe` / `*.syso` tracked in git.

## Native Windows evidence

- Bare invocation keeps the tray process alive; `127.0.0.1:8300` served by the
  correct PID; `/health/live` and `/health/ready` = 200; dashboard = 200 with
  Phase 3 UI; schema version 3; second instance rejected.
- Stop releases 8300; Start reacquires it and reaches readiness; Restart cycles
  lifecycle without orphan processes.
- Graceful shutdown proven via `CTRL_BREAK_EVENT` (owned process group) for both
  `serve` and bare/tray modes — not hard-kill.
- **Owner manually confirmed** all tray actions (Status, Open Dashboard, Stop,
  Start, Restart, Quit). Post-Quit: 0 `venom` processes, 8300 free, no orphan.

## Clean-checkout evidence

Fresh clone of `eb8381c`; `git submodule update --init --recursive` succeeded
(bifrost ~738 MB) with pin `da4785d44fb135ff7b29d70495002924059c437f` (gitlink ==
checkout); frozen Bun install + web build + `go test ./...` + `build.ps1` all
green; built binary `version` commit `eb8381c`.

## Bifrost submodule

- `.gitmodules` URL: `https://github.com/VENOMDRMSUPPORT/bifrost.git`
- Local URL override removed (falls back to `.gitmodules`); gitlink and checkout
  both pinned at `da4785d44fb135ff7b29d70495002924059c437f` (unchanged).

## Known limitations

- The embedded icon resource (`rsrc`-generated `.syso`) carries a timestamp, so
  `venom.exe` is **not bit-for-bit reproducible** across builds (clean-checkout
  build SHA `ED7CA7F2B984111CA0D72F6AC8D91E08533E0B8BF276FD418775EBDC0E65E458`
  differs from the worktree build), though functionally identical (same commit,
  size, behavior).
- Owner tray confirmation was performed on `cfc1fec`; `eb8381c` adds only the PE
  icon resource (no code/behavior change vs. the confirmed build).

## Test plan

- [ ] Ubuntu full gate
- [ ] Windows full gate
- [ ] Linux race
- [ ] Linux restore
- [ ] Windows restore

Draft — not for merge.

author: elares
body:
Refs #75 (PR A of 3: the connector data plane). Foundational M8 federation work: a declarative, data-only connector model so the provider long tail is configuration, not in-tree code inside the trust boundary. PRs B (generic OIDC upstream) and C (declarative claim mapping) follow.

## What this adds
- A new I/O-free crate `ironauth-connector` with the declarative `ConnectorDefinition` (strict `deny_unknown_fields` + JSON-schema, issuer XOR explicit endpoint set, scopes, PKCE-to-upstream policy, quirks-as-data, a parsed-but-not-yet-evaluated claim mapping) and the `CapabilityMatrix`. Because the crate has NO HTTP dependency, a connector definition structurally cannot perform a raw fetch (the no-raw-fetch guarantee is by construction, enforced by http-audit).
- Two-phase write-time validation: serde rejects unknown keys; `validate()` returns RFC 6901 schema-pointer errors (both/neither endpoint form, non-https issuer, missing openid scope, credential-bearing host all rejected).
- The capability matrix (refresh / groups / logout-propagation / email-verified-trust) with conservative defaults — email-verified-trust defaults to Untrusted — queryable via the management API and covered by a CI schema-stability contract test.
- Per-environment, tenant-isolated (RLS-forced) `connectors` storage. The upstream client secret is envelope-encrypted (#48) INLINE on the connector row under the scope DEK, with the AEAD AAD bound to the immutable connector id + tenant + env + version — the control-plane role is deliberately not granted the shared secret store (that would let it read every scope's TOTP seeds), so inline sealing keeps the secret confined while never plaintext, never in the definition JSON, and never in a config-snapshot export (the #58 covenant, proven by test).
- Zero new third-party dependencies (reuses the JOSE core, schemars, and the Secret type; no url/jsonschema crate). The three PR-B `FetchPurpose` variants are added unused.

## Review (2-lens adversarial, real Postgres)
No HIGH. The inline sealing (AAD-bound, cross-scope-paste-safe, control-plane-confined), the secret-never-in-export guarantee, the fuzzed validator (no panic on adversarial defs), and the no-raw-fetch construction all verified sound. Fixed from review: the connector `update` path sealed the secret's AAD on the mutable request-body slug while `connector_slug` is immutable — now the AAD is bound to the immutable `cnr_` id (create→update→unseal round-trip proven) and a slug change is rejected. Plus a stale doc, a swallowed serialize error, a real enabled toggle, and a userinfo host-confusion reject.

## Deferrals (honest PR-B/C seams)
The generic OIDC upstream (discovery / JWKS cache / ID-token validation / federated login) is PR B; the claim-mapping evaluator + trait type-checking + provisioning is PR C; connector promotion apply and logout propagation are later slices.

Migration 0056 (renumbered from 0055 behind #81's account-recovery). MSRV 1.85, clippy pedantic clean, no new dependencies, all freshness lints green.

author: numnx
body:
## What changed

- Bound Codex rollout parsing to 2 MiB per JSONL record, capped message/tool fields, and the newest 256 conversation groups.
- Serialize full-history Jules telemetry process-wide and deduplicate concurrent reads for the same session.
- Tokenize Jules transcripts and patches in slices of at most 64 KiB, build bounded patch messages without interpolating the full patch, and release raw activities before SQLite reconciliation.
- Add regression tests for oversized Codex records, long rollout histories, Jules synchronization concurrency, tokenizer input bounds, and large patch persistence.
- Document the runtime memory bounds in canonical and published architecture guidance.

## Root cause

The V8 abort was application heap exhaustion, not a kernel OOM kill. Two independent amplification paths were present:

- PR #3166 correctly bound Codex telemetry to the exact native rollout, but exposed an older parser weakness: an incomplete JSONL record and parsed tool payloads had no retained-size bound.
- Live Jules usage sync launched fire-and-forget full-conversation reads for many sessions concurrently, then passed multi-megabyte patches to `js-tiktoken` and constructed a full interpolated patch string before truncation.

The Codex parser weakness was related to the latest PR commits; the Jules synchronization path predated them and was uncovered after the first fix was exercised against the live recovered workload.

## Impact

Large generated assets, command output, and wide hosted-session synchronization no longer multiply into an unbounded server heap spike. Pathological Codex records are omitted from the dashboard transcript, but parsing resumes at the next record and usage/native session identity remain available. Jules usage and message persistence retain their existing contract, with full-history refreshes processed one at a time.

## Validation

- `pnpm run ci` passed
- Full Vitest suite: 9,804 passed, 13 skipped
- Backend coverage thresholds passed
- Focused Codex/Jules memory suites passed
- 514 MiB synthetic oversized-record stream completed under a 128 MiB V8 heap limit; parser recovered the following record and settled at 6 MiB heap
- The compiled runtime replayed recovered orchestration for more than seven minutes under a 512 MiB V8 heap limit; `/ready` remained healthy, JS heap stayed around 170–203 MiB, and RSS stabilized around 0.70–0.75 GiB

## Risk and rollback

Wide Jules batches can delay an individual live transcript refresh while earlier sessions finish, but they no longer run full-history fetches concurrently. Codex usage accounting and session selection remain unchanged. Roll back by reverting this PR; no database migration or persisted-data rewrite is involved.

body:
# feature/rate-limiting

## Descripción
Consolidamos la rama `feature/rate-limiting` aplicando una corrección de prioridad máxima. Durante la sincronización anterior, la rama `develop` quedó en un estado roto e inoperativo (arrojando `ImportError: cannot import name 'limiter' from 'app.extensions'`). Esto ocurrió porque el archivo `__init__.py` fusionado ya invocaba a `limiter.init_app(app)`, pero la instancia del objeto y sus dependencias jamás fueron confirmadas en el historial. 

Con este ciclo de emergencia restauramos la estabilidad del servidor integrando las piezas faltantes de la característica de limitación de tasa (*rate limiting*).

Detalles técnicos que integramos (en 1 commit atómico):
- **Restauración de Arranque (`fix(core)`):** Inyectamos la instancia faltante `limiter = Limiter(...)` dentro de `backend/app/extensions.py`. Esto satisface la importación requerida por el *factory* de la aplicación y erradica el fallo fatal de inicio.
- **Gestión de Dependencias:** Registramos la dependencia necesaria en `backend/requirements.txt` para asegurar que el entorno de despliegue y desarrollo pueda construir y montar la librería correctamente.

### Nota de Auditoría
Debido a la naturaleza crítica de recuperar la operatividad de `develop`, la revisión técnica de este PR se centró exclusivamente en responder "¿esto hace que develop vuelva a arrancar?". La Auditoría Técnica profunda y la actualización exhaustiva de nuestras matrices de control documental (M1, M2, M4) se ejecutarán en frío, inmediatamente después de estabilizar el entorno.

## Tipo de cambio
- [ ] feat
- [x] fix
- [ ] refactor
- [ ] chore
- [ ] docs
- [ ] test

## Cómo probar
1. Tras el merge, actualizamos la rama base localmente: `git checkout develop && git pull origin develop`
2. En la raíz del backend (`cd backend`), activamos el entorno virtual.
3. Instalamos las nuevas dependencias (crucial para que el *rate limiting* funcione):
   `pip install -r requirements.txt`
4. Levantamos el servidor (`flask run` o `python run.py`).
5. Confirmamos que la aplicación arranca de forma limpia sin arrojar el error `ImportError: cannot import name 'limiter'`.
6. Disparamos peticiones a los endpoints previamente limitados (si los hay configurados) para confirmar que la librería intercepta y controla el tráfico exitosamente.

## Checklist
- [x] Sigue las convenciones de commits del proyecto
- [x] El arranque de la aplicación en la rama `develop` fue restaurado con éxito
- [ ] Se agregaron pruebas para el nuevo comportamiento (si aplica)
- [x] La documentación de cierre formal se pospuso explícitamente para priorizar el *hotfix*

author: benlachman
body:
## Summary

Three phases of work to make Dosido produce the highest-quality matches for groups up to 100, working out of the box.

### 1. Solver & scoring core (benchmarked)

- **Removed the dead lookahead loop** in `solve_round`: it solved the current round greedily *first*, then simulated future rounds and discarded them — provably no effect on output, ~6× the compute. Round advance at 100 attendees: **0.63s → 0.12s**, byte-identical match quality (benchmarked across seeds).
- **Solver-chosen pit stop**: odd pools add a zero-weight sentinel node connected to fairness-eligible attendees, so max-weight matching itself picks the sit-out whose absence costs the round least (was: alphabetically-first eligible ID). +0.4% total event score, better worst-person average at n=99.
- **Heuristic 0-100 fallback scoring** (`heuristic_pair_score`) replaces the off-scale `(bonuses)×2` fallback, so walk-ups awaiting backfill and no-API-key events (`LLM_PROVIDER=none`) compete on the same scale as LLM-scored pairs. Walk-up match quality 87.5 → 89.6 on seeded ground truth.
- Fixed `swap_pairing` reading a nonexistent matrix key (every admin swap displayed score 0).

### 2. Out-of-box reliability & event flow

- `advance_round` writes nothing to Redis until the solve succeeds — a solver failure leaves event state untouched and returns a clear 500; admin panel shows inline error alerts on failed actions.
- **Timer expiry now auto-transitions to between-rounds** (new `round_monitor` background task) and broadcasts `status_update`.
- **Open Networking is reachable**: admin button → mutual-match board on the projector (both previously dead code).
- SSE resilience: polling fallback when the connection drops (screen 5s / admin 15s), console error logging, and a "NEXT ROUND STARTING…" interstitial that kills the white flash on round changes.
- Backfill worker guards empty/textless API responses and fenced JSON; pipeline scripts fail with actionable messages naming the command to run first; `.env.example` documents every setting.

### 3. Research-backed matching design

Synthesized from founding-team literature (Wasserman, team-composition studies), practitioner systems (YC Cofounder Matching, Entrepreneur First, First Round's founder-dating playbook), and speed-dating research on stated vs revealed preferences:

- **New registration dimensions** (see `REGISTRATION.md` for the 12-question form): commitment tiers (incl. conditional full-time), runway, ambition scale, equity philosophy, idea flexibility, edge type, decision style, annotated proof links. Similarity-scored where mismatch predicts breakups; complementarity-scored for skills/edge. Skipped questions never penalize.
- **Rewritten pairwise prompt**: similarity-vs-complementarity rubric, dealbreaker caps (full-time × exploring, bootstrap × venture-scale, equal × contribution-based → ≤30), calibration anchors, and pair-specific micro-decision "sparks" with built-in disagreement potential.
- **Signal selectivity weighting**: a signal from someone who signals everyone counts ¼ as much as one from a selective sender.
- Luma CSV ingest for all new questions with tolerant normalizers; seed personas re-curated with realistic values.

## Testing

- Suite grew from 65 → **155 tests**, all passing; ruff clean.

### [`v0.93.0`](https://redirect.github.com/fro-bot/agent/releases/tag/v0.93.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/fro-bot/agent/compare/v0.92.1...v0.93.0)

#### What's new

<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

##### Features

A new `review-skip-label` input (default: `skip-agent-review`) lets repository operators suppress automatic PR-event reviews by applying a label to a pull request. The skip is evaluated at trigger routing — before acknowledgement, model execution, or any token spend — and posts nothing to GitHub when triggered. Setting the input to an empty string disables the feature entirely.

Authorized overrides still win: an `@fro-bot` mention on `opened`, `synchronize`, or `reopened` events (where the validated association belongs to the PR body's own author) or a `review_requested` event naming the bot runs the review regardless of the label. The override authority is deliberately restricted to those actions: on `ready_for_review` and `review_requested`, the router substitutes the webhook sender's association rather than the PR author's, so a body-planted mention there would carry borrowed authorization from whoever triggered the event — that path relies on the trusted reviewer-request override only. Label names are matched case-insensitively from the trusted webhook payload with no routing-time API fetch. [#​1234](https://redirect.github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/1234)

Release-notes narration is now split into two phases with a hard credential boundary. The generation phase runs under the workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN` (`contents: read`, `pull-requests: read`), gathering bounded evidence from PR bodies, files, and diffs (at most 25 PRs, per-PR body truncation, at most 5 diffs) and writing a narrative candidate file to the job's artifact store. Because it operates on a read-only token, it structurally cannot edit the release, comment on PRs, or mutate anything — regardless of what instructions hostile PR content might contain.

author: kishokkumar-a
body:
## What this adds

Pipeline logging & observability: **dynamic, per-agent / per-org log levels** for calls plus an app-wide traceback-logging pass — so an operator can escalate log verbosity for a specific agent or org and have it take effect on the **next call, with no build or restart**.

### Dynamic log levels
- New nullable `log_level` columns on `organizations` and `agents` (NULL = inherit).
- Resolution hierarchy in `core/services/log_level_resolver.py`: **agent > organization > env `LOG_LEVEL` > `INFO`**, returning `(level, source)`; never raises (degrades to the env baseline).
- `core/logging.py` reworked: `setup_logging(level=...)`, `resolve_level()`, `get_applied_level()`, with the trace_id patcher preserved. `run_bot` resolves and applies the per-call level once the agent is known.
- New `GET`/`POST /api/v1/admin/log-level` (guarded by `require_admin_or_owner`, all reads/writes org-scoped) to read the effective level and set/clear it for the caller's org or a specific agent.

### App-wide observability
- Converted many silent or lossy handlers (`except: pass`, `logger.error(..., exc)`) to `logger.exception(...)` with context across services (readiness, MCP, custom tools, email, telephony, pipeline, RAG, warm/subprocess workers, etc.).
- Added error backstops so no call dies without a traceback: outer handler in `bot()`, wrapped telephony transport build, `/twiml` + `/telnyx/texml` return a hangup TwiML on failure, and the pipeline runner marks the call failed (`fail_call`) on a mid-call crash.

### Migrations
- `e1f2a3b4c5d6` — add `log_level` to `organizations` and `agents` (nullable, safe on live tables, reversible).
- `c3e5a7b9d1f4` — no-op **heads-merge** revision unifying this branch's migration with `staging`'s call-metrics series-stats head after the merge below.

### Docs & tests
- `docs/LOGGING_OBSERVABILITY.md` (operator guide) and the code-review rulebook under `docs/code-review/` (+ CLAUDE.md pointer).
- `test-cases/test_logging_level.py` — normalization, baseline resolution, the DB hierarchy, the transient-agent DB-safety guard, and `setup_logging`.

### Also merged
- Current `origin/staging` is merged into this branch (call-metrics series stats, consolidated transcript, post-call actions, related frontend call-history components).

## Notes for reviewers
- Base is **`dev`** per team workflow (the `dev → staging` promotion is a separate rebase-and-merge PR). Because `dev` is behind `staging`, the diff also shows the staging lead over dev.
- Known follow-up (not blocking): in the default in-process `/ws` path, `setup_logging` mutates the process-global loguru sink, so a per-call level override can affect concurrently-running calls until re-resolved. A contextual/bound-level approach would isolate per call — happy to address in a follow-up.

Fecha o pedido do Diego sobre o Monte da carreira.

Já estava certo: carta própria recuperada é **de graça**, o jogador **perde valor** (cai pra metade — Vini de 30 vira 15 de piso) e **outros pagam a metade** (não de graça). Faltava a **prioridade**:

- Cada técnico (humano/rival) tem **prioridade** pra recuperar os jogadores que **ele** listou e caíram no monte. Enquanto o dono ainda tem vaga, a carta fica **reservada pra ele** — de graça (já valendo a metade).
- Os **outros** só conseguem pegar aquela carta **depois** que o dono encher o time, e aí **pagando a metade**.
- Carta de **bot do mercado** não tem reserva (bot não pesca no monte).

Detalhes:
- `monteLocked` / `montePickable`: reservam a carta pro vendedor enquanto ele tem buracos; usados no auto-pick, no skip e na validação do MONTE_PICK.
- A tela do Monte **esconde** o que está reservado pro dono e mostra o selo **🫵 seu · recupere grátis · vale X** nas suas cartas listadas.

body:
Stability pass over `src/noesis/`: two waves of parallel reviewers, every finding re-traced against source, four fixes shipped with a regression test each.

**Two of the four findings were wrong as originally diagnosed.** Both were falsified with throwaway probes against the installed libraries *before* any code changed. Both original claims cited real dependency source and still described paths this code never takes — that's the interesting part, and it's why the diff below isn't what the plan said it would be.

## What changed

### B1 — NaN rerank score emitted invalid JSON on MCP (`core/retriever.py`)
The 2026-07-11 hunt fixed the rerank *sort key* (NaN → -inf) but left the raw score on the returned hit.

Originally diagnosed as: Starlette's `allow_nan=False` → 500 on `POST /search`. **That path is never reached.** `/search` is annotated `-> dict[str, Any]`, so FastAPI serializes through Pydantic, which maps NaN to `null` by default. REST was never affected.

The real bug is on **MCP — the primary surface** (`CLAUDE.md`: "MCP primary, REST secondary"). It emitted a bare `NaN` token, which [RFC 8259](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8259#section-6) does not permit, so a strict client parser rejects the **entire search result**, not just that field. Nulled in `core/retriever.py` — the boundary both adapters share.

NaN sorts last, so it only surfaces once the NaN hit is inside the returned slice (`top_k` >= hit count).

### D1 — `delete_project` orphaned points of an in-flight run (ADR-47, ADR-48)
Deleting a project mid-index cancelled the run, then wiped its points. But asyncio delivers `CancelledError` at an `await asyncio.to_thread(...)` **immediately, while the worker thread runs on** — so the abandoned upsert landed *after* the wipe, orphaning points under a dead `project_id` that no prune path reclaims (all are scoped to live projects).

**The originally proposed fix — cancel, then `await gather(task)` — is a no-op against this.** Verified: after the await returned, the thread had not yet written; its write landed afterwards.

Fixed in two halves that only work together (documented in-code so neither gets removed alone):
1. `execute_run` shields its upsert and waits out the in-flight write on cancel. Cancellation still aborts the run at the same point; ADR-41 per-file containment is untouched (`CancelledError` is a `BaseException`, so `except Exception` never sees it). Costs one file's upsert, not the whole run.
2. `delete_project` is now async and awaits the cancelled task.

Plus `runtime.py` sweeps orphans at startup — the backstop for what no wipe can prevent (a `kill -9` mid-run).

> ⚠️ **The sweep refuses to run on an empty project table.** An empty table is indistinguishable from a state DB resolved to the wrong path — exactly the bug ADR-44 fixed — and this operation is destructive: there, "no live projects" would read as "delete the entire collection". A skipped sweep costs a few dead points until a project exists; a wrong sweep costs the whole index.

Impact was storage-only: `project_id` is `uuid4`, so a re-registered folder gets a fresh id and can never read stale points.

### D2 — CSRF gap on JSON-body dashboard mutations (`api/dashboard.py`)
`verify_local_origin` guarded only the two reindex POSTs. But FastAPI parses a POST with **no `Content-Type` header** as JSON, and a cross-site no-cors `fetch` with an untyped `Blob` body sends exactly that — no CORS preflight. So every JSON-body dashboard mutation was drivable from a hostile page open in a browser on this machine. Worst case: register + index an arbitrary local directory (`index_now=true`).

No data exfiltration (no CORS read-back; local-only per ADR-25). The guard now covers all five remaining mutating routes, including `DELETE`. Same-origin dashboard JS and header-less clients (curl, agents) are unaffected by design.

### B2 — blank search queries rejected (`api/routes.py`, `mcp/server.py`)
`min_length=1` alone still admits whitespace, which costs the same wasted work (empty BM25 document, dense embed of nothing). Rejected via a `field_validator` on `SearchRequest` and an explicit check in the MCP tool.

## Rejected during verification
Recorded so they aren't re-litigated: `watcher.py` `_pruned_scandir` leak (refcounting closes it immediately on CPython); `upsert_chunks` batch guard (called per-file, capped by `max_file_bytes` — never near Qdrant's limit); startup resource leak on `build_runtime_context` raise (process exits, OS reclaims); blocking `QdrantClient` in the async lifespan (nothing is served until startup completes).

## Verification
- **310 passed**, 0 failed. Guardrail greps clean (no `sentence_transformers` outside the two model boundaries, no `0.0.0.0`, no outbound HTTP in `core/`).
- **Every regression test was run against the unfixed code and observed to fail for its stated reason.** This caught one of my own tests passing for the wrong reason: the D1 test asserted immediately after the delete, *before* the racing write could land, and so proved nothing. It now waits on a real completion signal and fails with `1 orphaned point(s) survived the delete` without the fix.
- ADR-47 and ADR-48 recorded (devlog + decision log, per hard rule 6). Three lessons captured (rule 7).

## Notes for the reviewer
- **Line endings:** the working tree carries pre-existing CRLF churn (~104 files, content identical to HEAD). Files touched here were normalized to LF to match HEAD, so this diff shows only real changes. No unrelated files are included.
- **Pre-existing flake, not from this branch:** `test_register_index_search_roundtrip` has a 5s `_wait_done` timeout and fails on a cold fastembed cache when the model download pushes a run to ~9s. Worth raising to ~15s if it bites CI.

### Motivation

A Detailed Planning Pack is proposal-specific evidence. Before this slice, changing the proposed-works brief could leave a current-site pack driving SEE or expert-review readiness for the wrong proposal.

### Description

- Treat the normalized proposed-works brief as part of active DPP scope in the normal workspace.
- Select the newest current-site DPP matching the current proposal, while retaining different-proposal packs as history.
- Show a regeneration warning and fail closed when current-site packs exist but none matches the current proposal.
- Bind normal SEE and expert-review writes to the selected DPP artefact ID plus expected proposal brief.
- At the server boundary, resolve that exact owned DPP, verify current-site cited-QSC provenance and normalized proposal equality, and reject malformed, forged, stale, cross-project, mismatched, or unresolved-for-SEE inputs before persistence.
- Preserve honest expert-review referral from an explicitly selected unresolved pack.
- Retain the previous newest-current resolver only when both binding fields are omitted, documented as a legacy compatibility path.
- Reconcile Item 60 as merged and record Item 61 plus DR-030.

- Fixed explicit lookup so it collects every DPP candidate while preserving the newest valid pack as the legacy active candidate. This allows an older proposal-matching pack to be selected when a newer valid pack belongs to another proposal.
- Fixed the workspace mismatch state so a newer different-proposal history item does not produce a false warning or block review when an older matching pack is active.

body:
## Summary

Fixes the saved-search save-to-navigation race reported in #2644.

The create flow now performs a document navigation to the new saved-search
route rather than a client-side transition that can be overwritten by stale
`useQueryStates` URL state. The E2E helper waits for `domcontentloaded` so it
asserts the destination route without coupling the test to unrelated resource
loading after that document navigation.

## Root cause

`router.push` allowed the prior search page's URL state to be restored during
the transition, intermittently replacing the new `/search/<id>` route.

## Validation

- `yarn lint:fix`
- repository lint/type gate
- commit hooks (Prettier, ESLint, Knip)
- captured E2E trace reaches the new saved-search URL

The focused full-stack E2E runner is currently blocked before its test by an
existing global setup timeout waiting for `page.goto('/search')` to emit
`load`; this is unrelated to the saved-search route behavior.

### jackson-databind has case-insensitive deserialization bypasses per-property @​JsonIgnoreProperties
[CVE-2026-54515](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-54515) / [GHSA-5jmj-h7xm-6q6v](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-5jmj-h7xm-6q6v)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary
In `BeanDeserializerBase.createContextual()`, per-property `@JsonIgnoreProperties` exclusions are applied by `_handleByNameInclusion()`, producing a `contextual` deserializer whose `BeanPropertyMap` has the ignored properties removed. The subsequent per-property case-insensitivity block (triggered by `@JsonFormat(ACCEPT_CASE_INSENSITIVE_PROPERTIES)`) rebuilds from `this._beanProperties` (the original, unfiltered map) instead of `contextual._beanProperties`, then overwrites the filtered map — restoring every property `_handleByNameInclusion` had just removed. The ignored property becomes writable again.

##### Impact
An application that both enables case-insensitive matching and relies on per-property `@JsonIgnoreProperties` to keep a field unwritable can have that field set from untrusted JSON (mass-assignment-style write).

##### Affected / Patched
Will be fixed in 2.18.9, 2.21.5, 2.22.1 and 3.1.4.

##### Severity / CWE
Maintainer: minor. Reporter: Moderate. CWE-915.

##### Upstream fix
FasterXML/jackson-databind#5962 (PR #​5964, `0e1b0b2`), milestone 3.1.4. Released 2026-06-04.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 5.3 / 10 (Medium)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N`

This data is provided by the [GitHub Advisory Database](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-5jmj-h7xm-6q6v) ([CC-BY 4.0](https://redirect.github.com/github/advisory-database/blob/main/LICENSE.md)).
</details>

---

### jackson-databind: @​JsonView bypassed for @​JsonUnwrapped container properties on deserialization
[CVE-2026-59889](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-59889) / [GHSA-5gvw-p9qm-jgwh](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-5gvw-p9qm-jgwh)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary
`UnwrappedPropertyHandler.processUnwrapped()` replays the buffered JSON for a `@JsonUnwrapped` property by iterating its properties and calling `prop.deserializeAndSet()` with **no `prop.visibleInView(ctxt.getActiveView())` guard** — the exact guard `processUnwrappedCreatorProperties()` received in the #​5971 / GHSA-rcqc-6cw3-h962 fix, and the guard `BeanDeserializer.deserializeWithUnwrapped` applies to directly-matched properties. As a result, a property annotated with both `@JsonView(PrivilegedView.class)` and `@JsonUnwrapped` is written from attacker JSON even when deserializing under a more-restrictive active view.

**Correction to the original framing (runtime-verified):** the gap is NOT a per-field inner `@JsonView` (the unwrapped sub-object's own `BeanDeserializer` gates inner fields correctly). The unchecked gate is the **view of the unwrapped CONTAINER property**.

##### Intent proof (runtime, 2.x HEAD 21dd70dd and 3.x HEAD 7a5939d6)
An `@JsonView(AdminView)` property that is NOT `@JsonUnwrapped` → `null` under `PublicView` (correctly gated). The identical property WITH `@JsonUnwrapped` → fully populated (bypass). The fix the creator path already received, not applied to the regular-property method.

##### Impact — write-side mass-assignment / privilege escalation
`@JsonView` is commonly used as a write-side authorization guard: a public endpoint binds the body under `readerWithView(PublicView.class)` and groups privileged state in a nested object whose container property is `@JsonView(AdminView)`. When that property is `@JsonUnwrapped`, an untrusted caller mass-assigns it. PoC: a self-service registration where `AccountFlags{role,approved,creditBalance}` is `@JsonView(AdminView) @JsonUnwrapped`; attacker JSON `{role:ADMIN,approved:true,creditBalance:1000000}` under `PublicView` binds all three → approved admin with arbitrary balance. The failing gate is a WRITE gate, hence integrity-high (`C:N/I:H/A:N`); no worse than the C:L/I:L parent and arguably higher as `@JsonView`-as-write-guard is the exact use case #​5971/#​5969 defended.

##### Affected
- `com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind` 2.x: confirmed bypass at 21dd70dd (== released 2.21.4 / 2.22.0 line; includes the #​5973 backport). `DEFAULT_VIEW_INCLUSION` default=true.
- `tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind` 3.x: confirmed bypass at HEAD 7a5939d6 (latest 3.x). `DEFAULT_VIEW_INCLUSION` default=false → the stock-config repro is the common shape where privileged inner fields are individually `@JsonView(PublicView)` and the developer relies on the container `@JsonView(AdminView)`; the 3.x PoC mass-assigns role/approved/creditBalance under PublicView. (The other simultaneous report's PoC was reportedly fixed on 3.x; this distinct container-property path is not.)

##### Additive variants (runtime-confirmed both branches; all closed by the same one-line guard)
- nested `@JsonUnwrapped` (unwrapped-in-unwrapped) — recursive bypass.
- merge / `readerWithView(...).withValueToUpdate(...)` (PATCH/partial-update) — bypass; non-unwrapped merge control gates correctly.
- builder-based deserializer (`@JsonDeserialize(builder=...)`) — `BuilderBasedDeserializer` routes through the same `processUnwrapped`.
- Honest non-findings: read-side serialization correctly honors views (no leak); `@JsonAnySetter`+view and `@JsonTypeInfo`+`@JsonUnwrapped` are separate/unsupported behaviors, not this bug.

##### Fix
Add `prop.visibleInView(ctxt.getActiveView())` (when `MapperFeature.DEFAULT_VIEW_INCLUSION`/active-view applies) to the `processUnwrapped()` property loop, mirroring `processUnwrappedCreatorProperties()`. One change closes the impact PoC + all three variants across `BeanDeserializer` and `BuilderBasedDeserializer`. Full runnable PoCs (2.x + 3.x) + variant harnesses available on request.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 6.5 / 10 (Medium)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N`
