author: agentydragon
body:
Closes out the seatphysical-login saga with a direction decision.

## Decision

The physical monitor and a remote console are **never needed at the same time** (confirmed with the owner), so the entire multi-seat design — and with it GDM's unfixable non-seat0 user-login blocker (gdm!291 / systemd#42247) — is unnecessary.

**Standing direction:** make the display 5090 the sole `seat0` graphical output. That's a normal, fully-supported GDM `seat0` login, so the physical seat "just works". Reach the desktop remotely via a **session, not a seat** — gnome-remote-desktop (incl. headless remote-login) or the **Sunshine** host already configured on wyrm2. SPICE is demoted to a Proxmox recovery console.

This **retires the whole DM search**: no PLM, no MR 155 backport, no carried patch.

## Doc changes

- New **DIRECTION CHANGE** block at the top of the decision section (the leading, standing resolution).
- "Path forward" bullet flipped from *not yet chosen* → **CHOSEN**; PLM + MR155 demoted to a shelved fallback (only if two *simultaneous local* seats ever become a real requirement); greetd remains source-verified out.

## Not done here

The actual `wyrm2.nix` change (drop `seatphysical`/`seatspare` udev rules, `mutter-device-ignore` the virtio-gpu + spare 5090, wire remote access) is **deliberately not in this PR** — this records the decision; the config change comes when the owner wants to execute it.

## Testing

Docs-only decision record; no Bazel target covers it.

﻿## Problem

When Treemon creates a new worktree, it forks a new branch from a base ref with `git worktree add -b {name} {baseRef}`. When `baseRef` is a remote-tracking ref like `origin/feature`, git's default `autoSetupMerge` makes the new branch **inherit the base branch's upstream** (`@{u}` points at `origin/feature`).

Treemon keys PR detection off `@{u}`, so the freshly forked worktree would incorrectly show the *base* branch's PR until the new branch was first pushed.

## Fix

Pass `--no-track` to `git worktree add` in `resolveWorktreeCommand` (`src/Server/GitWorktree.fs`). This disables `autoSetupMerge` for the fork, so the new branch starts with **no upstream** — which is correct, since a freshly forked branch has no remote of its own yet. PR detection then reports nothing for the new worktree until it is actually pushed.

## Changes

- `src/Server/GitWorktree.fs` — add `--no-track` to the `worktree add` command; document why on `resolveWorktreeCommand`.
- `src/Tests/CreateWorktreeServerTests.fs` — new test asserting the fork command contains `--no-track`.
- `docs/spec/worktree-monitor.md` — update the fork spec to reflect `--no-track` and the PR-detection rationale.

## Tests

- Added `forks with --no-track so the new branch does not inherit the base upstream` to `ResolveWorktreeCommandTests`.

No Docker setup existed for the project. This adds a full containerized environment covering all runtime components.

  | `redis` | `redis:7-alpine` | Broker + result backend; health-checked |
  | `backend` | built | Runs `migrate` then `gunicorn`; do not scale >1 without extracting migrations to a separate job |
  | `celery` | built | `celery -A config worker` |

```

body: ## Summary Delivers a complete, clickable prototype of `actual-truelayer-manager` covering spec phases 2–8, on top of the Phase 0/1 foundation. > Note: this branch stacks on the Phase 1 branch (PR #2), so this PR also contains the encryption/redaction commit. Merging this PR effectively includes Phase 1. ## Walkthrough [full_prototype_walkthrough.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-f2d9ae52-fb38-4fd6-9481-e502c0a2f7ea/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Ffull_prototype_walkthrough.mp4) End-to-end in demo mode: setup wizard → save Actual + TrueLayer config → connect demo bank → map accounts → dry-run → live sync → logs. Tokens stored encrypted (AES-256-GCM). - **Phase 4 — Provider abstraction** (`BankingProvider`, spec §7): live `TrueLayerProvider` (OAuth + Data API via native `fetch`) and a built-in `DemoProvider`; manual redirect-URL parser (spec §15.2). - **Phase 3 — Actual client** (spec §14): `ActualClient` interface with a lazy `@actual-app/api`-backed `RealActualClient` and an in-memory `DemoActualClient`. - **Phase 6 — Sync engine** (spec §13): dry-run and live sync, normalisation with deterministic fallback IDs, duplicate detection via `imported_transactions`, overlap window, and full `sync_runs`/`sync_run_items` recording. - **Phase 7 — Scheduler + management UI**: interval scheduler; server-rendered dashboard, connections, mappings, and redacted logs pages. - **Phase 5 — Setup wizard**: 7-step guided flow (Actual → TrueLayer → connect bank → discover accounts → map → dry-run → schedule). - **Phase 8 — Legacy import detection** for the two upstream projects (spec §18), read-only. ### Demo mode When no live credentials are configured (or `DEMO_MODE=1`), the app uses a simulated bank + in-memory Actual budget so the entire flow is runnable without external services. An ephemeral encryption key is auto-created under the data dir in demo mode. ## Testing - ✅ `npm run typecheck` - ✅ `npm run lint` - ✅ `npm test` (45/45 across 8 files) - ✅ `npm run build` - ✅ End-to-end flow (browser + HTTP): connect demo bank (3 accounts) → map → dry-run (fetched 14, would import 14) → live sync (imported 14) → **second live sync imported 0, 6 duplicates** (dedupe via overlap window works). body:
## Summary

Deduplicates the experimental NestDrop collection against the mainline lazy-loaded presets and applies a supplied curation list, shrinking `src/presets-extra/` from ~276 MB to **~190 MB** and the shipped preset count from 56,720 to **37,743**.

- **Main dedupe (15,739 `[EXP]` presets removed):** the EXP import re-converted the same source `.milk` presets the mainline collection already ships. 4,637 were byte-identical to mainline at import time (per manifest canonical hashes; later EXP-side normalization drifted the live bytes) and 11,102 are approved normalized-name matches. The mainline copy survives in every case. All removals went through `tools/remove-experimental-duplicates.py` from a `compare-experimental-presets.py` report filtered to live names, so index, chunks, inventory, removal ledger, manifest, and `experimental-exclusions.json` changed in lockstep.
- **Intra-EXP dedupe (247 removed):** exact byte-duplicate EXP presets under different names; the lexicographically first name per content hash is kept.
- **Stale index prune (38 removed):** index entries whose preset data was missing from their chunk files (leftover from an old partial removal); these surfaced as unavailable presets at runtime.
- **Supplied curation list (2,991 removed):** applied via `tools/remove_presets.js` (2,168 EXP, 823 mainline). The list's other 580 names were already removed earlier in this branch's dedupe pass, confirmed against the removal ledger.
- **Inventory reconciliation:** new `tools/reconcile_preset_inventory.py` (idempotent, stdlib-only) restored 2,046 inventory rows for presets that ship in the chunks but were missing from `preset-inventory.csv`; the inventory now matches the live index exactly (37,369 presets-extra rows + 374 vendored).
- README counts updated to the reconciled totals; CHANGELOG entries added. No chunk repacking: the 377 physical EXP files and all logical chunk IDs are unchanged, preserving the `window.__bcPresetChunk(logicalId, ...)` invariant.

## Verification

- Full consistency sweep after each pass: every index name present in its chunk file, no orphan chunk keys, zero remaining EXP/mainline name matches, zero duplicate canonical hashes within EXP, inventory rows == live presets.
- Re-running the compare report post-removal shows 0 live removal-eligible presets; `reconcile_preset_inventory.py --dry-run` reports nothing to do.
- `eslint` and `ruff` pass; `node tools/validate-experimental-presets.js` reports 0 invalid presets.
- Browser check (Chromium via Playwright against `npx serve src`): `obs.html` loads with zero console errors, the index exposes every shipped name, and both a mainline chunk (`chunk-000.js`) and an EXP chunk (`chunk-9000.js`) load through the real script-injection path with all index names present.

author: narasimha-sc
body:
**Problem:** connecting via a deleted or already-used link shows "Connection error (AUTH)" and suggests it "might be a bug - please report it", which confuses new users and invites bug reports for expected behavior.

**Cause:** AUTH from the server on connect means the link's queue no longer exists — the contact removed the link, or a one-time link was already used — but the message hedges instead of saying so.

**Fix:** replace the alert on iOS, Android and desktop with "Connection link removed" and a definitive explanation with a clear next step (ask the contact for a new link); string values only, translation keys unchanged.

`EpisodeDao.insert` は `OnConflictStrategy.REPLACE` を使用しているため、購読時 (`subscribeToPodcast`) やエピソード更新時 (`saveEpisodes` / 詳細画面のpull-to-refresh) にAPI由来のデータで全カラムが上書きされ、ローカルでのみ更新されるカラムがデフォルト値にリセットされていました。

- `lastPlaybackPosition` → 0にリセットされ、InProgress画面の表示条件 (`lastPlaybackPosition > 0`) から外れて消える
- `isDownloaded` / `localFilePath` / `downloadedAt` → ダウンロード済み状態も同時に消失(副次バグ)

再生中はアプリプロセスが生きている限り5秒ごとの定期保存で再生位置が書き戻されるため上書きが自己修復されますが、バックグラウンド再生中にプロセスキルされると書き戻しが止まり、その後のリフレッシュで位置0が確定して恒久的に消えていました。

## 変更内容
- `PodcastRepository` にエピソードのupsert処理を集約 (`upsertEpisode`) し、insert前に既存レコードからローカル状態 (`lastPlaybackPosition`・`listened`・ダウンロード系カラム) をマージするように変更
- 回帰テストを2件追加
  - `saveEpisodes_preservesLocalStateOfExistingEpisodes`
  - `subscribeToPodcast_preservesLocalStateOfExistingEpisodes`

- `./gradlew :composeApp:testAndroidHostTest` ✔
- `./gradlew spotlessCheck detekt` ✔

author: prajwal-144
body:
## Summary

Adds Stage D/E on top of the current fixed-SIS + FITS-PSF pipeline without modifying `train.py`.

### New files
- `physics_losses.py`: fixed-SIS magnification map, source-plane information map, differentiable soft magnification-adaptive source grid, `L_mu`, and source-plane intensity consistency `L_src-cons`.
- `train_mag.py`: standalone training entrypoint using the existing sparse SIS forward/backward mappings and FITS PSF.
- `test_physics_losses.py`: focused tests for magnification clipping, information mapping, constant surface-brightness preservation, adaptive-grid limits, and contributor consistency.
- `evaluate_mag.ipynb`: evaluates loss curves, magnification/information maps, LR residuals, adaptive source structure, and source-consistency diagnostics.
- `STAGE_D_E_FIXED_SIS.md`: physics, implementation details, commands, ablations, and run order.

## Physics conventions
- Lensing conserves surface brightness; magnification is never used as an intensity multiplier.
- For the centered fixed SIS, `mu = 1 / (1 - theta_E/r)`, clipped only for stable weighting near the critical curve.
- The source information score controls a soft fine/medium/coarse grid blend.
- `L_mu` suppresses unsupported high-frequency source structure primarily in low-information regions.
- `L_src-cons` is evaluated on the pre-PSF image. It combines agreement between the source and the back-projected image-plane mean with variance among effective multiple-image contributors.

## Validation performed
- `python -m py_compile physics_losses.py train_mag.py test_physics_losses.py`
- `pytest -q test_physics_losses.py`
- Result: 5 tests passed locally.

## Important constraint
`--theta-e` must match the SIS Einstein radius encoded in the existing sparse mapping tensors. This PR intentionally does not introduce learnable SIS/SIE/shear yet.

author: skjjcruz
body:
The League Teams cards rendered fine in Chromium but collapsed on top of each other on the owner's iPad.

**Root cause:** the card was a `<button>` with block-level rows (name, team, pts, needs, has, archetype) inside. Safari/WebKit renders a `<button>`'s children in an internal box that doesn't expand for block children, so the rows mashed together. The rest of the app already uses `<div role="button">` for clickable cards for exactly this reason — the League Teams card was the odd one out.

**Fix:**
- Card is now a `<div role="button" tabIndex={0}>` with `onKeyDown` (Enter/Space) for keyboard access — same tap → Owner DNA behavior.
- Hardened `.tc-lt-card` with `display: block; flex-shrink: 0;` so a card can never be compressed inside the flex-column scroller.

Reproduced the original clean-in-Chromium / measured-correct layout headless, and confirmed the div version renders the cards properly spaced. (WebKit isn't installable in CI here, but the button-content-box behavior is well-documented and matches the symptom exactly.)

Verified: eslint clean, JSX parses, 120/120 tests pass.

body:
## Summary

Adds a new `ensure-emulator-running` sequence/command action (feature **070**) that verifies the target **LDPlayer** emulator instance is running **and responsive** (not hanging) before automation runs, and starts a stopped instance or restarts a hung one, waiting for boot-complete before the step succeeds. It is the emulator-lifecycle sibling of the app-lifecycle `ensure-game-running`.

- **Health** = `ldconsole isrunning` + `adb devices` state `device` + `sys.boot_completed=1` (bounded probe).
- **Remediation**: not running → `ldconsole launch`; hung → `ldconsole reboot`; then poll to boot-complete up to a configurable max wait.
- **Parameterized** by instance name/index + `adbSerial` (like `connect-to-game`).
- **Graceful degradation**: non-Windows host, or ldconsole/ADB unavailable → neutral no-op; nonexistent instance or recovery timeout → step failure.

## How it's built

- New emulator-control surface: `LdConsoleClient` + `LdConsoleResolver` in `GameBot.Emulator` (mirroring `AdbClient`/`AdbResolver`), fronted by fakeable `IEmulatorControl` / `IEmulatorDeviceProbe` seams and orchestrated by `EnsureEmulatorRunningActionHandler`.
- Wired through the same surfaces as `ensure-game-running`: action-type consts, `PrimitiveActionTypes.All`, validation, `FileSequenceRepository` payload set, `SequenceRunner` dispatch gate, `SequenceExecutionService` + `CommandExecutor` dispatch, command DTO/enum + endpoint mapping, MCP tool description, and web-ui (selector + new `EnsureEmulatorRunningPanel` + `CommandForm`).
- Config knobs `GAMEBOT_EMULATOR_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS` (10s), `GAMEBOT_EMULATOR_BOOT_WAIT_MS` (120s), `GAMEBOT_EMULATOR_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` (3s), `GAMEBOT_LDCONSOLE_PATH` — startup-bound + runtime-mutable, documented in `ENVIRONMENT.md`.

## Testing

- Backend: `dotnet build` clean; **654** unit + **92** contract + **288** integration tests pass. New coverage: handler outcome matrix (incl. FR-015 device-only assertion), args/validation, ldconsole parsing + resolver, dispatch mapping, repo acceptance, and a real-adapter graceful-degradation integration test.
- Web-ui: `vite build` + **558** jest tests pass (new panel + selector tests).
- CI (.NET CI): build/coverage/perf gates + web-ui-tests all green.

## Spec

Design artifacts under [`specs/070-ensure-emulator-running/`](specs/070-ensure-emulator-running) (spec, plan, research, data-model, contracts, tasks). `docs/architecture.md` and `specs/STATUS.md` updated.

author: neoxelox
body:
Three QA improvements to the experiment creation flow and comparison table.

## Filters open on the first post-creation redirect

When you land on an experiment's detail page straight after creating or importing one, every variant's filter section now starts expanded, so the filters a preset seeded are visible instead of hidden behind a collapsed summary. On any later visit (or a refresh) filters default to collapsed as before.

The create/import redirects (`ExperimentCreateModal`, "Create experiment from search", and "Compare this search" on save) navigate with a `created` search param. The detail page captures it at mount into the initial `expanded` state passed down to each `FilterBuilder`, then strips the param from the URL so it only fires once. `FilterBuilder` gained an optional `initialExpanded` prop (default `false`), so every other usage is unchanged.

## Preset seeds name and description

In the create modal, clicking a non-`custom` preset fills the name and description from the preset's own label and description. It only fills a field the user hasn't typed into — a value we auto-filled can still be replaced by a later preset pick, but text the user entered is never overwritten, and `custom` fills nothing.

## Metric tooltips + public API descriptions

Every metric in the collapsible entity groups now has a one-sentence tooltip on its label (the label only, not the whole cell) explaining what it measures. The four headline summary panels are untouched.

The tooltip text comes from a new required `description` on each `EXPERIMENT_METRICS` entry, written from the actual ClickHouse computations in `variant-metrics-repository.ts`. The same description is wired into the public API metric schemas (`metricDescription` in the OpenAPI experiment entity), so it propagates to `openapi.json`, `mcp.json`, and the generated TS/Python SDKs and CLI — all regenerated in this PR.

Generated-file changes are description-only (no new API surface), so SDK/CLI publish versions are intentionally not bumped; the generated sources are committed only to keep the `api-manifests.yml` drift check green.

## Validation

- `typecheck` clean for `@domain/experiments`, `@repo/operations`, `@app/web`; Biome clean on hand-edited files.
- `openapi:emit` / `mcp:emit` confirmed idempotent (no drift).

Includes UI changes to the experiment detail page and create modal — worth attaching a screen recording of the create → redirect flow for reviewer context.

## Summary

Closes #340

Implements the Go SDK client library described in issue #340, covering the same REST surface as the Python SDK (`packages/ledgerlens-sdk`) and TypeScript SDK (`sdk/`).

---

## Changes

### New: `go/` module (`github.com/Ledger-Lenz/Ledgerlens-core/go`)

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `go.mod` / `go.sum` | Module declaration, Go 1.22, single test dependency (testify) |
| `models.go` | `RiskScore`, `WalletScoresResponse`, `Ring`, `ShapContribution`, `WebhookSubscriber` and request/response types — json tags match wire field names exactly; includes v2 conformal prediction fields (`score_lower`, `score_upper`, `prediction_set`, `coverage_guarantee`) |
| `errors.go` | `LedgerLensAPIError` wrapping HTTP status, detail body, and `RetryAfter` (parsed from Retry-After header on 429s) |
| `options.go` | `WithAPIKey`, `WithHTTPClient`, `WithTimeout`, `WithInsecureSkipVerify` (test-only, clearly named) |
| `client.go` | `Client` with context-aware `GetScore`, `GetScores`, `GetRings`, `Health`, `RegisterWebhook`, `ListWebhooks`, `DeleteWebhook`, `ExplainScore`; `String()`/`GoString()` redact the API key |
| `webhook.go` | `VerifyWebhookSignature` (constant-time `hmac.Equal`, mirrors Python `hmac.compare_digest`) and `VerifyWebhookTimestamp` with `DefaultWebhookMaxAge = 5*time.Minute` |
| `client_test.go` | 12 tests: `httptest.Server`-backed happy paths, 401/404/429+Retry-After error mapping, context cancellation propagation, API key redaction, conformal fields round-trip |
| `webhook_test.go` | 15 tests + 1 Example: valid/wrong-secret/tampered-body/wrong-prefix/empty, all timestamp boundary conditions, cross-check verifying Go HMAC output matches Python scheme |
| `README.md` | Installation, quick-start, withdrawal-gating example, options table, method reference, error-handling snippet, full struct reference, security notes |

### Updated files

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `go-sdk` CI job: `go vet ./...` + `go test ./... -race -count=1`
- `docs/webhook_security_model.md` — cross-links Go `VerifyWebhookSignature`/`VerifyWebhookTimestamp` helpers alongside the existing Python reference

---

## Security

- `VerifyWebhookSignature` uses `hmac.Equal` (constant-time). Never `==` or `bytes.Equal`.
- `VerifyWebhookTimestamp` rejects future timestamps (delta < 0) in addition to stale ones.
- API key is never included in `String()`, `GoString()`, or error messages.
- TLS verification is enabled by default; `WithInsecureSkipVerify` is provided only for local test servers.

---

## Testing

```
go test ./... -race -count=1   # 27/27 pass
go vet ./...                   # clean
```

---

## Cross-repo contract

Struct field names/casing/units match `detection/risk_score.py`, `packages/ledgerlens-sdk/src/ledgerlens/models.py`, and `sdk/src/schemas.ts` per the README's Conventions for AI Agents rule. The Go module does not import from the core detection engine — it mirrors the schema independently, the same discipline followed by the Python and TypeScript SDKs.

author: matt-cochran
body:
## Tier 2 — structural findings (god-file decomposition)

Second slice of the StructureOS findings-cleanup campaign (sub-project A). Builds on the Tier-1 go/no-go slice (#2). Adds the **structural burn-down loop** that routes god-file findings (SOS001) through the referenced `flow.refactor.god-file` decomposition flow under a **per-target human gate** and a **budget cap**.

### What's in it
- **`flow.findings.structural`** — Tier-2 budgeted dispatcher: `scanning → extracting → picking → {done | paused | refactoring → counting → scanning}`. Stateless re-runs; loops until the budget is spent or no god-files remain.
- **`run.campaign.extract-godfile-summary`** — jq-parses the raw StructureOS scan text envelope (no `structuredContent`): `god_file_count = ._summary.by_id.SOS001 // 0`, `worst_path = ._summary.worst_files[0].path`.
- **`run.campaign.structural-report`** — Tier-2 observability report.
- **Cross-namespace flow reference** to `flow.refactor.god-file` (`kind: workflow` + `use.inputs.target_path`), documented for both `include:` (unprefixed) and `repos:` (prefixed) mount modes.
- **Fixtures**: `tests/fixtures/rust-godfile/` (533 LOC / 81 pub-fn crate that trips SOS001); zero-count reuse of the Tier-1 findings fixture.
- **Docs**: Tier-2 plan, `tests/campaign-tier2-e2e.md`, README Tier-2 wiring + id-prefix mounting note.

### Not agent-free (unlike Tier 1)
The god-file flow's `fixing` state is `actor: agent`, so the consumer gateway must have a coding agent wired. Tier 1 stays fully agent-free.

### Design notes
- **Worst god-file selection** uses `_summary.worst_files[0].path` (category-independent, score-sorted) — **not** `focus.items[0]`, whose priority order (ParseErrors > GodFiles) can mis-pick the target. Live-proven on frontrails-product.
- Additive `frontrails-campaign.yaml` — zero FrontRails diff.

### Verification
- `praxec check` validates (both `flow.findings.structural` + `flow.findings.sweep-safe` resolve).
- Both fixtures build/test.
- E2E procedure exercises selection / dispatch / budget / zero-count paths (all GO).

Unlike the earlier front-half spike, this consumes the **published** target schema (`linkml-ohdsi-gis-extension-envar`, #27) and links every row back to its EnVar sidecar — so it's the durable seed of D6.1, not throwaway scaffolding. (It supersedes the front-half PoC, which is being closed.)

## What it does

Row counts (24 = 3×8), `value_as_number` == source Tmax, provenance linkage (`exposure_source_value` = sidecar `provenance_id`) on every row, unique keys, headline `91204 / 2022-07-19 = 43.93 °C`. Output **validates** against the target schema (see patch note).

The script vendors a relaxed copy so output validates. **Stopgap pending an upstream fix in #27** — the vendored file is gitignored/regenerated, not committed.

author: ayo326
body:
## N1 (HIGH) - driver self-affiliation → carrier-authority bypass

A driver could self-declare `ownedByOperatorId` and inherit an arbitrary **VERIFIED carrier's FMCSA authority and insurance**, then haul real freight under it without that carrier's consent - defeating the core "only a VERIFIED carrier may accept loads" invariant.

Four hops, all unguarded:
1. `PUT /api/driver/profile` (`driver.ts:83`) - no request schema, raw body → `updateProfile`'s spread.
2. `POST /profile` - express-validator validates known fields but **does not strip unknown ones**.
3. `createProfile` (`driverService.ts:107`) copies `ownedByOperatorId` / `isSelf` from the body.
4. `resolveCarrierOfRecord` (`carrierOfRecord.ts:42`) trusted the field with **no back-check**.

### Fix - two layers

- **`routes/driver.ts`**: strip server-controlled fields (`driverId`, `userId`, `ownedByOperatorId`, `isSelf`, `status`) on POST + PUT `/profile`. Deliberately at the **route** (the untrusted boundary), not the service - so the server-derived writers (`createSelfDriver`, the consented fleet-invite accept, `createOrgDriver`, `updateStatus`) are unaffected.
- **`carrierOfRecord.ts`**: the operator must **corroborate** the link - the driver is in its `fleetDriverIds`, or the driver row belongs to the operator's own `userId` (the self-driver, which is deliberately never in `fleetDriverIds`). `driver.isSelf` is **not** consulted: it is forgeable by the same vector. An unclaimed link **falls through** to the org path, so a legitimate org driver carrying a stale field still resolves their real carrier.
- **`isFleetCarrierDriver`** no longer short-circuits on the raw field - that shortcut could answer "not a fleet carrier" while `resolveCarrierOfRecord` resolved a real `CARRIER_ORG`. One resolver, one answer.

### `carrierId` is intentionally NOT stripped

The audit recommended stripping it; checking the frontend showed that would **break driver onboarding** - it is a user-entered "Carrier ID" in `REQUIRED_PROFILE` (`SettingsPage`), so stripping it means the profile can never be completed. It is not an authority field: `resolveCarrierOfRecord` never reads it (only a capacity-event label fallback, where the resolved carrier wins).

## ENV-1 (MEDIUM) - parity checker was blind to the W9 access log

`check-table-env-parity.mjs` matched `DYNAMODB_[A-Z_]+_TABLE`; the class excludes digits, so **`DYNAMODB_W9_ACCESS_LOG_TABLE`** (the append-only log of every full W9/TIN open - "the most sensitive read on the platform") never matched. The checker under-counted config slots by one and **never verified dev/staging override it**; it stayed green only because dev happens to enumerate it today. Now `[A-Z0-9_]+` → reports **54** prefix-derived slots (was 53), still exits 0.

## Tests

**+8 net; suite 890 → 898 green, tsc clean.**
- New: 4 resolver-refusal cases (unclaimed link, forged `isSelf`, nonexistent operator, fall-through to real org), 3 route-strip cases, 1 fleet-pool case.
- Updated the tests that **encoded the old no-read shortcut** (`gates`, `invoicePayee`, `broadcastPersonaFilter`). The last was rewritten to route mocks **by command input** rather than call order, since its pool test resolves drivers concurrently and an ordered chain would be decided by scheduling.

## Rollout note

The corroboration is **fail-closed**: a driver whose operator does not claim them loses OO authority (they fall through to their org, or become unaffiliated). Legit paths set both sides (the fleet-invite accept sets `ownedByOperatorId` **and** adds to `fleetDriverIds`; the self-driver matches on `userId`), and prod's verified population is tiny, so blast radius is minimal - but this is the one behavioural change to sanity-check before/after deploy.

No infra change. No em/en dashes.

author: milos-agathon
body:
## Problem

Mesh-mode terrain lives in the world XY plane with heights along +Z (`terrain_pbr_pom.wgsl` `mesh_world_pos`), but `build_camera_matrices` orbits the eye around +Y with a hard-coded `up = Vec3::Y` — a grid axis. Oblique mesh renders therefore come out rolled with north-south inverted: the camera treats the terrain as a wall. The error nearly cancels at diagonal (phi≈45) cameras, which is how it survived visual review; forge3d-studio's final-render downloads surfaced it as "the downloaded image is upside down".

## Fix

- New opt-in camera mode string **`mesh:zup`** (colon-option, same pattern as `clipmap:N:M`): Z-up orbit with `up = Vec3::Z` (+Y fallback at the top-down pole where look_at degenerates). `cam_theta_deg` keeps its documented "0 looks straight down" meaning; `cam_phi_deg` becomes a true azimuth within the terrain plane.
- Plain `mesh` is untouched and stays byte-identical for existing callers.
- Hardened the three camera-mode checks that compared the raw string against `"mesh"` (aov/offline probe span, virtual-texture visible rect) to `is_mesh_camera_mode` so option suffixes cannot silently change probe scaling.
- Documented the mode in `terrain_params.py`; unit test for the suffix parser.

## Verification

Rebuilt the wheel and A/B-compared the offline pipeline against the interactive viewer on an asymmetric two-cone DEM at azimuths 0°/45°/135°: marker-vector angles agree within 2.5°. Consumers mapping north-up rasters use `np.flipud(dem)` + azimuth negation (the reflection flips orbit handedness).

author: mbouaziz
body:
The skipruntime half of #1369, and the same bug class as #1342 / #1365 / #1368. Both declarations are zero-argument natives over mutable host state, so every gate in `canCSECall` passes and two identical calls merge into one.

## `popContext`

```skip
@cpp_extern("SkipRuntime_popContext")
native fun popContext(): void;
```

Backed by `SkipRuntime_popContext(): void { this.stack.pop(); }` (`core/src/index.ts:999` → `Stack.pop`, `index.ts:232`) — a destructive pop of the host context stack.

**The existing call sites are safe today only by luck.** They all follow this shape:

```skip
pushContext(context);
try {
  ...
  popContext();      // success path
} catch {
| ex ->
  popContext();      // catch path
  throw ex
}
```

The two pops are on mutually exclusive paths, so neither dominates the other and GVN leaves them alone. But that is an accident of the current code, not a guarantee: inlining a push/pop function twice into one caller yields straight-line `pop(); pop();`, which **does** merge — one pop for two pushes, and the stack leaks. `pushContext` is unaffected, because its `mutable` argument already blocks CSE.

## `getFork`

```skip
@cpp_extern("SkipRuntime_getFork")
native fun getFork(): ?String;
```

Backed by `SkipRuntime_getFork(): Nullable<string> { return this.forkName; }` (`index.ts:1007`), where `forkName` is reassigned by the sibling setter `setFork` (`index.ts:1015`). The compiler cannot see that write, so two reads straddling a `setFork` collapse onto the stale first value. `getContext` is unaffected — its `?mutable Context` return already blocks CSE.

## On evidence

I have **not** constructed a running repro for these two, and I would rather say so than overclaim. What I do have is the structural proof from the sibling PR #1368: `printPersistentSize` has the identical signature shape — zero arguments, `void` return, stateful implementation — and two identical calls to it **provably printed one line instead of two**. `popContext` differs only in what the side effect is.

## The fix

`untracked` + `@allow_tracked_call`, as established in #1353. Verified both `skipruntime-core` and `skipruntime` (ffi) typecheck unchanged, so `@allow_tracked_call` holds across every existing caller in `BaseTypes.sk`, `Runtime.sk`, `Utils.sk` and `FFI.sk`.

Leaves the exception-slot trio (`getExn`/`saveExn`/`replaceExn`) from #1369 untouched — that one is exception plumbing and wants a deliberate call.

author: utkarshtiwari07
body:
…dup bug

The user's v6 live run had a clean funnel (no flooding, no crawl4ai in india_mnc, selection-gated sources) but still returned near-nothing: remote 787 fetched -> 18 candidates -> 0 reported; india 414 -> 16 -> 4 reported. v6 fixed the RATIO (candidate density 1% -> 20-40%) but never fixed the VOLUME: every source was still an ATS API or a guest scrape, none of which reach where the actual India/remote AI/ML job market lives.

Two root causes, both confirmed before writing any code:

1. CONFIRMED BUG - filters.prefilter marked every CANDIDATE as cross-run "seen", not just reported ones. Re-running the tool while tuning it (the user's own workflow) silently drained the whole pool on every run - a job that was never even shown to the user became permanently invisible. Fixed: only a job that reaches report_*.json is now marked seen (pipeline._pop_reported_fingerprints, called after the report is written); a --fresh flag skips the cache entirely for one run.

2. The pipeline never touched Indeed, Naukri (India's dominant board), LinkedIn's own search (with a real description this time), or Google Jobs. Researched open-source options per the user's ask ("sparkling or anything like that"): python-jobspy (github.com/Bunsly/JobSpy) is a maintained scraper fanning out to 8 boards behind one uniform API - verified live this session (Indeed India, LinkedIn Delhi): full markdown descriptions (500-8,800+ chars) and job_url_direct, the company's OWN careers URL when the board resolved it. Scrapling (the likely "sparkling") was also verified live but is an anti-bot fetcher (a crawl4ai alternative), not a job-board scraper - it wouldn't add a source, so it's documented but not integrated.

   Also researched Delhi NCR specifically, per the user's direct ask ("ai engineer job company name = housing.com"): live-probed 40 NCR tech companies (Housing.com/REA, MakeMyTrip, PolicyBazaar, Lenskart, Delhivery, Urban Company, Cars24, OYO, Blinkit, BharatPe, ...) - only 3/40 expose a clean ATS API (Paytm, Zomato/Eternal, Info Edge - added to the registry; Paytm has 11 current AI/ML titles, Zomato/Info Edge currently have 0 so the existing precision gate correctly left them out). The other 37 are structurally invisible to any ATS-only design; they're now reached via rotating, company-targeted JobSpy searches.

Changes:
- job/jobspy_source.py (new): fetch_jobspy() runs each configured search, normalizes JobSpy's uniform DataFrame schema to the shared job dict (prefers job_url_direct, falls back to the board's own posting URL - still a real fetched description, not a fabricated card). Guarded import: missing python-jobspy prints a loud warning, never a silent volume drop.
- pipeline.py: new Phase D0 (JobSpy) ahead of D1 (job-level Serper); _build_ncr_searches/_ncr_search_batch rotate ~10 NCR companies/run into company-targeted Indeed+Google searches; funnel reports jobspy_error / jobspy_searches_run / per-site counts.

body:
Bumps `github.com/gocronx-team/cron` from v0.1.3 to **v0.2.0** to pull in the scheduler concurrency/correctness fixes.

cron master HEAD is exactly the v0.2.0 tag, so `go get github.com/gocronx-team/cron@master` resolves to v0.2.0 (Go canonicalizes to the tag when the commit is tagged).

## Included cron fixes
- **GOC-22** — TOCTOU data race between `isRunning()` and `Start()`.
- **GOC-21** — `sync.Pool` dirty-result reuse.
- **GOC-23** — unbounded worker-pool goroutines under overload (+ saturation metrics).
- **GOC-20** — catch-up storm after a freeze (sleep/pause/long GC): missed fires are now **skipped** instead of replayed back-to-back.

## Behavior note
After a process freeze, a periodic task now fires **once** on resume and continues at normal cadence, instead of firing every missed slot. Normal on-time cadence is unchanged.

## Not releasing
Per plan, this only updates the dependency; no gocron tag/release is cut — it will ship with upcoming features.

## Verification
`go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and the full suite under `go test -race ./...` pass against cron v0.2.0. Only `go.mod`/`go.sum` change.

author: copilot
tikazyq
body:
Closes #247.

An author — human or agent — had no machine-discoverable way to learn what `with:` fields an action accepts or what `outputs` it produces (the canonical example: `ui/assert-element` produces `satisfied`, findable only in prose + Rust source). And `duhem validate` checked reference *wiring* but not against the action's *real* fields, so typos passed validate and failed only at run time. For a v0.x framework with no LLM pretraining corpus, that discoverability + verification gap is the dominant authoring-DX cost.

## What this adds

1. **A machine-readable contract on every action** — `Action::contract()` returns its `with:` fields (+ closed enums), outputs, and an example, defined next to each action so it can't drift from `invoke`. `duhem_actions::catalog()` / `contract_for()` expose it.
2. **`duhem describe <uses>` + `duhem actions`** — on-demand, version-exact ground truth (retrieval-by-tool, not docs-archaeology). `duhem describe ui/assert-element` shows `outputs: satisfied, count` and the `expected` enum.
3. **Validate-time field checking** — `duhem validate` cross-checks each step's `with:` keys, `outputs:` action-fields, and closed-enum values against the contract, failing with a prescriptive "valid: …" hint *before* run time.

## Design decisions (the spec's open forks)

- **Contract as an `Action` trait method** (over a separate table — can't drift).
- **Names + closed-enum values now**; per-field types later (spec's recommendation).
- **Field-checking layered in the CLI**, not `duhem-schema` (which doesn't depend on `duhem-actions`). It **under-enforces** — an unknown/custom `uses`, and actions with no listed outputs, are skipped — so a valid VD is **never false-rejected**; run-time `deny_unknown_fields` stays the backstop.

## Verified

- `duhem describe ui/assert-element` → `satisfied` (spec Test #1).
- `duhem validate` flags an unknown `with:` key, an unknown `outputs:` field, and a bad `expected:` enum — each with a "valid: …" hint — and still passes valid VDs (no false-reject).
- 173 `duhem-actions` + 132 `duhem-cli` tests; `cargo fmt` + `clippy` clean.

## Deferred (fast-follow)

Plan item 4 — generate the *static* docs action-reference from the contract + drift-check it in `xtask`. `duhem describe` already provides that reference dynamically, so it's additive; the sibling #248 (agent-authoring) can consume `describe`/`catalog` directly.

## Schema impact

**None.** Adds a trait method + two CLI commands + a validate pass. No wire-format change.

author: ryanmurf
body:
## M7 CP4 (M-k) — migrate bin/call.sh to an AMI operational command

The FreeSWITCH/ESL `bin/call.sh` (gateway preflight + `originate` + unconditional
`hupall` over ESL) is replaced by an AMI-native operational command.

- **bin/call.sh** — AMI-native (`Action: Originate` / `CoreShowChannels` /
  `Hangup`); reads its AMI secret from a mounted **k8s Secret file** (never argv);
  **refuses a duplicate** concurrent call to the same destination; and turns the
  old `hupall` foot-gun into an **explicit, doubly-guarded** operation —
  `--hangup-all` **and** `--force` are both required. `--hangup-all` alone
  refuses; a bare `--hangup DEST` targets only that destination.
- **bin/ami_call.py** — the low-level AMI transport (`list` / `originate` /
  `hangup`), secret read from `--secret-file`.

### Receiver-side proof (isolated offline-carrier harness)
`tests/cp4-call-command/run.sh` drives the command against the offline carrier:

```
A --dry-run places no call:                        PASS
B real call reaches carrier (1 INVITE):            PASS
C duplicate-call guard refuses 2nd identical call: PASS
D --hangup-all without --force REFUSES (guarded):  PASS  (rc=3)
E --hangup-all --force performs guarded hupall:    PASS
```

### Captured REDs (defeat each guard in the script)
- **A** dry-run branch defeated → it places a real call → `A FAIL`.
- **C** duplicate guard defeated → the carrier sees **two** INVITEs → `C FAIL`.
- **D** `--force` guard defeated → `--hangup-all` fires unconfirmed (rc=0), the
  live call is torn down → `D FAIL` (the foot-gun).

No Rust changes; `cargo test/clippy --workspace --exclude pjsip-shim` unaffected
(green). Tested only against the offline carrier — never live qa-sip.

Fixes #7862

## Description

Fixes Go binding parameter validation for direct `Query` and `Exec` calls.

Previously, direct calls such as:

 ```go
 db.Query("SELECT v FROM pair WHERE k=?")
```
could skip argument-count validation when no parameters were supplied. This change makes the driver validate the prepared statement parameter count before binding.

## Testing
- Adds regression coverage for missing parameters in both direct Query and Exec.

## Motivation and context

Missing parameters should return an error instead of executing with unbound placeholders.

body:
## Wave 4 — European Work & Project Calculator v1 (Draft, no merge, no deploy, no migrations)

### Audit finding first: what was NOT built
The deterministic cost engine **already existed** — `apps/web/lib/estimate/estimate.ts` (`ESTIMATE_VERSION = 1`, 9 sector templates, labour→direct→overhead→margin→contingency→total + low/base/high, validation, assumption/missing keys), persisted server-recomputed into `customer_requests.payload.estimate`, with builder/summary UI in the demand wizard and full tests. The spec's `lib/calculators/` second engine was **cancelled**; a guard now fails the build if that directory ever appears or the public page forks the math.

### Exact reuse map
| Reused as-is | `computeEstimate` + all engine helpers, templates/units lists, the whole `estimate` i18n namespace (fields/results/errors/assumptions/disclaimer), `csvCell`, `AuthCtaLink`, `MARKET_COUNTRIES` + `labourMarket.countryNames` |
|---|---|
| Refactored for reuse | `estimate-summary.tsx` → pure `EstimateSummaryView` (labels-as-props) + unchanged i18n wrapper. Rendered output identical; `estimate-builder.test.ts` guard reads the pair as one surface. |
| Why `EstimateBuilder` was not mounted directly | it reads `useTranslations("auth...")`; the marketing group ships a ~4 KB message pick and the client-messages allowlist guard (rule 9) bans non-literal namespaces there. Mounting it would push the ~28 KB `auth` tree onto every marketing page. All labels are server-resolved props instead (CompanyNeedForm precedent) — allowlist guard stays green with zero additions. |

### New
- **Public route** `/{lt,en,ru,nl,de}/calculators/project-cost` — stateless, account-free, SSG (9.33 kB page / 128 kB first load), 4-step progressive wizard, honest empty + incomplete states (quantities without rates → "estimate incomplete", never a fake 0), sitemap + curated cross-sector SEO (`projectCostCalculator` PAGE_SEO key).
- **VAT display layer v1** (`lib/estimate/vat-display-v1.ts`) — documented decision: the shared engine is untouched (`ESTIMATE_VERSION` still 1, stored payloads parse byte-identically; guard asserts no VAT concept in the engine). VAT lines only when explicitly entered; entered 0 % shown (reverse charge); sub-total excl. VAT / VAT / total incl. VAT.
- **Area quantity pack v1** (`lib/estimate/packs/area-quantity-v1.ts`) — pure, versioned; feeds `quantity`/`totalHours`/`materials` into the engine. Acceptance fixtures green: 100 m² net × 3 × 50 mm, 5 % waste, 6 m²/pkg → 300 m² coverage, 315 m² with waste, **53 packages** (52.5 up), 15 m³. Package count can never round down (float-noise-safe ceil; guard-banned floor/round).
- **CSV export v1** + **print stylesheet**: stable column ids + localized labels + version/provenance rows; `csvSafeCell` neutralises formula injection on top of shared `csvCell`; print CSS scoped to the result region (browser print-to-PDF).
- **Accommodation helper** (workers × days × price/day → written into the existing `transportAccommodation` field on click). Per-km transport omitted — no honest default rate exists; documented.
- **Bridges** (both resolve to real routes; guard-asserted):
  - auth: CTA → `/{locale}/dashboard#demand-intake` (existing anchored demand intake with the same estimate builder) via `AuthCtaLink`; copy says explicitly the numbers are NOT transferred (the wizard supports no prefill param today — no fake claim).
  - anon: CTA → `/{locale}/company-need?number_of_workers=N&country=CC`; new bounded adapter `lib/staffing/company-need-prefill.ts` applies validated defaults post-hydration (page stays static). Calculator sends ONLY worker count + country — no prices, no free text, no PII in URLs (guard-asserted).
- **Guard suite** `lib/guards/project-cost-calculator.test.ts` (24 tests): single engine, engine-untouched lock, never-round-down, CSV injection, cross-sector title copy (5 locales + SEO), real CTA routes, 5-locale key parity with no `[EN]`/empty values, bounded prefill.
- **Docs**: `docs/product/european-work-project-calculator-v1.md` (formula tables, rounding policy incl. the inherited `round2` float divergence, country/currency model, honesty boundaries, decisions).

### Enabled countries / currency
Country select = existing `MARKET_COUNTRIES` (LT LV EE PL DE NL DK NO SE FI) with `labourMarket.countryNames` labels; optional, display-only. Currency = free ISO text defaulting EUR (engine's existing model). No country→currency registry, no FX, no external APIs, no market averages, no AI numbers.

### Validation
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm -C apps/web typecheck` | PASS |
| `pnpm -C apps/web lint` | PASS (0 errors; 1 pre-existing unrelated warning in premium-hub) |
| `pnpm -C apps/web check:i18n-debt` | PASS — within baseline (da=829, de=0, nl=0, ru=0; no new debt) |
| `pnpm -C apps/web check:primary-route-smoke` | PASS — 46 routes, 0 blocking |
| `pnpm -C apps/web check:public-seo-indexing` | PASS |
| Targeted vitest (estimate suites, 3 new module suites, new guard, estimate-builder guard, e2e-presence, public-seo, client-messages-allowlist, i18n parity) | **190/190 PASS** |
| `pnpm -C apps/web build` | PASS — `● /[locale]/calculators/project-cost` SSG, 9.33 kB / 128 kB first load |

### Browser proof (local dev, port 3311) — honest scope
Pixel screenshots were NOT capturable on this shared machine (browser-pane screenshot capture timed out repeatedly); verification was done via accessibility-tree reads, DOM text dumps and JS inspection on the live dev server:
- LT + EN pages render (title/h1/lede/honesty block; canonical `https://labourmarket.ai/...`, hreflang lt/en/ru/nl/de/x-default, robots index,follow);
- all 9 sector templates + 10 localized countries in the selects;
- live acceptance fixture in the pack UI: 300 / 315 m², **53 pkg**, 15 m³, 530 EUR materials, 150 h, 50 h crew duration; "apply" filled quantity/hours/materials;
- honest incomplete state shown with materials-only total (530 EUR) and "labour cost missing" banner; after entering rate 20 → 3 530,00 EUR net, VAT 21 % → 741,30 → 4 271,30 incl. VAT;
- bridge hrefs live: `/lt/dashboard#demand-intake` and `/lt/company-need?number_of_workers=4&country=LT`; the company-need form prefilled workers=4/country=LT after hydration; invalid params (`99999`/`XX`/script) dropped to defaults;
- 320 px viewport: `documentElement.scrollWidth = 320` (no horizontal scroll; calculator content 272 px); print rules for `#pcc-print-area` confirmed loaded. Actual print-preview render not captured (same screenshot limitation).

### REQUIRES_OWNER_DECISION
- **Saved estimates** (persistence for anonymous users) — needs a table/migration + retention policy; v1 is deliberately stateless (CSV/print are the take-away).
- Future: ECB reference-rate adapter (external source gate), org rate books, demand-wizard estimate-prefill param.

### Limitations
- Stateless (reload clears); no estimate transfer into the demand wizard (disclosed in UI copy); VAT display-only; one quantity pack; money math inherits the engine's documented `round2` float policy (unchanged by mandate).

### Rollback
Single squash commit; revert removes the route, modules, guard and message namespace. The only touched shared files are `estimate-summary.tsx` (behaviour-preserving split), `company-need-form.tsx` (additive post-hydration prefill), `metadata.ts`/`sitemap.ts` (additive entries) and 5 message catalogs (additive namespace) — all trivially revertable.

body:
#1130

## Problem

Native NEAR swaps (and native NEAR payments routed through Intents) failed with "The account doesn't have enough balance" when the treasury had never held wNEAR: the batched `near_deposit` deducted the 0.00125 NEAR NEP-145 registration cost from the attached deposit, so the follow-up `ft_transfer` of the full amount overdrew the just-credited wNEAR balance.

Example failed transaction: https://nearblocks.io/txns/DqWintMv2onR1xpNnKJRHFWfm66Xc1A7vSb5B9BzAjzv/execution

## Change

Backend-only, using the existing relay `storage_deposit` infrastructure (`nt-be/src/handlers/relay/effects/registrations.rs`): the derivation now also registers the **treasury itself** on the called contract when a proposal contains a `near_deposit` action. Previously only the `ft_transfer` receiver (the 1Click deposit address) was registered.

Every vote is relayed through the backend, so the registration happens right before the approving vote executes the transfer. This covers:
- native NEAR swaps (`near_deposit` + `ft_transfer` batch),
- native NEAR payments via Intents (same batch shape),
- pure wraps (`near_deposit` only — previously silently wrapped 0.00125 NEAR less than quoted on first use),
- **already-created pending proposals**, with no changes to the proposals themselves.

`storage_deposit` is sent with `registration_only: true` and is skipped when the account is already registered (and refunded if the pre-check races), so repeat approvals cost nothing extra.

## Tests

Updated/added in `registrations.rs`:
- `near_deposit_plus_ft_transfer_registers_treasury_and_transfer_receiver`
- `near_deposit_only_registers_treasury` (pure wrap)

`cargo test --lib registrations` (12 passed), `cargo clippy`, `cargo fmt --check` all clean.

author: rodrigosaint
body: ## Summary Makes agent runs actually emit OpenTelemetry spans, reusing the workflow OTel module's already-registered global tracer provider so they land in the same backend as workflow traces — with no new exporter/provider created from the agents side. - **SDK (`packages/@n8n/agents`)**: `RuntimeTelemetry.withRootSpan` now starts spans with `root: true` (self-contained trace, source-agnostic shape) and accepts an optional `links` param — a seam for a future ticket (nesting delegated sub-agent spans), unused today. Root spans now carry generic OTel GenAI (`gen_ai.*`) attributes always; `langsmith.*` attributes are now gated behind a new `BuiltTelemetry.isLangSmith` flag (set automatically by `LangSmithTelemetry.build()`) instead of being emitted unconditionally on every span. Tool-call spans are renamed to the OTel semconv `execute_tool {name}` convention and carry `gen_ai.tool.*` attributes alongside the existing `ai.toolCall.*` ones. - **CLI (`packages/cli`)**: new `AgentRunTracingService` builds a per-run `BuiltTelemetry` from the OTel module's global tracer (`trace.getTracer('@n8n/agents')`), gated by `N8N_AGENTS_TRACING_ENABLED` (added in #34401). Wired into all three run sites: - `streamChatResponse` (chat/task runs — telegram/slack/n8n-chat/test/task) - `streamWorkflowAgent` (workflow-invoked runs, entity-backed and inline, with `execution_id`/`workflow_id`/`node_id`) - `resumeForChat` (HITL resume — recovers the original run's `source` via a new `AgentExecutionRepository.findLatestSuspendedByThreadId` query, since a resume request doesn't carry its own `source`) No provider is created, registered, or shut down anywhere in this change — the OTel module owns that lifecycle exclusively. When the module is disabled, the tracer is a no-op and nothing is emitted. ## How to test This feature requires the OTel module enabled — it has no effect on a default instance. 1. Run a local OTLP-compatible backend, e.g. Jaeger: ```bash docker run -d --name jaeger -p 16686:16686 -p 4318:4318 jaegertracing/all-in-one:latest ``` 2. Start n8n with: ``` N8N_OTEL_ENABLED=true N8N_AGENTS_TRACING_ENABLED=true ``` 3. Run an agent (test chat, a published chat integration, a scheduled task, or the AI Agent node inside a workflow), including a HITL tool-approval flow if configured. 4. Open http://localhost:16686, search for service `n8n`, and inspect the trace: a root `.stream`/`.generate` span with `gen_ai.*` attributes, nested `execute_tool {name}` spans, and (for workflow-invoked runs) `execution_id`/`workflow_id`/`node_id` in the metadata. 5. Confirm a workflow-hosted run and a chat-hosted run of the same agent produce structurally identical span trees, differing only in `source` (and the workflow-only correlation IDs). 6. Set `N8N_OTEL_ENABLED=false` and confirm agent runs complete normally with no errors and no spans emitted. ## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts https://linear.app/n8n/issue/TRUST-307 ## Review / Merge checklist - [x] I have seen this code, I have run this code, and I take responsibility for this code. - [x] PR title and summary are descriptive. ([conventions](../blob/master/.github/pull_request_title_conventions.md)) - [x] [Docs updated](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs) or follow-up ticket created. - [x] Tests included. - [ ] PR Labeled with `Backport to Beta`, `Backport to Stable`, or `Backport to v1` (if the PR is an urgent fix that needs to be backported) 🤖 PR Summary generated by AI ---

This replaces both local helpers with a shared `getGoogleThinkingBudget` in [google-shared.ts](https://github.com/PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-agent/pull/463/files#diff-b08913b9ac25a43585c80ef2d0fbd2dfd99de1f59459a69973b05bb6ed70c60d) that maps `2.5-flash-lite` minimal effort to 512 tokens. > > > > Macroscope summarized 3fb9523. > > --- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > Small provider payload fix with shared helper refactor and regression tests; no auth, data, or API surface changes beyond correct thinking budgets for one model family on Vertex. > > **Overview** > Vertex **Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite** with `reasoning: "minimal"` now sends a **512-token** `thinkingBudget`, matching the direct Google provider and Flash-Lite’s supported minimum. Previously Vertex reused the generic **2.5-flash** mapping (**128** tokens), which could yield invalid budgets. > > Budget selection is centralized in **`getGoogleThinkingBudget`** in `google-shared.ts`, with **`2.5-flash-lite` checked before `2.5-flash`** so lite IDs are not misclassified. Duplicate helpers were removed from `google.ts` and `google-vertex.ts`; custom `thinkingBudgets` and Pro/Flash mappings are unchanged. > > New Vitest coverage asserts the outgoing Vertex payload for stable and preview Flash-Lite model IDs. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 3fb95234f748d600ebc20c42f0741c0e83481a69. body:
## Summary
- New `apex build --purge` flag: builds CSS, then immediately tree-shakes the output in place using the project's own source files — one non-interactive command instead of two
- Exports `determineSourceDirectories` and `pruneBuiltCss` from `purge.ts` so `build.ts` reuses the existing scan/prune logic rather than duplicating it
- Deliberately scoped to CSS pruning only — `--purge` never modifies `apex.config.js`. That stays `apex purge`'s job; a `build` command silently rewriting config felt like the wrong default, especially in CI

## Why
The minimal-output path required two separate commands (`apex build`, then `apex purge --prune-css --yes`) with nothing prompting a user toward the second step, so most real builds shipped the full, unpurged CSS.

## Test plan
- [x] New tests for `runPostBuildPurge`: prunes CSS in place given project source, and warns/no-ops (doesn't throw) when no source directories are found
- [x] Full unit suite: 244/244 passing
- [x] `npm run check` (biome) clean
- [x] Verified end-to-end against a real Next.js app: `apex build --purge` runs build then prune in one invocation, producing the same output as running both commands separately

Closes #19

body:
## 目的
運動連鎖をより本質的に捉えるため、単純な「膝→肘」（PR #6）を、**床反力(proxy)→下肢→上肢**の3リンクに拡張し、**ズレがどのリンクで起きているか**を2つのギャップで示す。

## 指標（連動性/手打ち タブに2行）
- **床反力→下肢 `grf_to_lower_ms`**（Gap1）：踏んだ力が脚の伸展に乗るまでの遅れ
- **下肢→上肢 `lower_to_upper_ms`**（Gap2＝手打ち度）：脚の力が腕の伸展に乗るまでの遅れ

Gap1が大きい＝「踏む力が脚に伝わっていない」、Gap2が大きい＝「脚の力が腕に乗らず手打ち寄り」を切り分けられる。

## 算出方法
- **① 床反力proxy**：重心（股関節中点 hipY）の**上向き加速ピーク**。ニュートン f=m·a より上向き加速が上向き床反力の代理。hipYを平滑化してから非一様2階微分（`comUpwardAccelSeries`）。
- **② 下肢**：膝伸展角速度ピーク。**③ 上肢**：肘伸展角速度ピーク。②③は膝ピーク周辺の窓で探索し、着地スパイクを誤検出しない。
- 既存の `impulses`/`pickPeak` 機構を流用。

## 品質ゲート（偽値を出さない）
各ギャップは、対象が明確に追跡できている時だけ数値化。条件未達は **未確定(null)**。床反力proxyは2階微分でノイズに弱いため、平滑化＋窓＋「正の上向き加速」ゲートで保護。

## 安全性
純粋な指標の追加・整理。姿勢検出・ボール検出・他指標・UI構造・server.js は無変更。ゲート未達は既存の未確定表示。

## 検証（オフライン・実映像 IMG_7327）
- ① 2.10s → ② 2.167s → ③ 2.30s と近位→遠位で順序どおり。
- **Gap1（床反力→下肢）= +67ms / Gap2（下肢→上肢）= +133ms**。

## 既知の限界（正直に）
- 計測は**最も見える側**の腕（この検証クリップは左＝ガイド腕）。シュート側から撮ればシュート腕になる。
- **30fps＝各イベント±33ms**。ギャップは±33ms程度の粗さ。床反力proxyが最もノイズに弱い。
- n=1。ゲートにより悪い入力は未確定。実アプリ表示はマージ→デプロイ後に「連動性/手打ち」タブで確認。

author: johnnychris77
body:
## Summary

Implements Project Foundation Sprint 1 — making every governed object persistent, versioned, auditable, recoverable, reproducible, and traceable — with **executed** evidence wherever this environment allows:

- **PostgreSQL 16 verified for real** (first time ever): the full 13-revision Alembic chain applied cleanly (431 tables), downgrade/re-upgrade exercised, and the entire backend test suite run against a live PostgreSQL server. The first run failed 110 tests; every failure was a real defect SQLite had been masking, and all are fixed in this PR (details below and in `docs/foundation/POSTGRESQL_MIGRATION.md`).
- **Governed object storage**: new `governed_objects` registry (permanent `GOBJ-` Object ID, SHA-256, uploader, tenant, retention policy, storage URI, version/supersession chain) over the existing byte-transport layer; per-tenant SHA-256 dedup; fail-closed hash-verified reads; every register/access/integrity-failure written to the hash-chained audit trail. Migrations `d4e8a1c93f57` + `e7b2f4a86c31`.
- **Audit immutability enforced in the ORM**: `before_update`/`before_delete` + bulk-ORM guards on `audit_logs` raise `AuditImmutabilityError`; the tamper-detection tests now simulate out-of-band raw-SQL tampering — exactly the threat the existing hash chain detects. `audit_logs.details` changed `String(4000)` → `Text` so audit evidence can never be silently truncated (PostgreSQL was rejecting real compliance-bundle events).
- **Single-active-Production-model invariant** in `candidate_promotion.promote_candidate`.
- **Backup / restore / disaster recovery — executed, not just documented**: `backend/scripts/gpae_backup_restore.py` (pg_dump/sqlite + object storage + model artifacts, SHA-256 manifest, verify-before-restore). A real exercise ran against the migrated PostgreSQL database: backup 1.10 s → real `DROP DATABASE` + storage deletion → full restore 10.4 s with row counts, alembic revision, and object hashes verified → artifact corruption detected fail-closed and recovered in 16.0 s. Raw evidence committed at `docs/foundation/evidence/DR_EXERCISE_EVIDENCE.json`.
- **Monitoring**: GPAE deep health check across 7 persistence components with per-component status/latency, RBAC-gated `/api/gpae/health/deep` + `/api/gpae/monitoring/sweep`, and truthful alert dispatch (records `no_destination_configured` rather than claiming delivery; emails only when SMTP is configured).
- **14 documentation files** under `docs/foundation/`, each explicit about EXECUTED vs VERIFIED-BY-EXISTING-SUITE vs DEFERRED-to-managed-environment evidence.

## Why This Change

The Foundation Sprint 1 directive requires that nothing critical to clinical evidence depends on temporary development storage. Most persistence invariants (LCID permanence, frozen datasets, append-only Ground Truth/annotations, baseline lifecycle, hash-chained audit) already existed; the genuine gaps were that PostgreSQL support had never been executed, object storage had no governance registry, audit rows were not ORM-immutable, only one-Production-model was unenforced, and backup/restore/DR had never been run. This PR closes exactly those gaps and documents honestly what still requires a managed environment (a long-lived database/storage service, a configured alert destination, schedulers).

## Scope

- Backend: 6 new files (model, 2 services, route, backup CLI, test suite), 9 modified (main.py wiring, audit/inspection/supervisor-review/candidate-promotion models+services, p20 route FK-ordering fix, conftest, 3 test files), 2 new Alembic migrations.
- Docs: 14 new `docs/foundation/*.md` + committed DR evidence JSON.
- No new AI capability, no clinical-scope expansion, no new dashboards, no auth changes (per the sprint's constraints and standing security rules).

## Testing

- Full SQLite suite: **3683 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed** (12:11).
- Full PostgreSQL 16 suite: 110 failures on first-ever run → all root-caused and fixed → re-run **3682 passed / 1 failed**, final fix (recall-signal FK ordering) re-verified green on PostgreSQL (86 passed in affected files). SQLite's clean run includes all fixes.
- Alembic: upgrade head, downgrade -1, re-upgrade — all executed on PostgreSQL 16.13.
- Executed DR exercise: ALL_STEPS_PASSED (`docs/foundation/evidence/DR_EXERCISE_EVIDENCE.json`).
- `ruff check app tests`: clean. Frontend build: clean (4.20 s).

## Risks

- The audit ORM immutability guards will raise on any future code that tries to edit/delete `audit_logs` rows via the ORM — that is the intended behavior; raw-SQL remains the documented out-of-band boundary (closed operationally by DB-role permissions in managed deployments).
- The single-active-Production guard blocks a second Production promotion until the incumbent is rolled back — intended.
- Widened columns are strictly accepting-more; `details` → Text is lossless. Migration `e7b2f4a86c31`'s downgrade is deliberately a no-op (narrowing could reject existing data).

## Rollback Plan

- `git revert 15fd1c6` (single commit). Schema: `alembic downgrade 5b7eb6e147e2` removes `governed_objects`; the widening migration's downgrade is a safe no-op by design. No data migration is destructive.

## Warum „nichts passierte"
Der Paginierungs-Fix (#56) las >100k Historie-Zeilen in **100+ seriellen** 1000er-Anfragen. Die Vermögens-API brauchte damit länger als das 20-s-Client-Timeout → der Store brach ab, versuchte es alle 5 s neu, und die Charts blieben dauerhaft leer. Die App wirkte „tot".

## Fix
- `fetchAll` lädt Seiten jetzt **parallel in Wellen** (25 gleichzeitig); kleine Tabellen kosten weiterhin nur eine Anfrage. Alle paginierten Queries haben eine **eindeutige Sortierung** (stabile Seiten bei paralleler Ausführung).

- Dividenden-Events werden explizit nach Datum sortiert (die „Zuletzt"-Liste hing zuvor an der Query-Reihenfolge).

- `npm run build` grün.
- Prod-Check: Server antwortet (Login prerendered, 200) — Engpass war ausschließlich die Daten-API.

author: leoteissier
body:
## Contexte

Suite du chantier perf de l'audit runtime (#171, #172). La famille annotation était le plus gros gisement restant : ~1 s par action (`hubSaveAnnotation` 1264 ms, `hubSaveBookmark` 1160 ms, `hubDeleteBookmark` 1003 ms, `hubDeleteAnnotation` 1001 ms, `hubSaveFunctionReview` 999 ms, `hubClearBookmarks` 985 ms).

Cause : le handler webview `hubAnnotationSaved` postait un `hubOpenDisasm` forcé **inconditionnel** après toute mutation — y compris bookmarks, reviews et clears, qui ne sont jamais bakés dans le `.asm` (seuls `name`/`comment` alimentent l'overlay du désassemblage).

## Changements (`front/shared/messages.js`)

1. **`hubAnnotationSaved` délègue au chemin gardé par signature** (`refreshDisasmForAnnotations`) : seules les mutations qui changent réellement les entrées `name`/`comment` déclenchent un rebuild. Bookmarks/reviews/clears ne coûtent plus rien.
2. **Adoption de signature après chaque build** : `hubDisasmReady` arme un flag ; le rechargement d'annotations qui suit chaque build (systématique via `hubSetBinaryPath` → autoload) adopte la signature bakée au lieu de forcer un rebuild redondant. Corrige un gaspillage réel : rouvrir un binaire annoté avec cache disasm valide repayait un désassemblage complet à chaque fois.
3. **Fix staleness** : supprimer la *dernière* annotation ne rafraîchissait jamais l'overlay (retour anticipé sur liste vide) — le `.asm` gardait l'annotation supprimée. Le rebuild sur liste vide est maintenant déclenché si le binaire avait un overlay baké.

## Mesures (audit runtime, e2e-fixture-tiny.elf)

| Scénario | Avant | Après |
|----------|-------|-------|
| hubSaveAnnotation | 1264 ms (P1) | 688 ms (P2) |
| hubSaveBookmark | 1160 ms (P1) | 696 ms (P2) |
| hubDeleteBookmark | 1003 ms (P1) | 653 ms |
| hubDeleteAnnotation | 1001 ms (P1) | 648 ms |
| hubSaveFunctionReview | 999 ms (P1) | 656 ms |
| hubClearBookmarks | 985 ms (P1) | 648 ms |

Zéro rebuild `annotation-overlay` restant dans le run ; plus aucun scénario annotation en P1. Le résiduel (~650 ms) est du quiet-wait du harnais + le spawn `annotations.py` (~65 ms), pas du travail disasm.

## Note E2E

Dans le harnais d'audit, le webview jette les réponses `hubAnnotations` comme périmées (`ignored-stale-response` — pas de binaire « courant » sélectionné côté webview). Les rebuilds observés avant venaient du handler non gardé, qui rebuildait donc même sur état périmé. En usage réel (binaire courant sélectionné), le chemin gardé rebuilde bien sur tout changement `name`/`comment` — comportement verrouillé par les tests textuels de `staticStaleResponseGuards.test.ts`.

## Suite prévue (étape B, PR séparée)

Patcher les lignes du `.asm` en place via le mapping (`addr` → ligne) pour les commentaires au lieu d'un rebuild complet, et ajouter une signature d'overlay côté host dans la validité du cache disasm (le host devient l'arbitre de la fraîcheur, indépendamment de l'état du webview). Les renames garderont le rebuild (insertion de lignes + réécriture des opérandes de branchement).

## Validation

- `npm test` : 727 passing (2 tests ajoutés)
- `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` : OK
- `npm run test:e2e:audit` : exit 0, couverture 18/18 commandes, 102/102 webview
- GitNexus detect_changes : risque low, périmètre confiné aux 2 fichiers

author: michaelatamuk
body:
Paired: [GitHub #368](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/jiuwenswarm/pull/368) ↔ [GitCode !3802](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm/merge_requests/3802) **What type of PR is this?** /kind feature --- ## **What does this PR do / why do we need it** This PR adds **Iteration Budget Awareness** to the ReAct agent loop. When the agent is running low on iterations, it now receives a clear warning in its system prompt telling it: - exactly how many steps remain - to prioritise finishing current work - to produce the best partial result possible - to explicitly state remaining TODOs This prevents the agent from being **silently cut off** mid-refactor or mid-investigation. Issue #3548 --- ## **Problem** Agents working on long tasks often start large refactors or multi-step investigations late in the run — e.g., iteration 145 out of 150 — and then get terminated abruptly when the iteration counter expires. The agent had **no awareness** of how much "time" it had left. No graceful degradation. No opportunity to wrap up. The ReActAgent loop iterates from: ``` iteration = 0 … react.max_iterations ``` The current iteration is tracked in session state (`iteration` key written by ContextProcessorRail). However: - **No component** read this value - **No prompt section** communicated remaining budget to the LLM - The agent simply died when the counter hit max_iterations --- ## **Solution** The agent now sees a **visible iteration-budget warning** when it is running low. The warning tells it: - how many steps remain - to wrap up ongoing work - to produce a final partial result - to clearly list remaining tasks This gives the agent a chance to land gracefully. ```mermaid flowchart TD classDef ok fill:#BBDEFB,color:#111,stroke:#1565C0 classDef done fill:#C8E6C9,color:#111,stroke:#2E7D32 classDef plain fill:#ECEFF1,color:#111,stroke:#607D8B LOOP(["agent loop: iteration N
of max_iterations"]):::plain LOOP -->|"remaining = max_iterations - N"| RAIL["IterationBudgetRail
reads iteration state"]:::ok RAIL -->|"remaining <= threshold"| WARN["injects budget warning
into system prompt"]:::ok WARN -->|"agent sees how much is left"| RESULT["finishes current work
clean partial result"]:::done ``` A new **IterationBudgetRail** (priority 6) fires on **before_model_call** every turn. It: 1. Reads the current iteration from `ctx.session.get_state("iteration")` 2. Computes: ``` remaining = max_iterations - iteration ``` 3. If `remaining ≤ budget_warning_threshold`, injects: ``` PromptSection( priority=96, name="iteration_budget_warning", content="You are running low on iterations…" ) ``` 4. Removes the section when not near the limit 5. Removes stale warnings on every **before_invoke** to prevent bleed-through across invocations ### **Configuration** Added to the `react:` config section: ``` budget_warning_threshold: 10 # default ``` SkillsBench sets: ``` budget_warning_threshold: 15 # 10% of its 150-iteration budget ``` --- ## **Expected Impact** - Agents no longer get cut off mid-work - Better final outputs when near iteration limits - Clear partial results instead of silent termination - Improved benchmark stability for long-running tasks - No behavior change when far from the limit --- ## **Self-checklist** - [x] **Design**: Reviewed with maintainers - [x] **Test**: Verified warning injection/removal across multiple rails - [x] **Verification**: Confirmed correct behavior at thresholds and boundaries - [ ] **Interface**: No external API changes - [x] **Document**: Added bilingual documentation for iteration budget warnings Linked Closing Issues: - Fixes #3548

author: us
body:
Five CI failures across four PRs in one day, all `No space left on device` / `ld terminated with signal 7 [Bus error]`, all on `check`, all passing on re-run. Both error strings are the same failure: `ld` mmaps its output, so a full filesystem raises SIGBUS instead of ENOSPC.

### The bug

`ci.yml`'s `check` (debug) and `conformance` (release) shared one cache key, and **`actions/cache` does not save on an exact key hit** — so whichever job finishes first defines the contents. conformance (361s) beats check (401s), so the cache holds a **release** target.

From the job logs of one run, same commit, same cache:

```
conformance: Cache saved with key: Linux-cargo-8b096cc...
check:       Cache hit occurred on the primary key Linux-cargo-8b096cc..., not saving cache.
```

| job | crates compiled | first crate | 
|---|---|---|
| conformance | **10** | `crw-mcp-proto` (first-party) |
| check | **616** | `proc-macro2` (the whole dep tree) |

So `check` downloads 815MB it cannot use, rebuilds 616 crates **every run**, and stacks a 12-16GB debug target on the restored release one. `ubuntu-latest` has ~20GB free (GitHub guarantees 14GB). It fits, or it doesn't — hence the randomness.

The bare `-cargo-` restore-keys compound it: they resurrect the previous lock's target and save the union. actions/cache never prunes, cargo never GCs `target/`, so entries grow monotonically — measured `Linux-cargo-*` 491MB → 819MB in 16h, `Linux-cargo-openapi-*` 375MB → 730MB in 27h — against a 10GB repo quota that is currently **over** (11,453 MiB / 10,240 MiB).

### The fix

`Swatinem/rust-cache` keys on the job id (kills the collision), prunes stale artifacts before saving (kills the growth), and skips workspace crates. `save-if: main` matters: caches are **branch-scoped**, so saving on every PR ref is what blew the quota. PRs still restore main's cache, which is the entire win. (A Cargo.lock-changing PR is not left cold — the lock hash is only in the exact key, never the restore key.)

### Fuzzing was the critical path of every PR

678s wall: **519s (76%) uncached container build, 123s actual fuzzing**, for one 191-byte harness, on every PR including docs and SDK ones.

Now skipped for trees that cannot reach it. Deliberately `paths-ignore` rather than an allowlist of crates: the target reaches `crw-extract → crw-core → crw-mcp-proto` and fuzzes `htmd::convert`, whose version lives in the **root `Cargo.toml`** — so an allowlist would silently skip fuzzing on a dependency bump, the most fuzz-relevant change we get, and there is no cron leg to catch what a PR filter drops. Verified every path that feeds the harness (root Cargo.toml/lock, all three crates, `.clusterfuzzlite/`, `fuzz/`, the workflow itself) still triggers it.

### Also

- **concurrency groups** — a force-push (our normal rebase flow) left the superseded run to finish, burning ~26 runner-min and writing cache entries that compete for the quota. Guarded so main-push runs never cancel each other; `release.yml` already had one and is untouched.
- **timeouts** — there were none anywhere (default 360). conformance gets 40 because the first run on a new cache key is a full `lto = true, codegen-units = 1` build; the uncached release binaries measure ~10 min, so that is ~2.5x.
- **`CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=line-tables-only`** on `check` only — keeps file:line in panic backtraces (how we diagnose a CI-only failure) while dropping the rest. A true no-op for the release-building jobs (`strip = true` already).
- **conformance's readiness loop** fell through after 30 failed probes and ran the comparison against a dead server, reporting a confusing diff instead of "the server never came up".

### Expected

PR wall clock **11m18s → ~6m30s** on PRs that skip fuzzing, and lower again once `check` stops rebuilding 616 crates. The `~4m` figure is extrapolated from the 616-vs-10 crate delta, not measured — the crate delta is measured.

### Not in this PR

`release.yml` is untouched on purpose. Its `buildkit-blob` cache (`cache-to: type=gha,mode=max`) writes into the **tag ref's** scope — verified live: 1896 MiB under `refs/tags/v0.25.0`, 1896 MiB under `refs/tags/v0.25.1`, **zero under main**, so no tag run can ever read another's and the 3.8GB is write-only. Dropping it, sharing the dev-profile cache between the two `check` jobs, and giving `publish-crates` a barrier so nothing irreversible publishes before the killable work lands, are a separate PR — they need measuring, not reasoning.

Legacy `Linux-cargo-*` caches get swept after this merges; nothing restores them once these four blocks are gone.

author: jackneil
body:
## What this is

The kid-creator loop becomes visible in the app: games marked `madeByKid: true` (the marker make-a-game/remix-a-game already write) now get a **"🌟 My Games" shelf** at the top of the home page with a live personal-best stat per card, a **"🛠️ Games I Made"** section on the profile, and a warm invite card when the shelf is empty. The profile's played-games list renames to "Games I've Played" so one label never means two different things. Rider: signup password minimum 6 -> 8 (SECURITY_BACKLOG item 2), enforced server-side with client mirror.

## How it works

- **One source of truth, two existing channels**: the `madeByKid` literal in each game's `metadata.ts` flows through the runtime regex scan (`game-registry.ts` -> `DisplayItem` -> home shelf, instant in dev) and the build-time generator (`gameMetadata.generated.ts` -> profile, refreshed each build). Byte-identical regex + defaults on both sides, so home and profile can never disagree; the generator now also mirrors the runtime id->dirname fallback.
- **Personal-best stats without new state**: new `shared/lib/localProgress.ts` probes the repo's real storage-key conventions, unwraps the zustand persist envelope, and feeds the (promoted-to-shared) `gameStatExtractor`. Never throws: corrupt/missing saves read as "never played" and the card shows always-true invite copy instead of a claim that can be wrong.
- **Shared-device safety is structural**: convention-probed keys must pass `isClearedOnSignOut` (the shelf can never display account progress a sign-out wouldn't wipe), and an owner-marker guard mirrors the upload path (a surviving marker for someone else hides stats). Device-owned saves are an explicit, documented exemption.
- **The flagship card actually works**: Four-Wheeler Adventure (Hank's real creation) saves under its own `fwa_myland_v1` format inside a srcDoc iframe. It's a device-owned alias with a dedicated extractor case (plots owned + buildings, including the game's legacy owned-backfill), so the card shows a real "My Land: N plots" stat - proven end to end in a browser by invoking the game's own `saveMyLand()` inside the iframe and watching the shelf read it.
- **Routing has one owner**: `hrefForCategory` extracted into `app-routing.ts`; the four inline app-vs-game ternaries (GamesIMade, registry, GameProgressCard) all collapsed onto it.

## Review

Two-wave recursive DCR: 7 reviewers wave 1 (5 lens pairs incl. Fable security + Fable frontend-design with live browser access, plus a pre-mortem analyst), 2 re-checkers wave 2. 0 CRITICAL; 6 validated MEDIUMs, all fixed and re-verified clean: five stale doc pointers to the moved gameStatExtractor, the duplicated route ternary, the inert flagship stat (now live), the silent-marker checklist gap (madeByKid + storage-suffix rules now in the numbered New Game/App Checklist and make-a-game's anti-rationalization table), the stranded one-card desktop shelf (count-adaptive grid), and unprotected kid-typed names (break-words). Security + Access Control CLEAN on the Fable pass (no XSS/prototype-pollution/DoS path from crafted blobs; no cross-user read/write; existing accounts can't be locked out). Advisory LOWs were folded rather than shipped: typeof-password 400 guard, poisoned-blob test, structural clear-gate invariant test, legacy-save parity.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test`: **86 files / 441 tests passing** (master baseline 430 at branch; +11 covering the parser contract, localProgress conventions vs the REAL key names, shelf states, owner guard, the real four-wheeler id, and the password boundary at exactly 7/8)
- lint 0 errors - tsc clean - build green - generated lookup in sync (tree clean post-build); pre-push hook re-ran the full gate on push
- Live browser QA (desktop + 390px): populated shelf with real My Land stat, centered single-card layout, empty-state invite, search hides shelf while creations stay findable, no horizontal overflow, console 0 errors. Captures in `design/audits/screenshots/shelf-*.jpeg`
- Design doc: `design/MY_GAMES_SHELF.html`

## Next phases (tracked, not dropped)

Creator achievements in the trophy case; publish-share hardening (unguessable share URL, generic og:title, unpublish path, free-text PII guard); non-reader mode (read-aloud + icon-first instructions).
