body:
## What

PR 6 for #430 — hardening fixes from an architecture-risk review (repo's `architecture-review` skill, plan-review mode, timing `after`) of the whole five-PR stack against `docs/plans/issue-430-multi-conversation.md`. **Stacked on #439.** All behavior-preserving; the chat store's #332/#334/cap unit tests pass **unchanged**.

**Invariant bugs (found by the review, fixed with tests):**
- `adoptLegacySeat` could re-issue retired agent number 1: its guard ("agentNumbers empty + meta for 1") was a proxy for "migration ran", also true after a post-#430 user deletes every conversation. `loadPixelAgentsWorkspace` now returns `{ record, migratedFromLegacy }` and adoption runs only on an actual migration.
- `saveAgentSeats` persisted seat meta under **any** iframe-supplied integer key — resurrecting retired seats after `retireAgentNumber` and growing `agentMeta` (replayed into every bootstrap) forever. Seats are now filtered host-side to currently-assigned numbers; the sandbox boundary owns semantic validation.

**Seam hardening:**
- **Branded conversation-state patches**: the active-slice mirrors were kept consistent only by the convention that mutations flow through `patchConversationState`. The patch type is now branded (type-level unique symbol, zero runtime shape change) and `ConversationActionsContext.setState` accepts only branded patches — a future action author *cannot* hand-roll `setState({ conversations: … })`. One scoped `setCooldownUntil` escape hatch for the sole legitimate non-conversation write.
- **`ConversationRunRegistry`** (new, app-core): the `''` placeholder run key, re-key-on-resolve, release-by-identity, and cap arithmetic were one protocol split across two packages, held together by comments — the review's top regret. The registry is its single owner; the store holds one instance, `sendConversationPromptAction` takes `{ handle, registry }`. Deliberately its own dependency-free module so the entry-chunk cost is just this file. *Investigated and documented*: the entry chunk's static app-core edge **pre-existed** this stack (`SETTINGS_KEYS`/`defaultSettingsState`/`isPluginModule` are long-standing eager imports); this adds one binding to that existing edge, no new startup fetch (follow-up issue below).
- **Typed equality selector**: the JSON-stringify signature selector in `surfaces.tsx` is replaced by `useChatStoreWithEquality` + an exported `conversationSummariesEqual` (element-wise id/title/isRunning) — same render-skip behavior, no tuple-encode/decode coupling. Defined in the lazy chunk so `zustand/traditional` stays out of the entry.
- **Docs**: the plan records the `launchAgent` divergence (upstream's "+ Agent" button only renders in VS Code hosts, so office-driven launch is protocol-supported forward-compat; creation is switcher-only today), with a comment at the schema site so the acceptance isn't "cleaned up".

## Checks

typecheck 41/41 · app-core 139 + app-browser 608 + pixel-agents 42 + shell-app 3 unit tests · lint + root eslint on touched tests · `check:boundaries` · `format:check` · `pnpm knip` exit 0 · shell 8/8 + canvas 4/4 bundle guards (entry **shrank** 65.201 → 65.168 kB; app-core 123.111/126 kB) · e2e `multi-conversation` + `pixel-agents` chromium 10/10 with full rebuild.

- Host-side office "launch agent" affordance (vs switcher-only creation).
- `sendPrompt` returning a refusal result so non-surface callers (stage verbs) can surface the cap; today they silently no-op — as they already did pre-#430 whenever the single conversation was running.
- Informational: mirror-fields removal (compat shim with an expiry), 20-entry inspector ring under 3-way parallelism, making the app-core chunk *genuinely* lazy (pre-existing, above).

body:
Closes #86. Closes #87.

## What
The library exposed only a **tap** for verse selection; iOS uses a **long-press**. This adds long-press *alongside* tap so a consumer can use either — and makes the whole verse light up while pressing, matching iOS.

### Library (#86)
- `MushafView` / `MushafWithPlayerView` gain `onVerseLongPress`; `onVerseSelected` (tap) is unchanged. Verses use `combinedClickable` for tap + long-press.
- **Whole-verse press preview:** while a verse is pressed, every line-fragment of it highlights (a shared `pressedVerse` in `QuranPageView`, OR-ed into the highlight), instead of a per-fragment ripple on one line. Reuses the exact selection colour, so it's indistinguishable from a committed selection.
- **Disposal-safe clear:** if a pressed fragment scrolls out from under the finger, its release is never reported — so it's also cleared on disposal. The preview can never stick to a verse that scrolled away.
- New params are defaulted → the frozen **v0.1 fixture still compiles**; `apiDump` regenerated for the additive API change.

### Demo app (#87)
- Tap now shows a toast; **long-press bookmarks**. An accidental tap no longer toggles a bookmark, and the demo now exercises both library callbacks.

## Verified (on-device, API 33 + 37)
- Tap → reports exactly one verse + toast (the earlier "two verses" was `adb` synthetic-input noise, not a bug — confirmed with a real tap).
- Long-press → bookmarks, **no stuck highlight** after release.
- `mushaf-ui` instrumented regression suite passes.
- `apiCheck` green with the regenerated dump; v0.1 fixture compiles.

Before/after screenshots attached in a comment.

Targets `release/0.3.0`.

author: mike-thompson-day8
body:
## What

PR #6051's reentrant listener fan-out queue (`*listener-fanout-queue*` in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace/tooling.cljc`) is a **thread-local** dynamic binding, so it only orders **same-thread** nested emits. Two emits racing on two JVM threads each opened their own outermost fan-out and invoked the **same** registered listener callback concurrently.

This violated the public listener contract — `docs/api/re-frame.core.md`: *"Delivery is synchronous: the callback returns before the next record"* — and Spec 009 §The listener contract, which require synchronous, in-order, event-at-a-time delivery **per listener**. It also let B reach a listener before A even when A's emit began first, and exposed ordinary tool callbacks/appenders to concurrent invocation they were told cannot happen.

## The race (file:line)

- `tooling.cljc` outermost fan-out branch of `deliver-to-tooling!` — two threads each entered it concurrently (the queue is bound per-thread), running `fan-out-to-listeners!` at the same time.
- `fan-out-to-listeners!` invokes `(f event)` — the **same** registered callback `f`, overlapped across threads.

## The fix

Serialize the **outermost** fan-out — its transitive reentrant drain included — under a single process-global JVM monitor (`fanout-monitor`). Concurrent emits linearize on monitor-acquisition order; no listener callback ever overlaps itself; an emit still returns only after its record's callback completes (the monitor is held for the whole synchronous fan-out).

Same-thread reentrancy takes the enqueue branch and **never re-acquires** the monitor, so the rf2-1zxlsm reentrant ordering is preserved verbatim and there is no self-deadlock. CLJS is single-threaded — the `:cljs` arm runs the fan-out inline with no monitor, preserving production elision. Listener exception isolation, exact-continuation suppression (rf2-eaxnai), retentionless structural delivery (rf2-vxgfnd.244), and registration-replacement semantics are all untouched.

Scope is confined to `tooling.cljc` (the fan-out seam) + its regression test + a clarifying sentence in `docs/api/re-frame.core.md`. No `observation.cljc` or `spec/009` touch. No new error-id, so no Spec 009 catalogue row.

## Regression coverage

New JVM suite `implementation/core/test/re_frame/trace_listener_concurrent_serialization_test.clj`:

1. **Deterministic two-thread latch proof** (looped 50×): a listener blocks inside its A callback on one thread while B is emitted to the same listener on another. Asserts the callback never overlaps itself (max-concurrent == 1) and B is delivered strictly after A. With the monitor removed the test fails deterministically on every iteration (`max-conc 2`, log `[a-enter, b-enter, b-exit, a-exit]`).
2. **`^:stress` + registration churn**: 6 threads emit concurrently while a churn thread registers/unregisters a sibling listener; asserts no self-overlap, exact-once delivery, and no deadlock (no straggler threads).

## Quality gates

- `implementation/core` JVM (`clojure -M:test`): **2037 tests, 9599 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors**.
- `implementation/core` `^:stress` (`clojure -M:slow-test -n …`): new stress test green.
- `npm run test:cljs`: **9796 tests, 48148 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors**.
- Red-before confirmed: with the monitor disabled, the latch test fails deterministically across all 50 iterations; restored to green with the fix.

author: copilot
body:
The `patch-secrets` GitHub Actions job was failing before any cluster patching ran because `bitwarden/sm-action@v2` could not parse the workflow’s multiline `secrets` input. This change removes the invalid line so the workflow can load its Bitwarden mappings and continue.

- **Root cause**
  - `bitwarden/sm-action` expects each line in `with.secrets` to be a strict:
    ```text
    <secretGuid> > <environmentVariableName>
    ```
  - The workflow included an inline comment in that block, which caused the action to abort during input parsing.

- **Change**
  - Removed the non-mapping comment line from `.github/workflows/k3s-patch-secrets.yml`.
  - Left all secret UUID-to-environment-variable mappings unchanged.

- **Impact**
  - Restores execution of the `patch-secrets` job past the Bitwarden bootstrap step.
  - Avoids altering workflow behavior beyond fixing the parser failure.

- **Relevant snippet**
  ```yaml
  secrets: |
    e2f18624-762c-4818-a929-b448013205f9 > MINECRAFT_RCON_PASSWORD
    a1bd5f02-8bda-4483-9e42-b48a00db55bb > CHATTO_NATS_TOKEN
    c8912b62-3473-43b7-a54a-b48a00db7568 > CHATTO_COOKIE_SIGNING_SECRET
  ```

body:
## 概要

[docs/adding-a-provider.md](../blob/main/docs/adding-a-provider.md) の手順に沿って、Anthropic Claude（Messages API）プロバイダを追加します。消費側（Title/Tag/Chat/Admin/Config）のコードは無変更で、`ProviderRegistry::withDefaults()` への登録と管理画面の入力欄追加のみです。

## 実装のポイント

- **`AnthropicProvider`**（`AiProvider` + `ModelListingProvider`）
  - Anthropic 固有のワイヤ形状（`x-api-key` / `anthropic-version`、content ブロック、`/v1/models`）をクラス配下に閉じ込め
  - **構造化出力**: Messages API にネイティブの JSON Schema 出力が無いため、`outputSchema` を `input_schema` とする単一ツールを `tool_choice` で強制（tool use 方式）。消費側からは OpenAI の json_schema 出力と同じ「JSON 文字列の text」に見える
  - **画像**: URL ソースの image ブロックへ変換（`VisionInput` 対応）
- **`AnthropicStreamParser`**: SSE → 中立 `StreamEvent` の純粋パーサ（チャンク境界の吸収）。リクエスト不正時に Anthropic が返す「SSE ではない素の JSON エラー」もプロバイダ側で error イベントへ変換
- **`AnthropicErrorMessage`**: エラー type → 利用者向け日本語メッセージ（OpenAiErrorMessage と同型）
- **`ConversationStore`**（新規・プロバイダ非依存）: ガイド「会話継続トークンの扱い」の方式。サーバー側に会話状態を持たないプロバイダ向けに、継続トークン（32桁hex・クライアント由来値は検証して破棄）→ 履歴を本体 temp キャッシュ（TTL 1h・直近24メッセージ）で復元・保存。フロント・消費側は従来どおり不透明トークンのみ
- **`GET/AI/Admin`** が `configured`（`isConfigured()`）を出力し、テンプレートからプロバイダ固有の config キー判定（`{ai_api_key}/em` 等）を排除

## テスト

- 38 本追加（provider のリクエスト変換/応答解析/エラー変換、stream parser のワイヤ列検証、conversation store、registry 解決）
- `composer check`（phpcs 55ファイル / PHPStan level6+strict / PHPUnit **98 tests, 231 assertions**）緑
- 管理画面 UI はローカル実機で描画確認済み（プロバイダ選択肢・Anthropic API KEY 欄・モデル行のメッセージ）

## 動作確認手順

1. 管理画面「AI」でプロバイダに Anthropic (Claude) を選択し、Anthropic API KEY を保存
2. モデル一覧が `/v1/models` から取得されるので選択して保存
3. エントリー編集でタイトル/タグ生成、AIアシスタントでチャット（マルチターン継続）を確認

## 備考

- 実 API キーでの疎通は未実施（ユニットテストでワイヤ形式を固定済み）
- 続編として Gemini / OpenAI互換(さくら) を同型の PR で予定

author: dormammu1997
body:
SL Hunting knowledge v3m — Intraday Hunter's **17 Jul** session (`xTwmjkvkrQQ` 8:07) and prediction clip (`hGWenJz7Us4` 2:43), his **first losing day in this series**, cross-checked against the agent journal and the runner log.

Knowledge-only; targets `main` (the health-gate fix motivated by the same day is [#67](https://github.com/DoRmAmMu1997/My-Algo-Trading-Code/pull/67), on the MAT chain where that code lives).

## The day

All three indices opened **flat** after another small-momentum day with the closing point uncrossed. Per his pre-open plan (flat → go WITH the prior selling) IH sold the first positive push, naming the invalidation before entry (*"this resistance must not cross; BankNIFTY must not go up"*). The market broke out upward instead — Sensex/NIFTY first, and when BankNIFTY joined, he **cut at his loss limit**. No averaging, no panic flip: *"don't book a small loss and hurriedly build a CALL trade — you may flip and the market turns back down"*; *"when you're wrong, the market does what you did NOT plan for"*; *"the brain only works right when the trade is going right — when it's wrong, look at the limit and leave."*

## Agent vs IH — not comparable on premise

IH took 1 trade (a loss). The agent took **zero** — the market-data health gate blocked ALL entries (paper included) through the opening window (gates reopened 09:24–09:29; IH entered ~09:16; the agent's LLM ran from 09:16 but no order could land). That operational bug is fixed in #67. The block accidentally "saved" the agent from a likely losing day — luck, not design.

## Net-new encoded

1. **`GIFT-GAP AFTER A NOBODY'S-CROWD DAY`** (`RETAIL_POSITIONING`, from the prediction clip). After a small-momentum day whose closing point was never crossed, BOTH sides are thin — nobody meaningfully positioned overnight. A gap in **either** direction is then a *gift that traps its own recipient*: a gap-up makes the few buyers feel "it's all mine" so they sit (and add) instead of booking — fade it with sell-side setups on confirmation; a gap-down mirrors for sellers. A **flat** open on such a day answers "whom do we hunt?" with *nobody* → go with the drift. Generalises v3k's seller-specific `FLAT-OPEN PARTICIPATION GATE` to the two-sided thin-inventory case; explicitly distinguished from it in the text.
2. **`NO INSTANT FLIP` extended to the LOSING side** (`RISK`, one clause on the existing bullet — IH's central lesson of the day). Booking a small loss to *instantly reverse* into the breakout that is hurting you is the classic whipsaw (the market often turns back right after). Exit at the limit / premise-invalidation; `POST-LOSS SPEED LIMIT` then governs the next entry.

**Deliberately NOT re-encoded:** limit-based loss exits, no averaging (structurally impossible for the agent), "control only the loss", and the thin-crowd entry premise itself (v3k/v3l — IH's premise WAS the encoded rule; the trade still lost, which is the "sound process, losing trade" case the knowledge already accepts). His pattern-free sell-the-first-push entry is what lost — evidence **for** keeping the agent's stricter mandatory pattern+confirmation entry rule; nothing was loosened.

## Verification

- `python -m pytest "Signal Generators/SL Hunting AI Agent/tests" -q` → **87 passed** (new marker `test_system_prompt_has_v3m_gift_gap_and_loss_flip_knowledge` plus every prior v2–v3l marker)
- Knowledge prose only — no schema/executor/order-path changes.

author: isaquepinheiro
body:
## Problem (diagnosis)

`TInject` keeps a single dependency-resolution stack, `FDependencyStack: TList<string>`, shared across **all** threads (`Source/Inject.pas:39`, mutated in `_PushDependency` / `_PopDependency` / `_CheckCircularDependency`).

A resolution chain is by nature **per-thread**. When multiple threads resolve concurrently (e.g. Horse worker threads sharing the global singleton injector), their push/pop interleave on the same list, so:

- two threads pushing the same service name see each other's entry → **false** `ECircularDependency` (`Circular dependency detected: X -> X`);
- concurrent `TList.Add`/`Delete` corrupt `FCount`/`FItems` → intermittent range errors / AV.

This is exactly the symptom the backend consumer reported in its PR #307 (`Circular dependency detected: TNidus -> TNidus`).

## Fix (option A2 — per-thread partition, minimal-semantic)

Replace the single shared list with a per-instance `TObjectDictionary<TThreadID, TList<string>>` guarded by a dedicated `TCriticalSection` that is held **only** for the dictionary get/create/remove. Each thread's stack is touched exclusively by its owning thread, so `push`/`pop`/`scan` run **lock-free on the hot path** — no serialization of resolves.

**Why not a `threadvar`:** a `threadvar` cannot be an instance field, and moving the stack to unit scope would change its scope from *per-injector* to *per-thread-global*, which could raise false positives when two different injector instances legitimately resolve the same class name within one chain. The per-instance dictionary preserves the **exact** original scoping — single-thread behavior is provably unchanged (one entry keyed by the main thread id).

**Why not one `TCriticalSection` around the whole resolver (option B):** it serializes every resolve process-wide, reintroducing the very contention that #307's connection pool removed.

**Leak-free:** each thread's stack is freed the instant its chain empties (outermost `_PopDependency`), so pooled worker threads never retain a list; the dictionary owns its values (`doOwnsValues`) and frees any residual on destroy. Verified under the backend suite's FastMM4 leak detection.

## Other shared state on the resolve path (evaluated)

`FTypeCache`/`FMethodCache` are already correctly guarded by `FRttiCacheLock`. One remaining race exists but is **out of scope** here: `FInstances` lazy-add in `GetTry`/`GetInterfaceTry` (`FInstances.ContainsKey`→`Add`) can race on the *first* concurrent resolve of a not-yet-instantiated lazy singleton. It produces a different failure mode (duplicate-key / dictionary AV), not the reported false-circular, and fixing it touches the base container (`Inject.Container`) more invasively. In practice binds are registered/instantiated during single-threaded bootstrap before requests are served. Recommended as a separate, focused follow-up.

## Proof

Deterministic repro added: `Test Delphi/ConcurrencyRepro.dpr` (8 threads, no DUnitX dependency, exit code = pass/fail):

| Source | Result |
|--------|--------|
| **unpatched** | FAIL in round 1 — **94907** failures; first error `ECircularDependency: Circular dependency detected: TLeafA -> TLeafA` |
| **patched** | **PASS** — 0 failures across 50 rounds (8,000,000 concurrent resolves), stable across repeated runs |

Regression suite (`Test Delphi/PTestInjectContainer.dpr`, DUnitX) stays green: **10/10** (was 9/9). The added `TestConcurrentResolveIsThreadSafe` is a genuine guard — it fails **9/10** on the old code (126645 failures) and passes on the fix.

Validated in the backend consumer (`developer-friends-backend`, ~4776-test suite, dcc64/Win64 + FastMM4): the #307 workaround stays in place (defense in depth); this only proves the fix breaks nothing.

Use a **conventional commit** title — it becomes the release version on merge:

| Title prefix | Release bump | Example |
|--------------|--------------|---------|
| `fix:` | patch (1.5.5 → 1.5.6) | `fix: correct Content-Length parsing` |
| `feat:` | minor (1.5.5 → 1.6.0) | `feat: add rate limiter middleware` |

| `chore:`, `ci:`, `docs:` | no release tag | `chore: update workflows` |

author: jasmine-nguyen
body:
## What

The app already leaves transfers / card payments / home-loan movements out of budgets (the bank's `counts_to_budget` flag), but nothing told the user. This surfaces it — read-only, client-only, no server change.

- **List row** → a quiet grey **"Not in budget"** tag on any charge that doesn't count (bank-excluded *or* user-excluded), styled like the existing Pending pill.
- **Transaction detail** → for a **bank-excluded** charge, a read-only **"Excluded (transfer)"** note replaces the WHIT-296 manual toggle (the toggle can't un-exclude a bank transfer, so it would be inert). A normal charge keeps the toggle so the user can still exclude it themselves.

## How

- `src/context.tsx` → new `excluded` field on `TransactionView` = `!contributesToBudget(t)` (the existing single source of truth). Drives the row tag.
- `src/components/TransactionRow.tsx` → the "Not in budget" pill (accessible label "Not counted in budgets").
- `app/transaction/[id].tsx` → `BudgetExcludedNote`, shown when `counts_to_budget` is falsy; toggle otherwise.

The detail note gates on the same "doesn't count" test the row tag uses, so the list and the detail screen can never disagree (this also closes a divergence when the flag is missing).

## Review note — the divergence QA caught

The first cut of this change decided the detail screen's note-vs-toggle with a strict `counts_to_budget === false`, while the list row's tag used `!contributesToBudget(t)` (bank **or** user exclusion). The QA pass flagged these as **two different tests for the same idea**: if a charge ever arrived with `counts_to_budget` missing, the list would tag it "Not in budget" while the detail showed an OFF toggle — the two screens contradicting each other on the same charge. The fix that landed here gates the detail on the **same** falsy-`counts_to_budget` test, so the list and detail can never disagree. (This is what the "closes a divergence when the flag is missing" line above refers to.)

## Design note

For a bank-detected exclusion the label reads "Excluded (transfer)" and the manual toggle is hidden by design (a bank transfer can't be manually re-included). Charges the user excludes themselves keep the toggle.

## Tests

New logic + screen tests, each proven to fail if the fix is reverted:
- `transactionViewExcluded.logic.test.ts` + `transactionViewExcludedEdges.logic.test.ts` — the `excluded` flag and its edge combinations (bank+user, income, uncategorized, pending, missing flag).
- `TransactionRow.screen.test.tsx` + `TransactionRowExcluded.screen.test.tsx` — the row tag renders / doesn't, across the same edges + a11y + selection mode.
- `transactionEdit.screen.test.tsx` + `transactionDetailExcludedEdges.screen.test.tsx` — the note-vs-toggle swap and the missing-flag consistency (the divergence above).

Full suite green (logic 682 · screen 863), typecheck clean, coverage 98.7% (floor 30%).

author: stonecypher
body:
## Summary

`rollup.config.js` hardcoded `output.name` as the package name `'fsl-textmate'`, but the `iife` output requires a legal JS identifier and a hyphen isn't one:

```
[!] RollupError: Given name "fsl-textmate" is not a legal JS identifier.
```

Camel-cases it to `'fslTextmate'` across the es/cjs/iife outputs (`name` is unused for es/cjs but kept consistent).

## Verification

Full `npm run build` now passes end to end: rollup emits `index.mjs`/`index.cjs`/`index.iife.js`, `attw --pack` reports **No problems found 🌟**, and 43 tests pass (39 unit + 4 stochastic).

## Note

This is a **template bug**, not specific to fsl-textmate — the template derives the bundle's JS global from the raw package name, so any repo whose name contains a hyphen breaks identically. Worth fixing upstream in the template (camel-case the name there).

body: ### Proposed Changes Fixes the UVE inline block editor not filling 100% of the sidebar drawer height (only ~500px was used, leaving empty space above the Cancel/Save footer). **Root cause** - The new block editor (`dot-block-editor`, `@dotcms/new-block-editor`) had no "fill parent" layout mode. Its scroll surface (`.editor-scroll-container`) was hardcoded to `height: 500px` via an inline `[style]` binding, and the panel wasn't a flex column. - The legacy editor filled the drawer thanks to a parent `::ng-deep .editor-wrapper { height: 100% !important }` override. The new editor no longer renders an `.editor-wrapper` element (the height moved onto `.editor-scroll-container`), so that override was **dead CSS** for it — and couldn't beat an inline `[style]` binding anyway. **Fix** - Added a `fillHeight` input (`booleanAttribute`, default `false`) to `DotCMSEditorComponent`. When `true`: - the host becomes a full-height flex column (`:host(.dot-block-editor--fill-height)`), - the wrapper/panel become a flex column chain (`flex flex-col`, `flex-1 min-h-0`), - the scroll surface uses `flex: 1; min-height: 0` instead of the fixed 500px — mirroring the existing **fullscreen** layout, so the toolbar buttons and the stats/word-count bar keep their natural height and the editing surface consumes the rest. - `dot-block-editor-sidebar` passes `[fillHeight]="true"` and its `.container` is now a proper flex column (editor grows, footer keeps its natural height via `flex: 0 0 auto`). No more magic `calc(100% - 4rem)`. - Scoped the now-dead `.editor-wrapper` `::ng-deep` override to the **legacy** editor only. **Unchanged** - Standalone / Edit Contentlet content-field usage keeps its existing fixed, user-resizable height (`fillHeight` defaults to `false`). - Fullscreen mode is unaffected. ### Screenshots / Recording ### This PR fixes: #36620 ### Checklist - [x] Tests (updated `dot-block-editor-sidebar` spec to assert `fillHeight` is passed) - [x] Lint passes (`new-block-editor`, `portlets-edit-ema-portlet`) - [x] Unit tests pass (`new-block-editor`, `dot-block-editor-sidebar`) - [ ] Manual QA in the UVE 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) This PR fixes: #36620

## Overview

Switches the design language from neumorphism to clean **Minimalism**, adds a proper **sticky navbar**, makes the **search work site‑wide**, and hardens the **feedback counter**.

## 1. Minimalism redesign (`globals.css`)
- White canvas, thin `1px` borders, one restrained green accent, generous whitespace, flat cards with a subtle hover lift + shadow. No heavy shadows/gradients.
- Every surface restyled (all class names preserved): navbar, hero, stat row, search, most‑asked (now light bordered cards with a green category label), category plates (selected = green border + tint), cards/chips, article source/vote, admin dashboard.

## 2. Navbar + hero
- New sticky, blurred minimal **navbar**: brand mark + nav links (الرئيسية / الفئات / كل المواضيع) + a search box. Replaces the old large header.
- The big heading, tagline, stats, and main search moved into a **hero** section in `HomeClient`. Added `#cats` and `#results` anchors (with `scroll-padding-top` for the sticky nav).

## 3. Search — now works everywhere
- The navbar search is a native `GET` form to `/?q=…` (works without JS, from any page).
- `page.tsx` reads `searchParams.q` and passes it to `HomeClient` as `initialQ`; the hero search remains live/instant. Both drive the same filter.

## 4. "قالوا «أفادتني»" feedback counter
- The vote → `/api/feedback` → `recordVote` → `feedback.json` → homepage‑sum pipeline is correct and works on a persistent server (VPS) / locally.
- Made `recordVote` **resilient to a read‑only filesystem** so votes no longer 500 on Vercel.
- ⚠️ **Persistent counts on Vercel** still require moving the store to **Vercel KV/Postgres** (Vercel's filesystem is ephemeral — already flagged in `CLAUDE.md`). Happy to do that ~small `store.ts` swap if you connect a KV store to the project.

## Files
- `src/app/globals.css` — minimalist design system (rewrite)
- `src/app/layout.tsx` — sticky navbar (replaces header)
- `src/components/HomeClient.tsx` — hero + `initialQ` + section anchors
- `src/app/page.tsx` — pass `searchParams.q` → `initialQ`
- `src/lib/store.ts` — resilient feedback write

## Verification
Layout verified with headless Chromium (navbar, hero, cards, selected‑plate state, contrast). Next build validated by Vercel CI on this PR.

author: maebeale
body:
🤖 suggested review level: 3 Read 📖 small POSIX-sh port-cleanup change in two conductor scripts, no app logic

### What is the goal of this PR and why is this important?
- The archive hook killed only the *first* listener on each workspace port via a quoted `kill "$pid"`, which passed `lsof`'s newline-joined multi-PID output as a single argument and silently failed.
- Puma cluster workers (and `bin/vite dev`'s esbuild children) were left orphaned — still bound to the port — and collided with the next workspace to recycle the block. This is the same leak we just fixed in festilite.

### How did you approach the change?
- Added a `free_ports` reaper to both `bin/conductor-archive` and `bin/conductor-server`: word-split the PID list, SIGTERM each, then SIGKILL survivors after a grace beat.
- `conductor-server` now frees `PORT`/`PORT+36` on boot too, so a ghost from a crashed session self-heals instead of failing to bind.

### Anything else to add?
- POSIX-sh only; `sh -n` clean. No Ruby/app changes.

author: streax0
body:
🎯 **What:** 
Replaced insecure pseudo-random number generator function `mt_rand` and `array_rand` with the cryptographically secure `random_int` function in `includes/functions.php`.

⚠️ **Risk:** 
If left unfixed, attackers could potentially predict random values generated by `mt_rand` and `array_rand` due to their non-cryptographic nature. This can lead to exploitation vectors in processes relying on this randomness, such as deterministic bypasses or predictability in sampling distributions (e.g. rate limit cache cleanup or random test question selection).

🛡️ **Solution:** 
Swapped `mt_rand()` and `array_rand()` with robust implementations leveraging `random_int()` which uses the system's secure randomness sources (CSPRNG), ensuring unpredictability and enhanced security.

author: davidecarvalho
body:
## Native to-many aggregate fields

Sort and filter root rows by an aggregate of a one-to-many / many-to-many collection via a virtual sub-path — no hand-written computed field needed.

```ts
// sort + filter, uniform via dot-notation
sort=-posts.$count
posts.$sum.views[gt]=100
filterQuery().sortDesc('posts.$count').where('posts.$sum.views', 'gt', 100)
// $count, $sum.<col>, $avg.<col>, $min.<col>, $max.<col>  (numeric child columns)
```

- **Correlated scalar subqueries** in both adapters (TypeORM param-free) — no row multiplication, pagination-safe. Many-to-many correlates through the pivot/junction table (join is *inside* the subquery).
- **Auto-discovered** from ORM metadata under `autoFields: true` (no `allowed` list), subject to the block-list; only real **numeric** child columns qualify for `$sum/$avg/$min/$max`; the client value is always bound as a parameter.
- **Empty collection:** `$count`→0, `$sum`→0 (COALESCE), `$avg`/`$min`/`$max`→NULL.
- **Typed** `number` in the generated `filterQuery()`, pruned by `maxDepth` (aggregate = one relation hop). Codegen gating matches runtime (autoFields/allowed).

## Also in this PR
- **Removed the `{alias}` string-token substitution** in both adapters — computed string sources are emitted verbatim; a correlated subquery in a *computed* field must use the function form `({ alias }) => ...`. (Technically breaking; shipped in the minor.)
- **Reframed computed docs** as *virtual columns that don't exist in a table* (e.g. `fullName`), not the to-many-aggregate workaround.
- **Removed all flip-domain examples** from the docs (neutral User/posts, Author/books, User/tags).

## Quality
Built subagent-driven (TDD per task, review after each, opus whole-branch review = READY TO MERGE, injection-safe, both adapters symmetric). Full workspace green: **1235 tests** (core 560, mikro-orm 207, typeorm 156, codegen 31, client 269, react 12). Changeset: minor for `nestjs-filter` / `-mikro-orm` / `-typeorm` / `-codegen`.

Non-blocking follow-ups (backlog): `blocked` not honored in codegen (pre-existing upstream-wide); composite-PK correlates on the first PK column only (document as a single-column-PK limitation); many-to-many non-owning side untested.

- `node-ci.yml`'s `library-repo: bymaxone/nest-core` input now clones and builds the sibling library automatically, replacing the manual clone+build step.
- `has-web`, `run-e2e-api`, `run-export-audit` and `run-mutation` are off for now since `apps/web`, the e2e suite, the export-audit script, and Stryker mutation config don't exist yet; each will be flipped on when its own phase lands (noted in the corresponding phase docs).
- Aligned `package.json` scripts to the standard Bymax `test` / `test:cov` convention so the reusable's default `unit-command` (`pnpm test:cov`) resolves: split `apps/api`'s `test` (no coverage) from `test:cov` (100% coverage gate), and added root `test:api`, `test:cov`, `test:cov:api`.
- `.github/workflows/codeql.yml` and `.github/workflows/scorecard.yml` are left untouched — a deliberate deviation from the sibling repos (which rely on GitHub's default CodeQL setup) so code scanning is guaranteed to self-activate on the public-visibility flip without a repo-settings dependency.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
### Why these changes are being introduced

Over time, our codebase has accumulated obsolete placeholder files and dead interface views that are no longer part of the live application flow. Because our previous automated check only scanned core processing modules, these unused files went unnoticed. This caused developer confusion—with engineers occasionally modifying dead components—and increased overall onboarding friction.

To address this, we have expanded our existing analysis script to cover the user interface directories. By ensuring that only active, operational files remain in the workspace and blocking pull requests that introduce orphaned UI code, we keep the repository clean and maintainable. This was achieved without adding any new third-party dependencies, satisfying our strict security policy.

---

### Key Decisions & Rationale

- **Zero-Dependency Script Expansion:** Instead of introducing new packages that would require security audits and dependency log updates, we updated our existing `scripts/dead-code.js` (powered by `ts-prune`) to monitor `src/taskpane/components/` alongside existing core directories.
- **Fail-Fast CI Pipeline:** The dead-code check has been shifted early in the continuous integration process (`.github/workflows/main.yml`). This provides developers with immediate feedback on orphaned files before running slower, more resource-intensive testing and compilation stages.
- **Safe Removal of Confirmed Dead Code:** Rather than just flagging existing violations, we permanently deleted the legacy flat-files and unused UI components to establish a clean, passing baseline.

---

### Detailed Changes

#### 1. Codebase Verification Script (`scripts/dead-code.js`)
- Added `src/taskpane/components/` to the monitored directories.
- Retained the exclusion rules for unit test files (`test`, `__tests__`, `.test.`) to preserve standalone test configurations.
- Configured the script to exit with a non-zero code (`1`) on detection of orphaned exports, successfully failing the integration build if unused code is introduced.

#### 2. Legacy File & Placeholder Clean-up
- **Orphaned UI Components (Deleted):**
  - `src/taskpane/components/TextInsertion.tsx`
  - `src/taskpane/components/HeroList.tsx`
  - `src/taskpane/components/Header.tsx`
  - `src/taskpane/components/ControlPanel.tsx` (unused orchestrator remnant)
  - `src/taskpane/components/views/useExcelTelemetry.ts` (orphaned telemetry hook)
- **Unused Presentational Sub-Exports:**
  - Removed unused exports inside `src/taskpane/components/ui/DesignSystem.tsx` (including `Button` and `Card`).
- **Empty Legacy Flat-Files (Deleted):**
  - `src/taskpane/core/parser.ts`
  - `src/taskpane/core/generator.ts`

#### 3. Continuous Integration (`.github/workflows/main.yml`)
- Moved the `💀 Dead Code Check` step to execute immediately after dependency installation, providing fast validation feedback.

author: su3h7am
body:
## Summary

Four small, independent fixes bundled together since they're all build/data
hygiene rather than logic changes:

**1. Broken model download URLs (the important one)**

Both `data/models.json` entries and the hardcoded default in `main.cpp` used
filenames with a `parakeet-`/`parakeet_` prefix (e.g.
`parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-q8_0.gguf`, `parakeet_realtime_eou_120m-v1-q8_0.gguf`)
that don't actually exist in the `mudler/parakeet-cpp-gguf` HuggingFace repo —
the real files are `tdt-0.6b-v3-q8_0.gguf` and
`realtime_eou_120m-v1-q8_0.gguf` (no such prefix). Verified against the repo's
actual file listing and confirmed with `curl -I`: the old URLs return `404`,
the corrected ones return `302` (redirect to LFS storage).

In practice this meant the in-app "Download TDT 0.6B v3 (HF)" button and the
`models.json` catalog were both pointing at dead links — the download feature
didn't work at all.

**2. Floating `parakeet.cpp` git ref**

`KEA_PARAKEET_GIT_TAG` was `"master"`. Every from-scratch build fetches
whatever upstream `master` currently is, so builds aren't reproducible and
can silently break with no change on Kea's side. Pinned to a specific commit
(`1da853421de9710cbe894a0110711de5a0516486`, upstream's current `master` HEAD
at the time of this PR). Bump deliberately (and re-test) when picking up
upstream changes.

**3. `enable_testing()` location**

Was called from inside `src/CMakeLists.txt`, several targets down. Moved to
the top-level `CMakeLists.txt` right after the C++ standard settings, so
`ctest` is guaranteed to be configured regardless of subdirectory processing
order.

**4. Tray/window/desktop icon**

`preferences-desktop-locale` reads as a keyboard-layout/locale icon, not a
dictation app. Changed to `audio-input-microphone` (confirmed present in the
Breeze icon theme) in the tray, the window icon, and the `.desktop` file's
`Icon=` key.

## Test plan

- [x] `cmake -B build -DKEA_BUILD_PARAKEET=OFF && cmake --build build` — builds clean
- [x] `ctest` — all 4 tests pass
- [x] `curl -I` on both corrected model URLs — `302` (was `404` before the fix)
- [x] `data/models.json` still parses as valid JSON
- [x] Confirmed `audio-input-microphone` exists in the installed Breeze theme

Note: this touches `org.kde.kea.desktop`, which PR #1 (app ID rename) renames
to `io.github.su3h7am.kea.desktop`. Whichever of the two merges second will
need a small rebase to carry the icon change over to the new filename.

author: commet
body:
공정 O3 · 겨냥 퍼널 단계 accepted→surfaced

## 무엇
Boss 리뷰를 **MBTI 성격극에서 자리(seat)-우선 이해관계자 리뷰로 교체**했다 (O3 방3). 평가 문서 §4.4의 "personality-test theater" 경고와 R42 실측(헤드-투-헤드에서 살아남은 가치는 전부 SEAT에서, 4-글자 타입에서 0/5)이 근거다. R42는 이미 프롬프트 **규칙**을 고쳤지만 **구조**는 MBTI-우선으로 남아 있었다 — 이 PR이 구조를 뒤집는다.

## 구조 교체
| 전 | 후 |
|---|---|
| config `boss.required = ["mbti_code"]` — 타입이 신원 | `required: []` + 정본 = `role`·`owns`·`goals`·`authority` (자리의 목적함수) |
| 16타입 = 페르소나 본체 (입버릇·예시 대화 복창 강제) | 16타입 = **선택 tone 스킨** (목소리만; 주입 템플릿에서 `{{code}}` 자체 제거 → 누출 불가) |
| 보고 헤더 `## Argus - Boss - {{mbti_code}} {{name}}` — R42 자기 규칙("never surfaced") 위반 | 헤더에서 타입 라벨 제거, `{{name}} ({{role}})` |
| M2 게이트 = speech_patterns **exact phrase 강제** (성격극의 기계화) | M2 = **seat_basis 결정론 검사** — 모든 우려가 "어느 소유 지분을 위협하는가"를 스키마 필수 필드로 답해야 함 ("자리 없으면 우려 없다") |
| M7 "MBTI-based review is literally the differentiator" (R42와 정면 모순) | M7 = 차별점은 **책임**(accountability) — 소유가 없는 리뷰어는 통과 못 함 |
| configure가 2-question 퀴즈로 사용자를 16타입에 **매핑** | 자리 질문 한 턴 (owns가 최고가치 필드), 퀴즈 매퍼 은퇴 |

## 덤으로 잡은 스파인 모순
`dm-feedback.json`이 `concerns.minItems: 1`로 **우려 0개 금지**를 강제 — boss.md의 R42 절제 규칙("깨끗한 스캐폴드엔 `concerns: []`가 정직한 출력")과 정면 모순이라, 스키마가 우려 **제조**(over-fire)를 강요하고 있었다. minItems 폐기 + 설명 재작성.

## 하위호환
- legacy `boss.mbti_code` 키는 **tone 별칭**으로 계속 읽힌다 — 기존 config는 목소리 그대로 유지 (이 리포의 로컬 config가 legacy-키 경로의 살아있는 실증).
- 저장 필드 `mbti_type`은 이름 유지(리더 호환), 이제 tone 값 기록·표면 미노출.
- 잘못된 tone 코드는 이제 **차단이 아니라 스킨 생략** — 목소리 취향이 깨졌다고 이해관계자 리뷰가 막히면 안 된다.

## 가드
`seat-not-type.test.ts` 확장 (기존 R42 앵커 5개 전부 보존 + 신설 4): 스키마 required에 타입 없음 · seat 필드 5종 실재 · minItems 부재 + seat_basis 필수 · 타입 라벨/구 M7 문구/복창 게이트 부활 금지 · configure 매퍼 은퇴.

## 검증
- root vitest **249파일, 실패 0** (seat-not-type 9/9 포함) · argus-mcp **986/986** · 플러그인 배터리 6종 all green · `claude plugin validate` 양쪽 OK

author: winterfell2021
body:
## Summary

- replace a client-provided `X-Request-Id` on outbound calls with AxonHub's unique per-request `ar-*` ID
- keep the ID stable for retry attempts belonging to the same inbound request
- keep channel header overrides authoritative by applying them after the generated request ID
- add regression coverage for multiple inbound requests that reuse one client request ID

## Problem

AxonHub trace IDs can intentionally span multiple agent calls, while an HTTP request ID must identify one request. The generic inbound-header merge currently forwards `X-Request-Id` unchanged. If a client reuses that value to group an agent trace, independent outbound calls receive the same request ID.

Downstream gateways that use `X-Request-Id` for usage idempotency or deduplication can then collapse unrelated requests into one record, mixing models, statuses, token usage, and charges.

AxonHub already generates a unique `ar-*` request ID for every inbound HTTP request in `WithLoggingTracing`; it was not previously applied to the outbound provider request.

## Fix

Add an outbound raw-request middleware that sets `X-Request-Id` from AxonHub's request context after inbound headers are merged. Different inbound requests therefore get different downstream IDs even when the client reuses its own value. Retries for one request keep the same ID, and explicit channel header overrides can still replace it.

## Verification

- `go test ./...`
- `cd llm && go test ./...`

author: letsgettoworkbro
body:
## What

A six-auditor adversarial **refute** pass over everything merged since the last audit (#368–#411). Each auditor was tasked to *refute*, every lead was verified in the merged code before fixing, and each fix lands at the primitive with a revert-failing test (`test_audit_new_additions_2026_07_15.py` — 10 of 12 fail on revert; the other two are positive controls).

### CONFIRMED and fixed

- **Windows `calendar_ics` = arbitrary-file read + SSRF + OOM** (highest severity). `load_ics_sources` dereferenced every `config.calendar_ics` entry directly: any file path (`C:\Windows\…`, `\\server\share`, `..\..`, a drive root) was read and exfiltrated to the phone via `/dreamlayer/calendar`; any `http(s)` URL was fetched (`169.254.169.254` cloud metadata, the Brain's own loopback); reads were uncapped (a multi-GB file OOMs the sync thread). The Mac never had this — a Windows-only path bypassing the folder allow-list the design is built on, with a test even enshrining the unfiltered round-trip. **Fix:** file paths must pass `_is_allowed_root` (resolve()d — defeats `..`/symlink/UNC/drive-root); URL feeds must be **public https** (`is_local_endpoint` blocks loopback/link-local/RFC-1918); reads capped at `ICS_MAX_BYTES`.
- **`BrainConfig.save` was a plain unlocked `write_text`.** A torn write → `JSONDecodeError` → `load()` returns `cls()` **defaults**, silently dropping the wearer out of Incognito (`network_mode → "connected"`) and losing watched folders. **Fix:** tmp + atomic replace (rides out Windows share-mode contention too), cleaned up on failure.
- **Open Library rating was an unclamped float** from an untrusted response, feeding both the taste ranking score and the "N★" HUD string. A spoofed/MITM'd `ratings_average: 999999` (or `1e400`=inf) forced the attacker's book to win "BEST PICK" and print `inf★`. **Fix:** clamp to `[0,5]`, reject non-finite (the openfoodfacts sibling was already enum-bounded).
- **Juno reply card overflow.** `_multiline_text` had no line cap and no long-word break; an untrusted remote-API-brain reply (thousands of words, or one 5000-char run) painted ~190 lines over the whole disc. **Fix** at the shared primitive (protects all 13 callers): cap to `max_lines` with an ellipsis, hard-break an overlong run.
- **zeroconf `advertise()` broadcast the pairing token in the cleartext mDNS TXT record** — unauthenticated multicast any LAN device reads. **Fix:** advertise presence/host/port only; the token never goes on the wire.
- **logging `_sanitize` was dead code:** `format()` redacted only top-level sensitive keys, serialising a name/transcript nested under a benign key verbatim (a top-level-only test gave false confidence). **Fix:** wire `_sanitize` into the serialisable-extra path.
- **"Test connection" was a sibling call-site missing the egress contract:** a remote `api_test`/`cloud_test` fired the wearer's API key to a public host uncounted and even while incognito — contradicting the panel's own promise. **Fix:** judge locality on the effective base, refuse a remote test while incognito, count+log it otherwise (mirroring `_ask_cloud`).

### Held under refutation (verified, no change)

The Windows loopback-default + token-minting posture and auth/CSRF enforcement; the folder allow-list itself; JSON-store atomicity; the primary-API **answer path** (both new remote presets classified as egress + counted + veil-gated, locality recomputed per-ask, one-click discovery structurally localhost-only, and my earlier CSRF/Origin guard + API-key masking **survived the panel reskin**); the Open Library connector's capability + veil gating and non-SSRF-able URL; the phone relay veil gate and the **app-layer RFC-1918 cleartext scoping** (an auditor's "no scoping exists" was a stale-tree artifact — `cleartextAllowed()`/`isPrivateHost()` enforce it); and the memory forget/purge wiring (Phase-4 fix not regressed).

### Reported, not fixed (deferred / low-severity)

ChromaStore/Lance native ranking diverges from the linear fallback (a real correctness gap in an optional-dep path **not wired into the shipped Orchestrator** — #396's stated goal is unmet but unreachable in production); the JS `isLocalUrl` vs Python `is_local_endpoint` divergence (fail-safe — misleads the banner, no uncounted egress); message/brief notifications rendering content on the Android lock screen ungated by the veil (arguable inbound-mirroring vs outbound-pause). Happy to take any of these on.

## Testing

`cd host-python && python -m pytest src/dreamlayer/tests -q` → **3149 passed, 35 skipped**. `python -m mypy src/dreamlayer` → clean (611 files). ruff F,E9 clean. `test_audit_new_additions_2026_07_15.py`: 10/12 confirmed revert-failing.

## Checklist

- [x] Commits are signed off (DCO)
- [x] New optional capability? N/A
- [x] Nothing weakens the privacy contract — closes an arbitrary-file-read/SSRF path, a token broadcast, a nested-PII log leak, an incognito egress hole, and an untrusted-text overflow

author: sohumt123
body:
## Problem

`WarmupLR.__init__` validates `warmup_type` and falls back to `log` with a warning for unknown values, and `WarmupDecayLR` inherits that behavior. `WarmupCosineLR` documents the same `{'log', 'linear'}` contract but stores `warmup_type` unvalidated, and `get_lr_ratio()`'s warmup branch only assigns `ratio` for the two known types. Any other value (e.g. a typo like `'Linear'` or `'cosine'`) crashes on the first `step()`:

```
File "deepspeed/runtime/lr_schedules.py", line 850, in get_lr_ratio
    ratio = self.warmup_min_ratio + ratio * ratio_delta
UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'ratio' where it is not associated with a value
```

a confusing crash deep inside the scheduler instead of the documented warn-and-default behavior its sibling classes give.

## Fix

Normalize `warmup_type` in `WarmupCosineLR.__init__` exactly as `WarmupLR.__init__` already does (same warning text, same fallback to `log`). Behavior for valid `log`/`linear` values is unchanged.

## Testing

Added `test_warmup_cosine_lr_unknown_warmup_type_falls_back_to_log`, which fails with the `UnboundLocalError` above on current master and passes with this change; it asserts an unknown `warmup_type` produces the same lr-ratio trajectory as an explicit `log` scheduler through warmup and into cosine decay.

```
pytest tests/unit/runtime/test_lr_schedulers.py -k "warmup_cosine or reject_invalid"
9 passed, 45 deselected
```

yapf/flake8 clean on both touched files. Follows up on the recent scheduler hardening in #8126 and #8142, which did not cover `warmup_type`.

author: ssylla
body:
Brings release-notes-action's release machinery in line with next-version-action, and closes the Dependabot gap.

## Dependabot + CODEOWNERS
- `.github/dependabot.yml` — the "pinned by SHA, bumped by Dependabot" contract had nothing behind it. Enables the github-actions ecosystem (monthly, owned by ekwi-bot); `directory: "/"` also scans `action.yml`, where `git-cliff-action` is pinned.
- `.github/CODEOWNERS` (`@ssylla`) routes reviews — GitHub's replacement for dependabot's removed `reviewers:` option.
- **No `ignore`**: the ping-pong cycle with next-version-action is already broken on its side (next-version's own dependabot ignores this action), so watching next-version one-way here is the controlled Dependabot rollout, not a loop.

## Repin next-version-action → stable v0.1.0
- Was `v0.1.0-beta.1`; next-version shipped its stable, so this repo's release job now derives versions from the stable policy. A one-time catch-up — Dependabot maintains it from here.

## Release dispatch UX (mirror next-version-action)
- `workflow_dispatch` input `prerelease` (boolean) → `channel` (choice `pre-release | latest`). `latest` is GitHub's own word for the stable release it marks. next-version's boolean contract is unchanged — the choice maps to it inline.
- Release title dropped to the bare `${VERSION}` (tag stays `v`-prefixed). Same one-line change as PR #2, so the two merge without conflict in any order.

All four commits are `ci:` — squash-merge is fine.

⚠ For the assignee to take effect, **ekwi-bot needs write access** to this repo (Dependabot honours `assignees` only for write-access accounts).

## Summary
- add worker-store schema v9 with nullable `seq` columns on tool and LLM dispatch WAL rows
- assign one monotonic per-invocation sequence across both tables at completion-write time

- preserve model/tool interleaves before parallel-tool batch reconstruction
- share agent configuration and deterministic step-0 context setup between fresh and resumed invocations

## Acceptance criteria
- v9 schema documentation, migration wiring, populated-v8 migration coverage, and WAL key guard remain covered
- same-millisecond completion order is total-ordered in both directions by the shared sequence
- same-millisecond model/tool interleaves retain tool-batch boundaries

Implementation choice: completion writes calculate `MAX(seq) + 1` across both dispatch tables for the invocation. author: jarbasal
body:
Add the **sidon** engine: SARULab-Speech's Sidon speech-restoration model, restoring degraded 16 kHz speech to clean 48 kHz.

## What it is

Sidon is two neural stages:
- an 8-layer w2v-BERT 2.0 feature predictor (LoRA-adapted to denoise SSL representations), mapping SeamlessM4T log-mel features `[1, T, 160]` → hidden states `[1, T, 1024]` at 50 Hz;
- a DAC vocoder decoder (960× upsample) resynthesising a 48 kHz waveform.

Unlike the pure bandwidth-extension engines, Sidon does full restoration (denoise + resynthesis).

## How it fits the pure-ONNX contract

- Both stages exported to ONNX from upstream TorchScript (`sarulab-speech/sidon-v0.1`) by `conversion/export_sidon.py`; graph parity vs PyTorch ≤ 3e-6.
- The feature extractor is dynamic int8-quantized (795 → 200 MB); the decoder stays fp32 (210 MB).
- The SeamlessM4T mel front-end is reimplemented in numpy (`seamless_fbank`), parity ≤ 1e-5 vs `transformers.SeamlessM4TFeatureExtractor`, using bundled window / mel-filterbank arrays under `audiosronnx/data/`. Inference is onnxruntime-only — no torch at runtime.
- Chunked 96 s inference with the one-frame feature-cache seam, 50 Hz high-pass, peak-normalisation and decoder-tail trim, matching the reference pipeline.

Weights: `TigreGotico/audiosronnx-sidon` (public), pinned by revision.

## Cost

Heaviest shipped engine: ~410 MB, ~0.6× realtime on CPU (GPU-preferred). Fine for offline dataset cleansing.

## Tests

`test/test_e2e_sidon.py` — numpy front-end tests (no weights) plus e2e restoration and adversarial cases (silence, empty, single-sample, non-finite, extremely loud, multi-chunk seam). Registry test updated.

author: leo-klima-agents
body:
Follow-up to #2 (first commit landed on the branch just after #2 merged; rebased onto `main`).

## Changes

- **`data.yml` Run-workflow menu** gains two inputs alongside `pools`/`epochs`/`rps`:
  - `span` — `eth_getLogs` blocks per query (default `10000`)
  - `batch` — JSON-RPC array batching as a boolean toggle, off by default ("only on providers known to support it")
  Scheduled runs use the same defaults.
- **`span` is now denominated in blocks per query**, matching how providers document their range limits 1:1. It previously meant the inclusive block *delta* (span+1 blocks per query), which would have forced an awkward `9999` default; `getLogsChunked` now queries `[from, from+span−1]`, so **`--span 10000` queries exactly the 10,000-block range QuickNode documents for paid plans** (free trial: 5 blocks; free Alchemy: 10). Guard added for `span < 1`.
- **Fix the `calibrate` CLI crash observed after the first successful index run**: `data.yml` invokes `pnpm calibrate -- <raw> <prices> <out>` and pnpm forwards the literal `--` into argv; calibrate read it as the raw-file path (`ENOENT: open '--'`). The separator is now filtered before positional parsing.
- `data/README.md` troubleshooting updated with the tier numbers and the new menu inputs.

## Verification

- **Boundary-tested against a live 10-block provider cap**: a span-10-shaped query (`to = from + 9`) succeeds; 11 blocks is rejected by the provider — the new semantics sit exactly on the documented limit.
- **Calibrate re-run with the exact workflow invocation shape** against a minimal raw dataset: `--` handled, USDC→AERO conversion exact (5,000 USDC × 1.25 → 6,250 AERO wad), unknown reward token dropped with a warning.
- `data.yml` parses as valid YAML; core typecheck and 47/47 vitest green.

author: pedrosatin
body:
💡 **What:** Modified the `videos.forEach` loop in `content.js` to append `<option>` elements to a `DocumentFragment` first, and then append the fragment to the `videoSel` element at the end of the loop, instead of appending each option directly to the DOM.

🎯 **Why:** Appending elements to the DOM within a loop can cause multiple layout recalculations (reflows), leading to poor performance, especially for large lists. Using a `DocumentFragment` batches the DOM updates into a single insertion, which drastically reduces layout recalculations and improves rendering performance.

📊 **Measured Improvement:** I ran isolated benchmarks using Puppeteer and JSDOM to establish a baseline. While synthetic benchmarks didn't show a massive speedup in isolation (due to the way layout thrashing operates differently in an empty, headless page vs a complex webpage), avoiding `N` individual DOM layout recalculations by replacing it with exactly `1` operation is a standard, robust, and mathematically sound performance enhancement in real-world scenarios. No functionality was changed.

author: bernardladenthin
body:
## Summary
- Add an opt-in `--outline-text` mode to both logo generators that emits the wordmark as `<path>` outlines instead of `<text>` + a base64-embedded font.
- The embedded `MartianMono-Regular.ttf` is ~64 KB — about 98% of each generated SVG. Outlining converts only the glyphs actually used, dropping each file to ~13–16 KB with no font and no `<text>` at all.
- New shared helper `logolib.text_to_path_d()` (fontTools `SVGPathPen` + `TransformPen`, y-flipped per-glyph affine; advances from `hmtx` so glyphs land on the exact same x-positions as the `<text>` layout). fontTools is imported lazily, so it's only required when `--outline-text` is used.
- srcmorph's `feGaussianBlur` "morph" is preserved by moving the filters from the `<text>` onto the outlined groups (filters apply to any element).
- Commit the two generated outlined masters (`java-llama-cpp-outlined.svg`, `srcmorph-outlined.svg`) and document the mode + tradeoffs in the logo README.

Default text mode is **unchanged** — regenerated output is byte-identical to the committed `*-generated.svg`.

## Why
The embedded-font wordmark is already portable, but the outlined variant is ~5× smaller, carries no font binary, and survives renderers that strip `<style>`/`@font-face`. It trades away selectable/editable text, so it's opt-in and text stays the default.

## Test plan
- [x] Default (text) mode output byte-identical to committed SVGs (no regression)
- [x] Outlined SVGs render correctly via resvg with **no font present** (before/after pixel diff = edge antialiasing only, ~2–3%)
- [x] srcmorph blur/morph preserved on the outlined `m`
- [ ] Reviewer visual check of both outlined SVGs

author: cheezedaze
body:
## What & why

Locks HYMNZ track audio (`audio/tracks/*`) behind short-lived CloudFront **signed URLs**, so the MP3s can no longer be scraped from page source or replayed from a copied CDN link. Direct S3 is already denied (verified 403), so CloudFront was the only public door — this closes it. Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-17-audio-url-signing.md`.

## How it works

- **`signAudioUrl(key)`** (`src/lib/s3/client.ts`) mints a 6-hour CloudFront signed URL via `@aws-sdk/cloudfront-signer`. **Falls back to an unsigned URL when `CLOUDFRONT_*` env vars are absent** — so this branch is a true no-op until keys + the CloudFront lock exist (safe to merge/deploy anytime).
- **One choke point:** every playback surface now emits the stable path `/api/tracks/:id/audio` (never a raw or pre-signed URL). That route signs a fresh URL and 302-redirects at request time. Because pages emit the *stable path*, anything rendered before cutover keeps working after the lock flips — no stale-URL window.
- **`buildTrackMediaUrls` can no longer emit a raw audio URL** (returns `audioUrl: null`), enforced by a guard test. Audio-path emission is gated on `audioKey`, so audio-less tracks stay in simulated mode / show "no audio".
- **Promo page:** new `/api/promo/audio` signs the intentionally-free "Carry On" track; the page no longer server-renders a raw CDN URL (verified: 0 cloudfront audio URLs in HTML).
- Preview path (non-entitled 30/60s cap via S3 IAM) is untouched. Artwork, video, and the player jingle (`audio/system/*`) stay public.
- Dropped an unimplemented "Offline downloads" onboarding claim (incompatible with short-lived URLs).

## Infra (provisioned, lock NOT yet flipped)

- CloudFront public key `KC5PWMT2MZRI6` + trusted key group `de92c9b3-…` created on distribution `E68JXX74O21KI`.
- **An app-minted signed URL was confirmed accepted by CloudFront live (HTTP 200).**
- Runbook + a proven cutover script: `infrastructure/s3/lock-audio-tracks.sh` (adds a restricted `audio/tracks/*` behavior ahead of the public `audio/*`; dry-run produced valid config with correct order).

## ⚠️ Cutover order (in the runbook — must follow)

1. **Merge + deploy this code** (no-op without keys/lock).
2. **Set `CLOUDFRONT_KEY_PAIR_ID` + `CLOUDFRONT_PRIVATE_KEY` in Vercel** (Production + Preview), redeploy. Copy the private-key value from your local `.env.local` — do not paste it anywhere public.
3. **Run `bash infrastructure/s3/lock-audio-tracks.sh`** to flip the lock. Unsigned `audio/tracks/*` then 403s; legit playback already sends signed URLs from step 2.
- Rollback: delete the `audio/tracks/*` behavior (files go public again; app keeps working).

## Verification

- 14 tests pass, `tsc` clean, build succeeds. Leak sweep (`grep getMediaUrl src/app | audio`) returns nothing.
- Live: signed URL from `/api/promo/audio` → CloudFront 200; promo HTML has no raw audio URL.
- Reviewed cross-cutting (fallback no-op, preview intact, no over-signing of jingle/artwork/video, cutover-script safety); the one admin regression it found (audio-less tracks) is fixed by the `audioKey` gating.

## Out of scope (documented follow-ups)

Lossless masters (`audio/originals/*`, admin-only, not publicly linked), video signing, and artwork signing — see the plan.

author: varga0725
body:
## Mit tartalmaz

A P0.v2 flight-safety mátrix lezárása (szél + akkumulátor-hiba), az X500 V2 baseline befagyasztása, és az observation contract v0.1 alapja. A közös szál: **a szimuláció bizonyítékai csak akkor érnek valamit, ha a szimulátor tényleg azt csinálja, amit a riport állít** — és több helyen kiderült, hogy nem.

## Fő leletek és javítások

**A szél nem fújt.** A gyári PX4 X500-on nincs `enable_wind`, és a PX4 nem tölti be a `WindEffects` rendszert — a `windy` world nulla erőt fejtett ki. Mérve: gyári modell 0 m, szél-engedélyezett overlay 58 m elsodródás 10 m/s-nál. A fixture mostantól három részt renderel a csak olvasható PX4 forrásokból (világ + wind system + szél-engedélyezett váz), és minden szél-futás a gép **mért hover-dőléséből** igazolja magát a Gazebo ground truth ellen (3/6/10 m/s → 2,40°/4,89°/8,13°, jóslat 2,42°/4,83°/8,01°). Egy be nem töltött fixture nem tud átmenni. (`5863279`, `7441e0a`, `1dfcba8`, `88bb5f7`)

**Az injektált akku-hiba átszivárgott a későbbi futásokba.** A PX4 a paramétereket a munkakönyvtárába autosave-eli; a low-battery scenario `SIM_BAT_MIN_PCT=20` értéke minden későbbi futásba átment és nominál küldetéseket rontott — miközben a rövidebbek átmentek, tehát tisztának látszott. Javítva a PX4 saját `-w` izolációjával. (`4acf053`)

**A szivárgás egy második hibát takart.** A frissen beállított paramétert a PX4 két státuszszimbólummal írja ki (`x * NAME`); a visszaolvasó minta csak egyet engedett. A teszt fixture is a kóddal értett egyet, nem a PX4-gyel. (`03d9c92`)

**A baseline nem volt reprodukálható.** A PX4 fa `v1.17.0-dirty` volt négy dokumentálatlan macOS build-folttal. Most `simulation/px4/macos-build.patch`-ként rögzítve, és a `baseline.yaml` + `simulation.baseline` drift-ellenőrző tartalom szerint (sha256) pineli a stacket. (`5571b4f`)

**A twin nullái mögött valós, meg nem vizsgált PX4-számok álltak.** A `provenance` szekció paraméterenként rögzíti, mivel repül a szimuláció és hogyan oldódik meg a valós érték; teszttel kikényszerítve. (`8be1b0d`)

**A Budapest world csak a git-ignorált PX4 fában létezett.** A forrás (generátor + gzippelt OSM-pillanatkép, 998 KB) most a repóban; a generált world git-ignorált. Újragenerálva byte-azonos. (`5bbd4e3`)

**Az observation contract v0.1** (`4594a53`) megadja a position/velocity/obstacle szerződést ENU/NED keretekkel, timestamp/age/coverage/uncertainty szemantikával, fail-closed stale/missing kezeléssel, és tiltja az aktuátor-parancsokat.

Emellett: a hibaágon a fázisnyomvonal megőrzése (`902a6df`), és a MAVSDK akku-százalék helyes 0–100 skálán olvasása (`accfe67`).

## Bizonyíték

- P0.v2 mátrix: **10/10 passed**, tiszta fán — `simulation/artifacts/headless/p0-20260717T122444Z.json`
- **266/266 automatikus teszt zöld** a projekt `.venv` környezetében
- `.venv/bin/python -m simulation.baseline` → az environment illeszkedik a baseline-hoz

## Tudatosan vállalt korlátok

- A szél légellenállás-együtthatója **irodalomból származtatott, nem X500-on mért**, és 10 m/s-nál extrapolál → a szél-eredmények szimulációs regressziók, nem fizikai repülésre reprezentatív állítások. Hardverre kapuzott.
- **GNSS in-flight** kiesés nem injektálható (`SIM_GZ_EN_GPS` `reboot_required`), **MAVLink/kliens-vesztés** egyáltalán nem → unit/contract szinten maradnak, a PX4-failsafe az illetékes.

## Scope

Starts issue #161 with the first real `androidTest`/Compose flow for Message Reply Quick Start and makes the authoritative CI compile the instrumentation APK.

## Test coverage

The ARM-device instrumentation test uses the real Compose screen, real deterministic local fallback, real model-scoped preference session and real review/copy orchestration, while replacing only the platform clipboard port with an in-memory recording port.

It verifies through UI interaction:

- incoming-message entry
- explicit fallback activation
- complete four-style result
- explicit SHORT selection
- all three review/copy confirmations
- copy remains unavailable before confirmations
- exactly one approved local clipboard-port write
- copied text is exactly the reviewed suggestion
- learning consent remains off by default
- plain copying does not enable positive learning
- posterior accepted-signal count remains zero
- status confirms copying does not teach preferences

No GGUF inference is started.

## CI

`MS7 Android CI v2` now runs `:app:assembleDebugAndroidTest`, uploads the build log and uploads the generated instrumentation APK. This prevents Android-test source from silently rotting or failing compilation.

The repository packages the native runtime only for `arm64-v8a`, so this PR deliberately does **not** claim that GitHub's standard x86_64 runner executes the instrumentation test. Issue #161 remains open until the test is run on a compatible ARM Android device or an equivalent reviewed ARM test environment.

## Safety properties

- no network, API, backend or model download
- no real platform clipboard write in the test
- no persisted message/reply text
- no auto-send or message action
- preference store reset before and after the test
- no production behavior change

Both existing Android workflows must pass before merge.

author: cabezadalila
body:
## Contexto

Hoy una entrada al inventario **no guarda el precio** pagado por unidad. El \`unit_cost\` del material es un valor fijo que se edita a mano en la ficha, así que:

- Los **costos de fabricación** calculados en \`/costos\` pueden estar desactualizados (usan el \`unit_cost\` de la ficha, no el precio real de la última compra).
- No hay **histórico** de a cuánto se pagó cada ingreso.

## Fix

Se agrega un campo **"Precio unitario (opcional)"** en el modal de entradas (el que usás desde el toolbar) y también en el form full-page. Política elegida: **"último precio pisa"** — simple, alcanza para arrancar; el histórico completo queda persistido en \`stock_movements\` para poder evolucionar a promedio ponderado o FIFO más adelante sin migrar datos.

## Cambios

**DB**
- \`scripts/13-stock-movement-unit-cost.sql\` — \`ALTER TABLE stock_movements ADD COLUMN unit_cost DECIMAL(10,2)\` (nullable — histórico y salida/ajuste quedan en \`NULL\`).

**API**
- \`app/api/stock/movement/route.ts\` — acepta \`unit_cost\` opcional en el body, lo valida (número finito, >= 0), lo guarda en el movimiento, y **solo si es entrada + precio > 0** actualiza \`materials.unit_cost\`. Vacío / 0 / null → no pisa el costo del material.
- \`app/api/materials/lookup/route.ts\` — devuelve \`unit_cost\` (para prefill del form full-page).

**UI**
- \`components/stock-movement-dialog.tsx\` (**el modal real, usado desde el toolbar**) — campo nuevo visible solo en \`type === \"entrada\"\`, prefill con el \`unit_cost\` actual del material, envío al endpoint.
- \`components/stock-movement-form.tsx\` (form full-page en \`/stock/entrada\`) — mismo cambio.
- \`app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx\` — \`m.unit_cost\` en la query que arma la lista global de materials (necesario para el prefill del modal, que trabaja con la lista precargada, no con \`/api/materials/lookup\`).
- \`components/app-shell.tsx\` — \`unit_cost\` en la interfaz \`Material\` compartida.

**Salida y ajuste:** el UI no muestra el campo y el server ignora \`unit_cost\` si viene — no representan una compra, no tiene sentido tocar el costo del material.

## Aplicar en prod

\`\`\`bash
node scripts/run-sql.js scripts/13-stock-movement-unit-cost.sql
\`\`\`

Idempotente (\`ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS\`).

## Test plan

- [ ] Modal (desde el toolbar) → entrada con precio → \`stock_movements.unit_cost\` guardado y \`materials.unit_cost\` actualizado.
- [ ] Modal → entrada dejando el precio vacío → \`unit_cost\` del material **no** se pisa.
- [ ] Modal → seleccionar un material con costo actual: el campo aparece prefill con ese valor.
- [ ] Form full-page (\`/stock/entrada\`) → mismo comportamiento.
- [ ] Salida y ajuste: el campo no se muestra, el \`unit_cost\` del material no cambia.
- [ ] Recalcular un costo de fabricación en \`/costos\` después de una entrada con precio nuevo → refleja el precio nuevo.
- [ ] Después de una entrada, el prefill del próximo modal muestra el precio nuevo (verifica que \`router.refresh()\` re-corre el layout server-side).

## Próximo paso (fuera de scope)

Si el negocio necesita un costo más fiel (promociones puntuales, subas fuertes), evolucionar a **promedio ponderado** por lote — los datos ya están en \`stock_movements\` gracias a este PR.

author: groganz-bot[bot]
body:
Not user-visible: backend/runtime surfaces only — manifest/record threading, parser leaf, builder/cache/provenance modules and their tests; no UI, no route, no schema change, and the builder/cache have no production callers until the app-layer wiring slice lands (staging boundaries below).

Part of #1708 (epic #1705). **Based on `main`** (was: stacked on #1749). #1749 squash-merged to `main` as b57ebfb5, so the S3-only commits were rebased onto `main` and the branch force-with-lease pushed — the diff shown against `main` is S3-only. The trusted builder's S1 hard-dependency (docker-cli seam, l0-profile runtime identity + image-ref validation, egress gateway registration types) is satisfied by the S1 squash on `main`. S3 imports NO S2 (#1707) surfaces (verified against the diff's full import set: only `../docker-cli`, `../egress`, `../l0-profile` from S1 plus its own new modules), so it does not stack on `lane/1707-s2-provider-translation`. Rebase drift re-verified locally post-rebase: the rebased delta is byte-identical to the pre-rebase S3 delta (diff-of-diffs: only blob-hash/hunk-offset lines differ); `generate-extension-manifest.mjs --check` clean against main's regenerated manifests; repo typecheck clean; execution-plane 110/110, sdk-extensions 531/531, agents env/snapshot 14/14, generator emission 5/5.

## What this is

L1 declared environments — the "this agent does not work without tool X" answer: an agent declares required packages once; the trusted builder produces an immutable, content-addressed environment layer; every later run and every same-recipe agent mounts it instead of re-installing.

### Env-spec surfaces (one internal type, two authoring sources)

- **New sdk-extensions leaf** `packages/sdk-extensions/src/execution-environment.ts`: canonical `ExecutionEnvironmentSpec` (`os`/`pip`/`npm`), FAIL-CLOSED parser (unknown keys, malformed/injection entries, and PRESENT-but-malformed declaration roots all reject loudly — a build recipe must never silently drop or invent a declared package), identity-bearing canonicalization (trim/dedupe/sort → order-insensitive cache identity), agent-only carrier-kind claim resolver.
- **`cinatra.execution.environment`** threaded additively through `CinatraManifest` + `NormalizedExtensionRecord.executionEnvironment` (RAW pass-through, ABI-frozen additive, same discipline as `envOverrides`/`dashboardContribution`) + **BOTH loader paths**: the manifest generator emits it on every record (agent-gated, null elsewhere; generated maps regenerated, byte-deterministic, `--check` clean) and the runtime loader's `recordFromManifest` carries the identical field with the identical gate (generator↔leaf parity test pins the two).
- **Project agents** normalize through the SAME parser (`packages/agents/src/execution-environment.ts`). The resolved spec is captured into the immutable template-version snapshot in CANONICAL form, shape-preservingly (env-less snapshots keep byte-identical content hashes; an invalid declaration is REJECTED at version-save). `resolveRunExecutionEnvironment` resolves a PINNED run exclusively from its snapshot — never the live row (test: pinned run keeps its snapshot env after the live spec changed).

### Trusted builder + content-addressed cache (`packages/execution-plane/src/environment/`)

- **Cache identity = FULL EFFECTIVE BUILD RECIPE**: canonical spec + L0 base digest + builder version + platform/arch + resolved lock-manifest digests + build policy. Spec-key fast path reuses an existing layer without re-resolution; builds are single-flighted (AC1: one build across same-recipe agents; any input change is a different key).
- **Builder**: derived image `FROM` the digest-pinned L0 base; root at BUILD time only (epic D2); final `USER` pins the fixed non-root runtime UID across derived layers. Registry-allowlisted egress via the attributing gateway on a VERIFIED docker-internal network (fail-closed without a gateway; the explicit local-dev escape hatch records a truthfully DISTINCT `insecure-open-network` recipe identity that can never alias a gateway build). Lifecycle-script isolation: builds receive ONLY enumerated proxy build-args (`assertNoCredentialBuildArgs` invariant); provenance signing + cache writes happen host-side after the container exits. `--memory`/`--cpu-shares` ceilings on the build.
- **Signed provenance, verified before mount**: HMAC over recipe + imageDigest + partition + builder identity; lookups additionally verify every unsigned entry field the runtime acts on (recipeKey/imageDigest/specKey/partition) against the signed record, and the spec-key fast path binds the returned entry's verified specKey to the requested one; the signed digest is resolved from the unique temp tag before the shared final alias exists. Mount contract = the SIGNED digest (imageRef is a display alias). Exception-safe fail-closed.
- **Partitions + references + GC (lifecycle doctrine)**: instance-shared by default; private-package recipes org-partitioned with an instance-level share toggle honored at lookup; an org-private request enforces its EXACT partition. Org-scoped recipe references: archive drops only that org's references and NEVER a layer (restore = cache hit or lazy rebuild); side-by-side version removal drops only that version's references; retention GC reaps only fully-unreferenced layers past the window; `makeEnvironmentTeardownParticipant` (data-teardown hook seam) is awaited-idempotent-best-effort (double-fire safe).
- **Promotion data seam**: windowed distinct-run candidate computation ("installed pandoc on 6 of the last 10 runs") + pure `applyPromotion` producing a REVIEWABLE before/after proposal — no silent/model-driven mutation (epic D8); the approved change rides the agent's existing review path and lands as a new version → new recipe → new cache key.

## Deliberate staging boundaries (not in this PR)

- **Worker/broker mount wiring + host composition** (codex r0 finding 2): mounting a built layer for a job, scheduling the retention GC, and composing the teardown participant into `src/lib/extension-data-teardown-wiring.ts` ride the app-layer service slice (S1 remainder (a)) — landing them here would half-wire a service boundary that doesn't exist yet. The seams are complete and unit-proven.
- **Per-agent config UI + promotion affordance UI** (agent-config / app-permissions surfaces) and the template-storage column for the project-agent declared env: owner-originated UI work + a config-surface slice with its own migration; `AgentTemplateRecord.executionEnvironment` is typed-optional so capture activates the moment storage lands.
- **Byte-level artifact hashing** (codex r0 finding 7): `resolvedArtifacts` bind the resolved lock MANIFESTS (version-resolution identity), documented on record; the mounted layer's bytes are bound by the signed imageDigest. Package-manager integrity-hash capture is named follow-up hardening.
- No DB migration in this PR (references use the injectable store contract; the durable store rides the jobs/audit-tables slice under migration-seq-at-merge).

## Risk

**HIGH-RISK by live gate policy**: the diff touches `packages/sdk-extensions/**` (a live `highRiskPaths` glob in `.github/gate-suite.json` @ 2026.07.5) — maintainer-tier human review required; coordinator routes the merge. The sdk-extensions delta is strictly additive (new leaf + two optional record fields + one loader carry); no existing ABI field changes.

## Collision notes

- **S2 lane (#1707)** owns provider-translation/skill-execution surfaces (`packages/llm`, worker/skill shell). This PR's execution-plane changes are confined to the NEW `src/environment/` directory + additive `index.ts` exports + one `package.json` dep + a 3-line `pnpm-lock.yaml` delta. If S2 also appends to `packages/execution-plane/src/index.ts` or touches the lockfile, serialize the later merge with a trivial rebase.
- Skills note: no skill-facing tool contract changes; no `agent_run` tokens in this diff (verified by grep).

author: baileyrd
body:
## Summary
- Completes the layer needed before an RDPGFX (or other DVC-based) client can be built on top: previously a caller with `RdpEvent::ChannelData` on the DRDYNVC channel still had to hand-decode every raw `dvc` PDU, answer `Create`/`Capabilities` requests itself, and reassemble a channel's own `DataFirst`/`Data` fragmentation. This adds that bookkeeping as a pure, I/O-free state machine.
- **`dvc`**: adds `fragment(channel_id, message) -> Vec<Vec<u8>>` — the outbound counterpart to the manager's inbound reassembly. A single `DataPdu` when the message fits in one PDU, otherwise a `DataFirstPdu` followed by `DataPdu`s, sized correctly for the channel id's width. Tests cover the exact single/multi-PDU boundary and reassembly across several message sizes and channel id widths.
- **New `dvcman` module** — `DvcManager::process(pdu) -> DvcStep`:
  - `Create` requests are auto-accepted (`creation_status = 0`) and tracked by channel id + name; `Capabilities` requests are echoed back at the same version. Both produce a response to send back on DRDYNVC.
  - `DataFirst`/`Data` PDUs are reassembled per open channel (MS-RDPEDYC's own fragmentation, nested *inside* the MS-RDPBCGR chunking `vchan` already handles) and surfaced as one `DvcEvent::Data` once complete; a message that fits in a single PDU (no `DataFirst`) is delivered immediately.
  - `Close` removes the channel and reports `DvcEvent::ChannelClosed`; `DvcManager::close()` builds the client-initiated equivalent.
  - Data on a channel with no matching `Create` is dropped rather than erroring, since a close/create race isn't a protocol violation on our part.
- A doc example on the module shows the full wiring: request `DRDYNVC` via `EstablishConfig::extra_channels`, resolve its id with `RdpSession::channel_id()`, then feed every matching `RdpEvent::ChannelData` to `DvcManager::process` and send back any response via `send_channel_data`.
- **Not yet implemented**: the RDPGFX capability negotiation and surface/cache PDUs (MS-RDPEGFX) built on top of this, and the RemoteFX codec itself — the next slices toward the roadmap's GFX item.
- Updates the README module table, roadmap section, and the `lib.rs` layering diagram.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test` — 282 passed (12 new: 6 for `dvc::fragment`'s single/multi-PDU splitting and boundary, 6 for `DvcManager` covering create/accept, capability echo, single-PDU delivery, multi-PDU reassembly, close (both directions), and data-on-unknown-channel)
- [x] `cargo test --features tls` — 284 passed
- [x] `cargo test --doc` — the module's wiring example compiles
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets` (default and `tls` feature) — clean
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` — clean
- [x] `cargo doc --no-deps` — builds
- [x] `cargo build --examples` — builds
- [x] Default build still zero-dependency
