🎯 **What:** The `addons/KGB_Agent/kgb_dock.gd` file had a vulnerability where it directly accessed deeply nested JSON keys (`json["candidates"][0]["content"]["parts"][0]["text"]`) without verifying their existence or type. 

⚠️ **Risk:** If the generative AI API returned a malformed response or an error format while still using a 200 OK code, the unvalidated access would cause the tool to crash, potentially corrupting editor state or exposing unexpected behavior.

🛡️ **Solution:** Added robust type-checking and key existence validation at every level of the JSON response hierarchy using GDScript's `typeof()` and `.has()`. It now safely handles malformed JSON and returns clear error messages to the user without crashing. Additionally, the HTTP request result is verified as `HTTPRequest.RESULT_SUCCESS`.

author: steipete
body:
## Summary

Zero-latency cursors for Share This Mac. The cursor leaves the video stream and becomes a negotiated client-side channel using standard RFB pseudo-encodings, so third-party viewers benefit too.

- Wire: `CursorWithAlpha` (-314, premultiplied RGBA) preferred, classic `Cursor` (-239, unpremultiplied BGRX + 1-bit mask with an anti-fringe alpha threshold) fallback, `PointerPos` (-232) for server-driven position; all per rfbproto, strict bounds, 128px cap.
- Host: 60 Hz polling with content-hash dedup and inverted-Retina mapping; 250 ms echo suppression so the host doesn't fight viewer-driven movement; per-display capture baking disabled only when every active session negotiated a cursor channel (audio-style refcount rule); system cursor visibility respected via a runtime-resolved `CGCursorIsVisible` probe with an always-visible fallback (the API is unavailable to Swift; a probe-resolution canary test flags if macOS ever drops the symbol).
- Arbitration: cursor and video share the pending framebuffer request through an explicit arbiter — cursor changes wake a waiting request (no frozen cursor on a static desktop), and fairness counts pending JPEG frame-store frames on the Tight path so continuous cursor traffic can never starve fallback video.
- Viewers: native sets the scaled AppKit cursor and draws a divergent-position overlay; browser uses a CSS data-URL cursor plus a remote-pointer overlay while divergent or unfocused.

## Review

Seven structured-review cycles. Fixed with regression tests: cursor-wake for pending requests (P1), Tight/JPEG starvation under continuous cursor traffic (P1 — arbitration now counts frame-store frames), resize stranding stale shape/position, pointer loss after hide/show, shape loss when position wins a simultaneous transition, system-visibility suppression. Final review: clean.

## Proof

- `pnpm check` / `pnpm test`: 955/955
- `pnpm macos:test`: RoyalVNCKit 115/115, app 226/226 — including loopback protocol tests for wake, fairness-under-continuous-cursor-traffic, resize replay, and hide/show replay via a new feedable byte-stream harness
- Wire encoders byte-cross-checked against the fork's parsers

Paul Emptoz

## Summary

`AGENTS.md` had diverged substantially between `master` and `v0.2.0` (`git diff --stat origin/master origin/v0.2.0 -- AGENTS.md` showed 354 insertions, 84 deletions), and separately, roughly two dozen genuinely normative bullets in the current text had never received an `[AG-XXX-NNN]` rule ID. This PR (against `master`) lands one reconciled, fully ID-tagged `AGENTS.md`. **Companion PR: #969** applies the byte-identical final file to `v0.2.0`, so both branches converge on the same text. This PR carries the exact same diff content and rationale as #969 -- see that PR for the full write-up (including the complete 28-row ID table and the full 11-item flagged-but-untagged list); this body summarizes it for reviewers who land on this PR first, without duplicating the full detail across both.

## Linked Issues

No tracking issue: this is a maintainer-directed governance-doc housekeeping change (per `AGENTS.md`'s own PR-template allowance for PRs with no issue to mirror labels from).

## What This Actually Changes

Verified every diff hunk between `origin/master:AGENTS.md` and `origin/v0.2.0:AGENTS.md` individually (not just the stat). Finding: `v0.2.0`'s content is a **strict superset** of `master`'s -- every line unique to `master` is either identical prose already present in `v0.2.0` (just not yet ID-tagged there) or content `v0.2.0` states in an equivalent or more complete form. `master`'s only branch-unique commit touching this file, `777b6c31` ("docs: require active issue/PR comment maintenance, #823"), added text present **verbatim** in `v0.2.0`'s "Issue And PR Tracking" section -- confirmed via issue #856 / PR #857 (closed, completed), which had already cherry-picked this and 4 other master-only commits onto `v0.2.0`. This PR replaces `master`'s current `AGENTS.md` with the same reconciled file being applied to `v0.2.0` in #969 -- no content is lost, since everything `master` had is already contained in the new text.

## What This PR Fixes / Adds

Same 28 new IDs as #969 (full table with verbatim bullet text there): `AG-GH-009` through `AG-GH-016` (Issue And PR Tracking), `AG-WF-020` through `AG-WF-023` (Agent Workflow / Agent Autonomy), `AG-VAL-025` (Required Validation), `AG-OP-014` and `AG-OP-015` (Setup/Migration, Coding Patterns), `AG-CI-009` through `AG-CI-011` (Coding Patterns), `AG-REL-008` (Coding Patterns), and a new `AG-HDR-001` through `AG-HDR-009` category for the previously-untagged File Headers section. Pure prefix additions only -- no existing wording changed anywhere. Matching Rule Enforcement Matrix rows added for all 28.

## What Changed In Code

Only `AGENTS.md` is touched. Same change set as #969: `[AG-X-NNN]` prefix insertions on 28 previously-untagged bullets, 28 new matrix rows, and the reconciled base text (v0.2.0's superset content). No existing sentence's wording was changed.

## Why This Matters For Users / Operators

No end-user/operator impact -- this is a governance/contributor-facing document. Matters for anyone (human or agent) working on this repo: these 28 rules were previously not citable by ID despite being just as binding as the rest of the document.

## Scope Boundaries

Only `AGENTS.md`. Does not touch `.github/AGENTS.md` (already byte-identical between branches) or `CLAUDE.md` (handled separately).

author: dagfinn2000
body:
## Reading log

Every change to **current page** is now kept as a dated `ProgressEntry` — zero extra effort, the page number you were already typing becomes data. Built on top of it:

- **Book page**: a progress-over-time sparkline for the current pass; pages/day pace with a finish forecast while reading ("~29 pages/day · on pace to finish 7 Aug 2026"), retrospective pace once finished ("~68 pages/day over 15 days"); a collapsible entry list with delete buttons.
- **Stats page**: a GitHub-style **reading-days heatmap** of the last 12 months, tinted by pages read per day, with reading-day totals and streaks.
- **Backups**: entries ride along in exports and restores. The export stays version-1 (additive field, like quotes and reads) — old backups restore fine, and new backups fed to an older instance are simply ignored.

**Mechanics**: pages/day is the delta between *consecutive* entries of a book; every reading pass opens with a page-0 anchor (first progress update, "Read it again", or the upgrade seed), so a lone entry credits nothing and corrections just move the baseline. The latest page-0 entry doubles as the pass boundary — that keeps a re-read started the same day as older entries cleanly separated (the started-date field only has day precision).

**Existing installs**: the migration is purely additive (`CREATE TABLE` + index + FK) and seeds an anchor from `currentPage` for books mid-read, so pace works from the first post-upgrade update without crediting a giant fake reading day. Applied automatically by `prisma migrate deploy` on container start.

## Per-user theme

The picked theme is now saved on the account (`User.theme`, additive migration) and server-rendered onto `<html>`, so signing in from a new browser or device paints your palette from the first frame. localStorage remains the fallback for signed-out pages, and the pre-paint script now defers to the server-set value and mirrors it locally.

## Bug fix: reading form silently reverting status

React 19 resets uncontrolled forms after a successful action, and the Radix Select's hidden native select snapped back to its mount-time value — saving reading data twice without a reload resubmitted the original status (e.g. Currently Reading → back to Want to Read). The form is now keyed on the server-side reading data so each save remounts it with fresh defaults. (A controlled `value` prop doesn't fix it: the reset happens at the DOM level where React never observes it.)

## Cleanup (no behavior change)

`requireUserId`/`ActionState` deduped into `lib/actions/helpers.ts` (5 copies → 1), `buildSearchText` shared between actions and backup import, stats/edit-page queries parallelized, two count queries folded into adjacent lookups via `_count`, dead `ratingToStars` and unused `skeleton`/`separator` components removed.

## Verification

Exercised end-to-end against a live Postgres 16 + dev server: logging/anchors, pace + forecast math, finish flow, re-read isolation, heatmap day totals (including that seeds and imports credit the right days), entry deletion, export→import round-trip of progress entries, the upgrade-seed SQL against pre-existing rows, the two-consecutive-saves repro for the form fix, and theme round-trip (pick → DB row → localStorage wipe → hard reload → server-rendered theme). `npm run build` green throughout.

body:
The scheduled OSV workflow (`scan-scheduled / osv-scan`) is failing on a known advisory (`GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr`) in the docs dependency tree. This PR scopes an OSV ignore to that advisory so scheduled scans stop failing until the VitePress v2 upgrade path is available.

- **Root cause**
  - OSV scan is configured with fail-on-vulnerability behavior and flags `esbuild` in `docs/package-lock.json` via VitePress v1 transitive dependencies.

- **Change**
  - Added a docs-local OSV config at `docs/osv-scanner.toml`.
  - Declared a single `[[IgnoredVulns]]` entry for `GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr` with an explicit temporary rationale.

- **Scope / impact**
  - Ignore is narrowly scoped to the docs dependency scan path rather than disabling OSV failure behavior globally.
  - Keeps scheduled security scans actionable while avoiding persistent noise from this known upstream constraint.

```toml
[[IgnoredVulns]]
id = "GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr"
reason = "VitePress v1 currently depends on vulnerable esbuild; tracked until VitePress v2 upgrade is available."
```

body:
## Summary

Follow-up to the booking redesign. The plan chooser is now shown only when the user hasn't already decided. Landing "Book Now" buttons carry the chosen plan, and the flow adapts to whether the user holds a package credit.

## Behavior

**Landing → booking**
- Consultation card → `?plan=consultation`
- Package cards + hero Emergency callout → `?plan=<slug>`
- Generic Book (hero / header / CTA) → `/booking` (no param)

**Booking flow**
- Pre-selected **consultation** → skip chooser → book (399, or 0 if a credit is held)
- Pre-selected **package + credit** → skip chooser → book (credit deducted at review)
- Pre-selected **package + no credit** → a purchase step buys that package first (shows its price → Stripe), then resumes into booking (credit deducted at review)
- **Generic** Book → always show the plan chooser

## Notes
- Removes the earlier credit-based auto-skip; credit is resolved up front (behind a loader) only when it changes the flow.
- Package-resume `success_url` now carries the plan slug so the return lands cleanly on date/time.
- `StepSelectPlan` gains a `restrictToSlug` mode for the single-package purchase step.
- No new payment backend — reuses the existing one-time (399) and package-purchase + resume flows.

## Testing
- API `tsc` · web `tsc` / `eslint` · `next build` all pass.

body:
## Özet

v2 kataloğunun (39 karat-ayrık listing) üstüne uygulanan **v3 transform**. İki
kullanıcı direktifi:

1. **Yarım bedenler eklendi** — US 4, 4.5, 5 … 16 = **25 beden**.
2. **2.0mm kalınlık kaldırıldı**, tek **1.5mm** kaldı ("2 kalınları temizle, 1.5mm olanı kalsın").

## Ne değişti

| | v2 | **v3** |
|---|---|---|
| Beden ekseni | 13 (tek sayı) | **25 (tam+yarım)** |
| Kalınlık | 1.5mm + 2.0mm | **yalnız 1.5mm** |
| Genişlik ekseni | 22 (katlanmış) | **11 (2–12mm)** |
| Varyant/listing | 286 | **275** |
| Toplam varyant | 11.154 | **10.725** |
| SKU | `<fam>-<W>MM-T<15\|20>-<SIZE>` | **`<fam>-<W>MM-<SIZE>`** |

- **Yarım-beden gramı** = komşu tam bedenlerin doğrusal orta-noktası (tablolar
  satır-doğrusal → birebir doğru). Örn. 14K·6mm·4=4.67g, 5=4.89g → 4.5=**4.78g**.
- **39 açıklama** iki-kalınlık dilinden temizlenip "whole and half sizes" + tek
  1.5mm ile yeniden yazıldı; sessiz-lüks ton + minimalist/kalıcı kural (fiyat/gram/
  servis-süresi/resize sözü yok) korundu.
- **Fiyat formülü değişmedi:** `ceil(gram × ppg_cent / 500) × 500 + 1000` ($10 kargo payı).

## Değişen dosyalar

- `supabase/migrations/0101_eon_catalog_v3.sql` — canlıya uygulanan transform'un
  aynısı (Bölüm A: varyant v2→v3; Bölüm B: 39 açıklama UPDATE). Preview provizyonu + kayıt.
- `docs/eon/gen_catalog_v3.py` — saf/kendi-kendine-yeter üretici (yalnız gram
  tablosu okur; iç assert'lerle 10.725/275/SKU-tekilliği doğrular).
- `docs/eon/eon-v3-catalog.json` — üretilen kanonik yapı/fiyat katmanı.
- `docs/eon/katalog-v3.md` — v3 runbook/karar kaydı.
- `docs/eon/README.md` — güncel katalog banner'ı v3'e taşındı.
- `docs/second-brain.md` — 4 ders eklendi.

## Doğrulama (canlı DB'de koşuldu)

- **Açıklamalar 39/39 temiz:** whole+half=39 · 2.0mm/two-thick/whole-US/servis/
  fiyat/resize leak=0 · v3 künye=39.
- **Varyantlar:** 10.725 hepsi `catalog_v3` · v2 kalıntı=0 · T15/T20 SKU=0 · 25 beden × 11 genişlik · bozuk gram/fiyat/adet=0.
- **Fiyat:** breakeven altı=0 · metal maliyeti altı=0 · **tüm 10.725 kârlı** (min %24.9 · ort %35.7).
- **Üretici ↔ DB birebir:** GLD-R-1401-6MM-7=5.34g/$735; global aralık $160–$3.265 = DB min/max.

> Not: kâr marjı metal+kargo üstü brüttür; Etsy ücretleri (~%9-10) + işçilik
> düşülmemiştir (breakeven tabanı zaten ham metale %10 tampon ekler).

- Shop links: the 11 unique retailer/manufacturer URLs all return HTTP 200; the rest are Amazon **search** URLs, chosen deliberately because a search never 404s (spot-checked — all resolve).

## Heads-up: likely data bug (left unchanged here)
Sourcing photos surfaced three phones whose real image contradicts the `formFactor` in `data.ts`:
- **Emporia Simplicity** — actually a big-button **bar** phone (listed `flip`)
- **Gigaset GL590** — actually a **flip** (listed `candybar`)
- **Alcatel 2057** — actually a **flip** (listed `candybar`)

Left as-is to keep this PR to UI + photos; worth a follow-up since it affects the Format filter.

author: hussain-jafari
body:
### Description
- *Category*: implementation (+ data artifact loader, observer, test)
- *JIRA issue*: https://jira.ihme.washington.edu/browse/MIC-7289
- *Research reference*: https://vivarium-research.readthedocs.io/en/latest/models/risk_effects/hemoglobin/index.html#hemoglobin-effects

### Changes and notes

Implements two hemoglobin risk effects, each of the form `X_i = X · (1 − PAF) · RR_hgb_i` (RR a non-log-linear function of hemoglobin, normalized to RR=1 at the TMREL of 120 g/L, clamped to the 40–150 g/L endpoints per the general GBD-2023 modeling-strategy rule). Both reuse the existing `HemoglobinRiskEffect` pattern (analogous to the maternal-hemorrhage / maternal-sepsis hemoglobin effects already in the repo).

- **Artifact layer** (`8e0f399`): rename depression RR/PAF `affected_entity` `depressive_disorders`→`postpartum_depression`; wire the depression PAF (`depressive_disorders_paf`, previously dropped) into `risk_factor.hemoglobin.population_attributable_fraction`; re-tag the neonatal-sepsis generated PAF `affected_measure`→`cause_specific_mortality_risk`; add `load_hemoglobin_neonatal_sepsis_relative_risk` + `data_keys.HEMOGLOBIN.NEONATAL_SEPSIS_RELATIVE_RISK` (dedicated direct mediation-adjusted RR by child sex × neonatal age group × exposure).
- **Component layer** (`03d863c`): `HemoglobinRiskEffect` on `cause.postpartum_depression.incidence_risk`; new `NeonatalSepsisHemoglobinRiskEffect` on `cause.neonatal_sepsis_and_other_neonatal_infections.cause_specific_mortality_risk` — dedicated RR source, RR/PAF keyed on child sex × neonatal age group, `(1 − PAF)` applied via the cause `.calibration_constant` (verified no double-count with the LBWSG ACMR PAF).
- **Observer layer** (`ebe02f4`): trace the hemoglobin RR on neonatal sepsis (`NeonatalCauseRelativeRiskObserver`, same stratification as the LBWSG RR).
- **Review fix** (`27a45c4`): clamp <40 g/L sepsis RR to RR(40) (the inherited max-RR left-bin rule is correct only for the monotonic maternal curve; the non-monotonic direct sepsis curve needs the general endpoint rule); doc corrections.
- **Regression test** (`7c1e7aa`): InteractiveContext checks for both effects (skips until an artifact with the new keys is present).

> The prerequisite `vivarium-gbd-mapping` 6.x pin fix landed separately on `main` (`ef9fb9b`) so the artifact env builds.

### Verification and Testing

RR-vs-hemoglobin, live sim, draw 60, Ethiopia (patched artifact):

body:
## Summary

Adds the `whisper-dictate dictate-run` foreground CLI verb — the driver for the full Rust dictation runtime (hotkey listener + coordinator + `DictateSession` action sink + real backends when the required cargo features are compiled in). Runs until Ctrl-C.

**Audit item 5 Phase A step 1** — see [`docs/design/item5-wire-dictate-session.md`](../blob/main/docs/design/item5-wire-dictate-session.md) § "Phase A: dual-path infrastructure (safe)".

## No production behaviour change

The verb exists on disk but nothing invokes it in production. `src/python/whisper_dictate/runtime.py::_run_session` still constructs `Dictate(...).run()` unconditionally, exactly as today. The follow-up **Phase A step 2 PR** will add the `VOICEPI_DICTATE_ENGINE=rust` dispatch branch at `runtime.py::_run_session` that shells out to this verb when the operator has opted in.

Splitting Phase A into two PRs (verb, then Python dispatch) contains the blast radius: this PR is pure additive Rust infrastructure — it cannot regress the shipping PTT loop because no code path reaches it.

## What ships in this PR

- New `Command::DictateRun { config, json_events, foreground }` clap variant.
- `main.rs` dispatch to `runtime::dictate_run::handle_dictate_run`.
- New module `src/rust/runtime/dictate_run.rs`:
  - Feature-gated behind `rust-hotkeys,rust-injection` (matches the `self-test ptt-wedge` policy from #510). Stock build parses the verb but exits 1 with an actionable "rebuild with --features …" message so the Phase A step 2 Python parent can distinguish "feature not built" from a runtime failure it should surface.
  - Reuses `runtime::rust_session_sink::build_production_sink` so a change to the production sink is felt by both the supervisor and this verb (single source of truth for the sink construction).
  - `--json-events` emits a stable `{"kind":"ready","ready":true,"engine":"rust","chord":"…","driver":"…"}` envelope BEFORE the loop starts so a supervising Python parent can gate on it, then one JSON per `RuntimeEvent` observed.
  - Ctrl-C via the small cross-platform `ctrlc` crate (new unconditional dep, ~200 LOC of glue).
- 3 CLI parse tests + 5 handler tests (`split_key_names`, features gate, stock-build refusal).
- New section in `scripts/integration/wayland-user-smoke.sh` that verifies `dictate-run --help` works on the shipped binary.

## Explicitly out of scope (defer to step 2 PR)

- Any Python change (`runtime.py` stays byte-identical).
- `VOICEPI_DICTATE_ENGINE` handling anywhere.
- Any user-visible behaviour change.
- Version bump.

## What was tested locally (devcontainer, Ubuntu 24.04)

- \`cargo fmt --check\` — clean.
- \`cargo clippy --all-targets --features rust-hotkeys,rust-injection -- -D warnings\` — clean.
- \`cargo clippy --bin whisper-dictate -- -D warnings\` (stock) — clean.
- \`cargo test --features rust-hotkeys,rust-injection\` — 1489 lib + 34 sub-suite tests all pass.
- \`cargo test\` (stock) — 1424 filtered + 9 new dictate_run/CLI tests all pass; stock-build refusal test is included.
- \`whisper-dictate dictate-run --help\` — prints the help text on both feature-on and stock builds.
- \`whisper-dictate dictate-run\` on stock — exits 1 with the actionable rebuild message (see test output in commit body).
- \`bash scripts/integration/wayland-user-smoke.sh\` — new section reports \`✓ dictate-run --help works\`.
- Did NOT run \`dictate-run\` for real in the container — the loop needs a display server + audio device that headless containers don't provide. The Phase A step 2 PR will exercise the end-to-end path from Python.

## Ship discipline

- **Draft PR** — reviewer eyeball required before merge. Not arming auto-merge and not tagging.
- Signed commit (Ed25519, on-disk key). \`git log --show-signature\` verifies with \`gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile\`.
- No touching Python dictation code, no touching `VOICEPI_DICTATE_ENGINE`, no touching the recently-landed inject_guard / evdev / rdev drivers.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green (build, tests, clippy, sonar).
- [ ] Reviewer confirms no production code path invokes the new verb.
- [ ] Reviewer confirms the featured / stock refusal path.
- [ ] Reviewer sanity-checks the `--json-events` `ready` envelope shape (Python parent will pin these keys in step 2).

author: nlebovits
body:
Closes #235 (the pass-2 analogue of #233 / #234).

## Problem

In **partitioning** mode a level's render set is the accumulating row-group prefix `0..=end_k` (spec §5.1). Pass 2 processed each level independently: for level `k`, every wave read the prefix (bbox-pruned to the wave's combined bbox), so a coarse row group belonging to level `j` was re-read and re-decoded by every finer level `k >= j` once per wave. Measured on the 12-level moldova partitioning overview: **2,688,955** pass-2 row decodes for a 631,910-row file (~4.3×). Duplicating mode is unaffected (self-contained bands).

## Fix

Pass 2 in partitioning mode now reads the file **exactly once**: a dedicated reader thread streams every band in order over a bounded channel (mirroring `overview/pipeline.rs`), the consumer decodes each batch once and clips every feature at **every including level's zoom** (band `j` → levels `{j..N}`), routing each clipped member to a per-`(level, wave)` `MemberStore` bucket. The existing wave loop then drains the store — one wave of partitions at a time, in the historical ascending (level, partition, tile) order.

**Memory** follows the converter's pass-2 sink policy (`auto_backing`, now shared): small buffered sets stay in RAM; large ones spill bit-exact member records (coordinates and property floats as raw IEEE-754 bits) to a single temp file. During the fill the in-RAM buckets are capped at 128 MiB (largest-bucket-first segment flushes keep spill writes chunky and sequential); at fill end every bucket is flushed, so the drain holds only **one wave of partitions** — the same ceiling as before. The #311 per-level density guard and #303 wave preflight are unchanged and feed the same plan the store is filled against.

The legacy per-level wave-read path is retained: it is still the production **duplicating** path, and the byte-identity oracle for the new one.

## Byte-identical

- A member's clipped geometry is key-window independent (pinned by `recursive_split_is_partition_range_invariant`), so clipping once over the full key range and routing by key yields the members the per-wave range-restricted clips produced.
- Within-tile order is carried by `seq` — now the global row index in band order, which restricts to exactly the relative order the pruned prefix reads yielded — and `encode_members` sorts by the unique `(key, seq)`, so buffer/spill order is irrelevant.
- The drain replays the identical ascending `(zoom, x, y)` writer add-order.

Verified end-to-end on real data — old (`main` merge-base ce0cde8) vs new export of the 12-level moldova **partitioning** overview (`corpus/data/overviews/polygons-ftw-moldova-large.par.parquet`, multi-wave at the finest levels):

```
old.pmtiles  180,182,276 bytes  sha256 25bb85bb…6c1513
new.pmtiles  180,182,276 bytes  sha256 25bb85bb…6c1513   ← cmp: IDENTICAL
```

(Reproduced identically across three runs, including a spill-forced auto decision — the store auto-chose Spill on this input.)

New tests:
- `partitioning_single_read_pass2_matches_legacy` — pins the new path, under **both** backings and across `(partition_target, wave)` combos that force many partitions and multiple waves, to the legacy oracle (bytes + report).
- `partitioning_export_is_partition_invariant` — partition-target invariance of the production partitioning path.
- `member_spill_codec_roundtrip_is_exact` — bit-exact spill codec round-trip (all `Geometry` and `PropertyValue` variants, `-0.0` included).
- `member_store_spill_segments_roundtrip` — multi-segment spill store round-trip.

Existing anchors stay green: `export_archive_matches_pre_refactor_reference` (frozen hash, duplicating path untouched), `partitioned_export_is_partition_invariant`, `export_wave_width_is_byte_invariant`, `fanout_scan_matches_per_level_prefix_scan_partitioning` — 22/22 in `export::`, 13/13 in `pipeline::`.

## Performance — honest framing

moldova, 12-level partitioning, 16 cores, warm cache:

| metric | old | new |
|---|---|---|
| pass-2 row decodes | 2,688,955 (Σ per-wave pruned prefixes) | **631,910** (1× file) — **4.3× less decode** |
| wall clock | 19.3s | 18.7–20.7s (noise-level) |
| peak RSS | 1.58 GiB | 2.47 GiB |

Wall clock is neutral on this encode-dominated, page-cached export — the structural win is the provable 4.3× decode reduction, which grows with pyramid depth and matters most on large / cold-cache / slow-storage inputs. Peak RSS rises by a **bounded constant** (~0.5–0.9 GiB here): the 128 MiB fill buckets, spill read/decode transients, and per-member (rather than per-feature) property `Arc`s after spill decode, plus allocator high-water from the fill churn (under `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2` the pair measures 1.31 → 1.87 GiB). Scaling is unchanged — the buffered set spills, and the drain is `O(one wave of partitions)` exactly as before; the budget constant was measured to not be the driver (256 → 128 MiB moved RSS by ~1%).

### Fix

## What
Add error handling to the swap quote selection flow so failed gas-fee/quote
fetches are caught, surfaced to the user, and no longer flood Sentry with
expected errors.

Expected quote failures (e.g. "pair not available" and "insufficient funds for
gas price") were being reported to Sentry as unhandled exceptions, creating

author: andriipasternak31
body:
Fixes #1449

## What

Scrubs stale drain-replay **PII** from `schedule_executions.backlog_metadata` on
authoritative-terminal rows. `backlog_service.enqueue` `json.dumps`es the full
request — `user_message` / `user_email` / `system_prompt` — into that column so a
**queued** task can be reconstructed at drain. Nothing reads it once a row leaves
`status='queued'` (the drain claims only queued rows; the #1083/#1081 result
callbacks read the POST payload, not the row's metadata; canary E-04/G-04 are
queued-scoped), so on a terminal row it is stale PII sitting in the DB indefinitely
— bounded only by the 90-day `execution_row_retention_days` DELETE. This NULLs it as
soon as the row reaches a terminal state.

## How

- **`db.scrub_terminal_backlog_metadata(chunk_size)`** (`db/schedules.py`) — chunked
  `SELECT id … LIMIT N` → `UPDATE … SET backlog_metadata=NULL WHERE id IN (…)`, each
  chunk its own transaction (short write lock), mirroring `prune_execution_logs`.
  Facade delegate on `DatabaseManager`.
- **`cleanup_service._sweep_retention_772`** — appended as an **unconditional**
  sub-sweep (not age-gated, no ops-config key). Count feeds `CleanupReport` + the
  WAL-checkpoint sum; the blob itself is **never** logged (count-only — it carries PII).

### Two load-bearing decisions
- **FAILED is EXCLUDED** (`_AUTHORITATIVE_TERMINALS = success/cancelled/skipped`). A
  FAILED row is resurrectable to SUCCESS via a late token-gated CAS (`park_expired_lease`
  keeps its `claim_token`), so its drain-replay intent must survive. FAILED PII stays
  bounded by the 90-day row DELETE. (Regression-guarded by a dedicated test.)
- **Not an operator knob** — the scrub is a **security invariant**, so it has no
  retention window and runs every cycle even when all #772 windows are `0`. A fixed
  default sidesteps the #1638 floor-by-seed trap.

## Migrations / schema

**None.** This scrubs *values* in an existing column — no DDL, no new table, no
column. So there is **no dual-track (SQLite + Alembic) migration to add**, and the
`schema-parity` CI job is trivially green (no schema file touched).

## Tests

- `tests/unit/test_1449_backlog_metadata_scrub.py` (real DB via `db_harness`, not a
  mock): authoritative-terminal NULL-out, **FAILED-exclusion resurrection guard**,
  queued/running/pending_retry untouched, multi-pass chunking, idempotency,
  `chunk_size<=0` disabled, canary queued-scope smoke.
- `tests/unit/test_cleanup_inner_sweeps.py`: report field + WAL sum + "runs even when
  retention disabled" guards.
- `tests/unit/test_schedule_status_observability.py`: registers the new writer in the
  #1082 status-writer guard.

Local run: **35 passed / 1 skipped** (skip = Postgres dual-backend, no PG reachable);
canary + retention-prune regression sweep **142 passed**; `sys_modules` lint green.

## Docs

`requirements/infrastructure.md` §12.11 (RETENTION-002), `architecture.md` Cleanup
Service sweep line, `feature-flows.md` Recent-Updates row, and
`feature-flows/cleanup-service.md` all updated.

## Scope note (reviewer)

#1449 bundles two deliverables. This PR ships **only** the `backlog_metadata` PII
scrub (a live security win with zero pull dependency). The sibling — **callback/pull-path
chat-session persistence** — is **deferred to the #1081 single-applier work** (dead
code today: the callback path is unreachable by a manual `/task`, pull-mode is OFF),
with the verified design captured in the plan. The original bundled "reconciliation
sweep" design was **killed** in review — it would double-write live in-process-drained
chat rows. If you'd rather keep #1449 open for the deferred half, drop the `Fixes` to
`Refs`.

author: jrandallsexton
body:
## What

The home off-season countdown showed **wrong kickoff dates on both platforms**. This replaces guessed dates with the sourced one.

- **Web** hardcoded constants that had gone stale — NCAAFB read *74 days* to a Sept 29 that should have been Aug 29.
- **Mobile** *computed* kickoff from rules — NCAAFB "first Saturday of September", NFL "Thursday after Labor Day" — both wrong for 2026:

  | Sport | Rule computed | Actual (sourced) |
  |---|---|---|
  | NCAAFB | Sep 5 | **Aug 29** |
  | NFL | Sep 10 | **Sep 9** |

  NCAAFB has no fixed rule, and NFL's isn't a convention the league honors. A derived date is a guess that's plausible-but-wrong every year with no symptom — worse than web's loud staleness.

## Source of truth

The Regular Season phase (`TypeCode = 2`) `StartDate` of the sport's current season. Producer already has this in `SeasonPhase`; both 2026 phases are sourced with correct dates (confirmed against the DB).

## Design

Thin pass-through, no new persistence. Modelled as a **general per-sport season resource**, not a countdown-shaped endpoint.

**BFF vs. standard-endpoint line:** if it returned the *countdown* (`{ label: "NCAAFB in 43 days" }`, pre-computed for one UI) it'd be a BFF concern under `Application/UI/*`. It returns *raw* phase data for the client to interpret, so it's a standard endpoint and lives as a normal vertical slice under `Application/Seasons/`.

- **Producer** — `GetCurrentSeason` query + `GET seasons/current`. Resolves the current-or-upcoming season **from data** (earliest season whose `EndDate` is still future) with its phases. No calendar heuristic, and it naturally covers the Jan–Feb playoff window that broke naive `UtcNow().Year`.
- **Core** — `SeasonClient.GetCurrentSeason` + `CurrentSeasonDto` / `SeasonPhaseDto`.
- **API** — new `Application/Seasons/` slice: `GET api/{sport}/{league}/seasons/current`, per-sport via `ModeMapper`. One sport per call; the client asks per sport it surfaces.
- **Web + mobile** — both `PrimarySlotOffSeasonCountdown` components fetch per sport and read the `TypeCode 2` phase's `StartDate`. Deleted all hardcoded constants and the `ncaafbKickoff` / `nflKickoff` rules. A sport with no sourced season → "kickoff coming soon", never a wrong count. ISO strings throughout (no 0-indexed `Date.UTC` month construction).

Design doc: `docs/features/data-driven-season-countdown.md`.

## Testing

- Producer 5, API 3, mobile 2 new tests (current-or-upcoming resolution, phase projection/ordering, `NotFound` when unsourced, per-sport routing, `NotFound`/`BadRequest` propagation).
- Producer & API season suites **49 / 44** green; mobile **75 / 75**; web + both backend projects build clean.

## Reviewer notes

- **The "current" definition is the load-bearing decision.** Data-driven (`EndDate >= now`, earliest `StartDate`) rather than a year heuristic — worth a look at `GetCurrentSeasonQueryHandler`. It's what makes the Jan–Feb window and the off-season→next-season rollover both correct without special-casing.
- **Ops:** the API (`mode=All`) resolves each sport's Season provider URI via `SeasonClientFactory`, which falls back to a default key if `SeasonClientConfig:{FootballNcaa,FootballNfl}:ApiUrl` aren't set in `Prod.All`. A sport that can't resolve, or isn't sourced, renders "coming soon" — so if a countdown reads "coming soon" in prod, check that config first.
- **Follow-up (out of scope):** preseason pick'em leagues — the countdown window is where preseason games live, and `TypeCode 1` is available from this same endpoint if that's ever built.

## What this is

Groundwork so **oldman63 can finish the Hungarian translations in a PR**. This one adds the missing strings to the sheets; the actual Hungarian goes in on top (his credit).

## The situation

Every string oldman63 has already translated is compiled into the build. Hungarian is in fact the **most complete** language (FR/DE/PT/ES/IT are each 20-27 strings behind it). Nothing of his was dropped.

What was actually "not done": **39 on-screen strings were never added to any translator sheet**, so they render in English for every language, Hungarian included. Those are the ones he red-marked.

## Changes

1. **Removed a leaked template row** from `PLDR.I18N.HU` in `system.lua` (`["English (do not edit)"] = "Hungarian (put your translation here)"`). That was row 1 of the spreadsheet, injected by mistake. Whoever injects a `.tsv` next must skip the header row.
2. **Added all 39 strings to `hungarian.tsv` and `brazilian-portuguese.tsv`** as English-in-both-columns placeholders, with the exact keys, so a translator only overwrites the right column and the string still matches at injection time.

## Safety

- Every existing Hungarian row preserved **byte-for-byte** (verified: 0 lost, 0 altered, 39 added).
- Untranslated (`English == English`) rows are skipped on injection, so **the build is unchanged** until a translator fills them in.
- `system.lua` parses (lupa; the const-loop-var note is the known Lua 5.4 false positive), host harness 21/21.

## For the translator

The 39 new rows are the ones where both columns are identical. Fill in the right column with the Hungarian:

`(could NOT save -- reverts on reboot)`, `(the usual settings location wasn't writable)`, `-- launch cancelled`, `Adaptive BDMA couldn't stage`, `Applying SMB modules`, `BDMA source backend not ready:`, `BOOT.ELF failed to launch`, `Cannot access`, `Case/Symbols: UPPER  (R2)`, `Case/Symbols: lower  (R2)`, `Couldn't restore BDMA mode`, `Couldn't save settings`, `Couldn't update hidden state`, `Couldn't write .hide to the HDD`, `Cursor: L1 / R1`, `DKWDRV failed to launch`, `Edit`, `Game file missing`, `HDD dir read failed:`, `HDD not usable`, `Locating exFAT HDD POPS folder...`, `Looking for USB drive...`, `Missing BDMA UI source (tried):`, `Missing BDMA source (tried):`, `Missing SMB module (tried):`, `No '__.POPS' partitions on hdd0:\nformat one with __.POPS / __.POPS0...9`, `No DKWDRV found at this path`, `No POPSTARTER found at this path`, `Path saved, file not found:`, `Resolved:`, `Saved to`, `Slot:`, `Unknown BDMA mode:`, `You can still add a "<game>.hide" next to the .VCD from a PC.`, `adjusted -- using`, `check the memory card, or turn Adaptive BDMA off`, `re-select it under Settings > Storage to restage`, `return code:`, `status:`

author: fungc-io
body:
## What & why

The Angular single-page-app quickstart (`get-started/single-page-app/angular.md`) is out of date and no longer works if followed with current tooling:

- It instructs readers to edit `app.module.ts` / `app-routing.module.ts`, but the Angular CLI (17+) scaffolds **standalone** apps and generates neither file.
- `prompt: 'login'` no longer compiles with `@authgear/web` v5, which types the option as the `PromptOption` enum.
- `configure()` is called unawaited in `AppComponent.ngOnInit`, so it races `finishAuthentication()` on the redirect page and `fetchUserInfo()` on home. The SDK requires `configure()` to finish before any other call, so the redirect flow can land back on the home page still showing **Login**. (The doc already advised "render the app after `configure()` resolves" but the code didn't.)
- With zoneless change detection (the default on newer Angular), mutating the plain `isLoggedIn` boolean from the SDK delegate wouldn't update the UI.

This brings the tutorial in line with the sample project [`authgear/authgear-example-angular`](https://github.com/authgear/authgear-example-angular), which was upgraded to Angular 22 and verified end-to-end (login → redirect → home shows user info + Logout).

## Changes

- **Configure at bootstrap:** move `authgear.configure()` into `app.config.ts` via `provideAppInitializer`, awaited before render. Instantiate `UserService` first so its `onSessionStateChange` delegate observes the initial session state (fixes the "already logged in on load" case too).
- **Standalone components:** `app.routes.ts` + `provideRouter`, `RouterOutlet` import, `inject()` instead of constructor injection; drop the NgModule files.
- **Signals + `@if`:** session/loading/greeting state as signals so the UI updates under zoneless change detection.
- **SDK v5:** `prompt: PromptOption.Login`.
- Minor: `fetchInfo()` typo → `fetchUserInfo()`, refresh `angular.io` links to `angular.dev`, and a note about the CLI's new file-naming (no `.component`/`.service` suffix).

## Notes

- Targets Angular 17+; added an intro hint stating this and pointing older `NgModule` users to adapt.
- Kept the tutorial's structure, step numbering, GitBook hints, and images unchanged.

Closes #11
Closes #12

Implements approaches A + B from `docs/explainer-research.md` (#6). Stacked on the ui-teaching lane (base: `claude/lane-ui-teaching`); coordinates with its `?` interaction legend rather than competing with it.

## What changed

### #11 — pre-seed empty state (`public/preseed.js`, `public/preseed-pool.js`)
- Centered manifesto in the field, verbatim from the research doc: *"words condense out of latent space — they linger, then evaporate. / pin the ones that catch you; the rest is weather."*
- Meta-words about dewpt (starter pool from the doc, 7/6/5 entries by tier) condense and evaporate through motion mirrored line-for-line from `field.js`: same `.word t0/t1/t2` classes, same depth math (size/blur/opacity), same 5–10 s TTL, same drizzle-driven cadence, same reduced-motion guard. Dewpoint tier-weighting (the pinless branch of `tierWeights`) works pre-seed too, so raising dewpoint really does condense stranger meta-words.
- Static client-side pool — **zero network before session create** (verified: no `/api/` resource entries pre-seed).
- Teardown on `start()` (both seed submit and hash resume land there): timers cleared, manifesto and meta-words fade out with pointer-events off; a `torn` guard also covers the rAF fade-in race and the submit-during-resume-fetch race. URL-hash arrivals never see the pre-seed state at all (no manifesto flash).
- **Meta-word click behavior: focuses the seed input** (one of the issue's two sanctioned options — there is no session to pin into, so the click funnels to the one action that matters). Nothing can enter condensate or the evaporated sidebar from the pre-seed state (no pin/evaporate hooks exist there by construction).
- Screen readers: meta-words are `aria-hidden` (no live-region spam); the manifesto is mirrored in a static `.vh` element outside `role="application"`, the same pattern the hint line uses.

### #12 — "? what is this?" about panel (header)
- Worded toggle (`? what is this?`) styled like existing label copy; real `<button>` with `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`.
- Non-modal `aside` in the evaporated-sidebar family (`--hair` border, 14 px radius, `#171528` ground), anchored under the toggle via the same wrap pattern as the legend. No backdrop, no focus trap, nothing pauses — the spawn loop is untouched.
- Content, verbatim from the research doc: concept paragraph (incl. "ephemerality is the point" and "play, not productivity"), the dew-point name origin, the six-term glossary (dewpoint, altitude, drizzle, condensate, evaporated, condense / evaporate), and the linked Kevin Kelly credit.
- Closes via toggle, × button, or Esc; focus returns to the toggle on close. **Deliberately not closed on outside clicks** — it is a docked reading panel, and prospecting the field mid-read must not dismiss it.
- **Coordination with the ui-teaching `?` legend** (per the lane scope): clearly-distinct adjacent affordances — the worded header toggle is the concept layer, the bare `?` by the sliders stays the mechanics layer; they are mutually exclusive (opening one closes the other) and the panel cross-references the legend ("the moves themselves … are glossed under the ? beside the sliders").
- Open animation degrades to instant under `prefers-reduced-motion`; the manifesto/meta-word fades inherit the field's 0.5 s reduced-motion opacity path.

### Tests (TDD — written first, watched fail, then implemented)
- `test/preseed-pool.test.ts` — pool shape/lowercase/uniqueness, tier-weight curve parity with the demo formula, draw-never-repeats-visible, nearest-tier fallback, null only when the whole pool is on the field.
- `test/explainer-copy.test.ts` — pins the acceptance-criteria copy in `index.html` (manifesto lines, ephemerality framing, name origin, all six glossary terms, credit link, toggle semantics, hint line untouched).

- `npm test`: **106 passing, 0 failing** (5 files; 88 pre-existing + 18 new)
- `npm run typecheck`: **green** (tsc over src/test + scripts; `worker-configuration.d.ts` regenerated locally via `npm run types` — it is gitignored)

## Notes

- No server/generation changes; no new dependencies; vanilla HTML/CSS/JS only.

author: paolovalletta-exelab
body:
## What

Reopening a conversation from the playground sidebar now **reuses the same
`chatId`**, so the reopened chat continues the *same* conversation instead of
silently starting a new one.

## The bug

`LOAD_CONVERSATION` reconstructs the `chatId` from the conversationId so the next
turn addresses the same server-side conversation. It tested
`conversationId.startsWith("api-")`, but the real conversationId is
`${slug}:${channel}:${channelId}` (e.g. `assistant:web:api-<uuid>`) — the check
never matched, so the `chatId` became the *entire* conversationId. The next turn
then sent `chat_id = <full conversationId>`, the engine derived a fresh
`channelId = api-${that}`, and a **brand-new conversation** was created.

Symptoms: reopening a conversation lost thread continuity and any
per-conversation state (surfaced while testing per-conversation OAuth tokens —
the reopened chat asked to re-authenticate because it was, in fact, a new
conversation).

The existing tests hid this by using an unrealistic `api-abc` id rather than the
real `slug:web:api-abc` shape.

## Fix

Take the `channelId` (3rd `:`-segment) and strip the `api-` prefix. The recovered
`chatId` round-trips back to the original conversationId — the engine rebuilds
`channelId = api-${chatId}` (`openai.service.deriveChannelId`).

## Testing

- `npx vitest run --root packages/web use-chat` (17 pass; tests updated to the
  real conversationId shape + a round-trip regression test)
- `npm run typecheck -w @polyant/web`

author: ngha-boris
body:
## Objective

Every external service integration must expose a local/in-memory alternative alongside the production backend, selected at compile time via Cargo features rather than runtime configuration.

## Context

The server is currently hard-wired to production dependencies: PostgreSQL, AWS S3, AWS Secrets Manager, AWS Route53, and Redis. To keep CI fast, local development simple, and deployments portable, each integration should be wrapped behind a trait and gated behind Cargo features so that a fully in-memory build is possible.

This is a horizontal concern: each individual backend implementation is tracked in its own sub-issue, but this ticket establishes the pattern and fills the gaps.

## Deliverables

- [x] Agree on a crate-wide feature-naming convention (e.g., `postgres`, `sqlite`, `memory`, `aws-s3`, `redis`, `dns-route53`, `dns-cloudflare`).
- [x] Define the backend trait boundaries for:
  - status-list cache (#163)
  - certificate provisioning / store (#159)
  - certificate chain cache (#158)
  - DNS provider (#162)
  - signing-material / secrets store
- [x] Provide `memory` (or `sqlite` where appropriate) implementations for the backends that currently lack a local alternative.
- [x] Make `cargo build --no-default-features --features memory` produce a runnable minimal binary for local tests.
- [x] Ensure CI runs the test suite against the local backends.
- [x] Document the feature matrix in `README.md` and update `docker-compose.yml`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All production backends are selectable through Cargo features.
- No production credentials are required for default local development.
- Compile errors clearly indicate when a required backend feature is missing.

## References

- Related: #143 (database backend), #158 (cert chain cache), #159 (cert provisioning), #162 (DNS providers), #163 (status-list cache)

author: susomejias
body:
## Summary

Four independent robustness bugs in the shared shell plumbing (`apps/plugin/scripts/{_api.sh,_transcript.sh,prompt-nudge.sh}`) that cause silent data loss or hook/MCP split-brain. All four were empirically reproduced before fixing.

Closes #260.

## Fixes

- **`rembric_parse_dotenv` (`_api.sh`)** — now trims trailing whitespace from a value, not just leading. Bash's `[:space:]` class includes `\r`, so this closes both the plain-trailing-space case and the CRLF (Windows-saved `.rembric`) case in one fix. Previously a `.rembric` with trailing whitespace/CRLF resolved to a different slug in the bash hooks than in the JS bridge.
- **`rembric_json_escape` (`_api.sh`)** — now escapes every remaining C0 control character (U+0000–U+001F) as `\u00XX`, not just `\n \r \t`, matching what JSON (RFC 8259 §7) actually requires. A transcript containing e.g. a pasted ANSI escape byte previously produced invalid outbound JSON that the server rejected, silently dropping the session summary. `\x7f` (DEL) is deliberately left untouched — outside the JSON-mandated range.
- **`rembric_format_transcript_claude_code`/`_codex_cli` (`_transcript.sh`)** — no longer discard jq's already-printed partial output when a torn trailing line (a Stop hook racing an in-progress write, or a crash) makes jq exit non-zero. jq already streams output as it parses; the bash wrapper's `out="$(cmd)" || out=""` was discarding good data based on jq's exit code, not the data's validity. Removing the `||` is sufficient — a *total* failure still naturally yields `out=""`. The sibling title-extraction call sites (piped through `head -n1`, whose exit status is always 0) do not have this bug and were left untouched.
- **`prompt-nudge.sh`** — now fails closed (emits nothing) when its per-session counter file is unreadable/unwritable, instead of defaulting the count to `0` — which satisfies both firing thresholds (`0 % 5 == 0` and `0 % 10 == 0`) and spammed every nudge on every turn.

No breaking changes. No flag/env/protocol changes — same inputs, same outputs for every well-formed case; only malformed-input handling changes.

## Spec deltas

- `claude-code-plugin`: MODIFY the `_api.sh` helper requirement (C0 escape range + dotenv both-sides trim) and the `UserPromptSubmit` nudge-hook requirement ("fail safe" sharpened to "emit nothing," now explicitly covering an unwritable counter file).
- `plugin-session-protocol`: ADD a scenario to the summary-convergence requirement covering a torn trailing transcript line.

Archived at `openspec/changes/archive/2026-07-17-plugin-shell-robustness/`.

## Testing

- New `apps/plugin/test/api-sh.test.ts` — dotenv trailing-whitespace/CRLF trim, `rembric_json_escape`'s C0 range, DEL exclusion, and full JSON round-trip via real `bash -c "source _api.sh; fn ..."` invocations.
- Extended `apps/plugin/test/stop-sync.test.ts` — a torn-trailing-line transcript still produces a summary containing both good lines, asserted against the real POST body received by an in-process HTTP server.
- Extended `apps/plugin/test/prompt-nudge.test.ts` — `TMPDIR` pointed at a regular file (not a directory) so the counter can never be created; asserts empty stdout instead of spam.
- Full plugin suite green (83 tests).
- **Live e2e** against `pnpm run dev:docker:up`: `session-start.sh` with a `.rembric` carrying trailing whitespace (slug resolved correctly) → `stop-sync.sh` with a transcript containing a correctly-escaped control byte AND a torn trailing line → direct SQLite inspection of the persisted `sessions` row, confirming the summary contains both good lines and the control byte round-tripped intact. Full teardown after.

OpenSpec: plugin-shell-robustness

author: emiliano-go
body:
`import needle` pulled in HuggingFace `datasets` (and its `pyarrow`/`pandas`/`fsspec` tree) even though nothing on the inference path uses it. The tokenizer symbols that `run.py` and `__init__.py` need are defined in `needle/dataset/tokenizer.py` but were being imported through `needle/dataset/dataset.py`, which imports `datasets` at module level.

This repoints those imports at the module where the symbols are actually defined. Same objects, no API or dependency changes.

Closes #40 

### Changes

| File | Change |
| -- | -- |
| needle/__init__.py:14 | dataset.dataset → dataset.tokenizer |
| needle/model/run.py:11 | dataset.dataset → dataset.tokenizer |
| needle/dataset/__init__.py:2 | removed from .dataset import * |

**The third change is required, not cleanup.** `needle/dataset/__init__.py` executes on *any* `needle.dataset.*` import, so it triggers `datasets` before `tokenizer.py` is ever reached. Without it, the first two changes have no effect.

### Verification

```bash
python -c "import sys; import needle; print('datasets' in sys.modules)"
# before: True
# after:  False
```

- `needle.get_tokenizer`, `needle.generate`, `needle.load_checkpoint` all still resolve
- `get_tokenizer` is the same object as before (`gt1 is gt2`)
- `from needle.dataset.dataset import ...` still works; `datasets` loads lazily when training code actually runs

### Safety

No internal consumer relies on the star re-export. All existing imports are either submodule imports (`from ..dataset import dataset as data_mod`, `from ..dataset import generate as gd`) or submodule-qualified (`from .dataset import ...`), none of which are affected by removing it.

body:
## Summary

PR #185 made `consensus_threshold` and `similarity_threshold` per-run configurable via UI sidebar sliders, but every user-facing legend still hard-coded "≥ 75 %" and told readers thresholds live in `config.py`. When a user runs with a custom threshold, the rendered documents lied about what HIGH means.

body:
This pull request was created by @kiro-agent on behalf of @purendar950 :ghost:

Comment with **/kiro fix** to address specific feedback or **/kiro all** to address everything.
<sub>[Learn about Kiro Web](https://kiro.dev/web/)</sub>

---
## Problem

Deleted tasks kept showing up in the daily/evening Telegram reminders. The app maintains a tombstone ledger (`appState.deletedTaskKeys`) whose purpose is to stop a deleted task from a *regenerating source* (study-plan topic, mock/practice slot, course video, rolled-over task) from re-appearing. The in-app planner views honour this ledger, but **neither Telegram send path did**, so deleted items leaked back into the messages.

## Root cause

- `scripts/telegram-lib.js` → `buildTaskSections()` only filtered *done* tasks (`isDone`); it never checked the tombstone ledger, and it also re-materialised past-14-day incomplete tasks and course auto-scheduled videos.
- `js/features/telegram.js` → `buildTelegramDigest()` rebuilt the "Study Topics" section from the plan schedule map with no deleted-task filter, so a deleted plan topic regenerated into the stored digest.

The ledger is already persisted to Firestore as part of `appState`, so the server-side senders have access to it — they just never consulted it.

## Changes

- **`scripts/telegram-lib.js`**: ported the app's `taskDedupKey()` (same `ch:`/`vid:`/`txt:` signature format) and added `isTaskDeleted(appState, task)`. Applied the filter to all three sources in `buildTaskSections()` — today's tasks, the past-14-day preview, and course auto-scheduled videos. This covers both the morning and evening senders (they share this lib).
- **`js/features/telegram.js`**: `buildTelegramDigest()` now drops study topics whose `chId`/text signature is tombstoned, matching the planner views' behaviour.

## Testing

- `node --check` passes on both modified files.
- Wrote a functional harness that builds task sections with a mix of deleted (by text and by videoId) and kept tasks — confirmed deleted text tasks and deleted videos are filtered out while kept ones remain.

## Notes

- The two `taskDedupKey` implementations (browser + server lib) must stay in sync; a comment flags this in the lib version.
- No data-model or migration changes; relies on the existing persisted `deletedTaskKeys`.

author: chrox
body:
Fixes #5047

## Problem
Bulk-uploading many books to Readest Cloud froze the entire app until a force quit.

## Root cause
The library page subscribed to the *whole* transfer store with no selector:

```ts
const { isTransferQueueOpen } = useTransferStore();
```

A no-argument Zustand hook re-renders on **any** store change. During a bulk upload the store emits ~10 progress writes/sec per active transfer (×2 concurrent ≈ 20/sec), so this single line re-rendered the entire library tree ~20 times/sec and locked up the UI. It's platform-agnostic — on desktop the bytes stream through Rust, so the render storm, not the transfer itself, is what froze the app. This complements #5015 (which throttled the write *rate* but couldn't help while the page still subscribed to every write).

## Fix
Use a field selector so the page only re-renders when `isTransferQueueOpen` actually flips. It was the only non-selector transfer-store subscription in the codebase.

## Test
Adds a regression test that fires a 50-update progress burst: the old whole-store pattern re-renders 51 times, the selector renders once (verified failing→passing).

- `pnpm test` — 7603 passing
- `pnpm lint` (Biome + tsgo) — clean
- Verified in `pnpm dev-web` against a 704-book library: full grid renders, menus work, no console errors.

author: napetrov
body:
## Summary

The sticky PR comment reported a policy-gated but ABI/API-**compatible** addition (e.g. under `severity-addition: error`) with the headline "ABI BREAKING" — conflating "does this block CI?" (the gate axis) with "is this ABI/API-compatible?" (the compatibility axis), which ADR-042 explicitly established as independent.

## Motivation

With `severity-addition: error`, a new public function is correctly:
1. Still `COMPATIBLE` in the JSON report's `verdict`.
2. Correctly blocking CI with exit code 1.
3. But the sticky PR comment moved it into the "Breaking" bucket to match the red check, and the headline logic then said "❌ abicheck — ABI BREAKING" purely because that bucket was non-empty — regardless of whether it held a genuine incompatibility or a compatible finding promoted by policy.

This tells the reviewer "you broke the ABI" when the actual message should be "this compatible API expansion needs sign-off per your policy." The bug was locked in by an existing unit test asserting the old headline.

## Changes

- `abicheck/pr_comment.py`:
  - `Finding` and `CommentModel` now track the severity-config category (`abi_breaking` / `potential_breaking` / `addition` / `quality_issues`) responsible for each Breaking-bucket entry, threaded through `compare`, `appcompat`, and `compare-release` (release-mode `library_rows` + bundle/matrix global rows) modes.
  - The headline only reads **"ABI BREAKING"** when the bucket holds a genuine `abi_breaking` finding; a gated *source* break reads **"Source API break blocks this PR"**; a policy-only compatible block reads **"Public API expansion requires approval"** / **"Quality policy violation"** / a generic mixed variant — never "ABI BREAKING".
  - A new note block distinguishes the two axes explicitly for a policy-only block: `**Compatibility: COMPATIBLE** ... **Gate: BLOCKED** by severity policy — \`addition\` is configured as \`error\`.`
  - The Breaking section's own table title switches to "⛔ Blocked by policy (compatible)" in the same policy-only case.
- `action/run.sh`: the Job Summary's `SEVERITY_ERROR` line now names the actual blocking `severity.blocking_categories` from the JSON report (ADR-042) instead of a generic "Severity-level issue detected", when a JSON report is available (`FORMAT=json` + `jq`); falls back to the generic message otherwise.
- Tests: updated the existing tests that locked in the old "ABI BREAKING" wording, added coverage for addition-only / quality-only / mixed-category / real-break-plus-addition scenarios in `test_pr_comment.py`, and a new `test_action_run_sh_severity_summary.py` exercising the real `run.sh` snippet end to end.
- Changelog fragment added via `scriv create`.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added / updated for new behaviour
- [x] Changelog fragment added (`scriv create`)
- [ ] Docs updated if user-visible behaviour changed — the sticky-comment/Job-Summary wording change is documented in the changelog fragment and inline docstrings; no separate user-guide page describes the exact headline strings today
- [x] `ruff check abicheck/ tests/` and `mypy abicheck/` pass locally, plus the full fast unit suite (16,376 passed)

author: wo0jun
body:
## Summary

This PR contains my MVP proposal for Codex Inspector.

The goal is to help engineers answer two questions:

1. Which recent Codex sessions are worth reviewing?
2. What actually happened inside a selected session?

The core product loop is:

```text
compare sessions → select a session → inspect the evidence
```

## Demo

![Codex Inspector running inside Codex](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dylanjbarth/codex-inspector/24c17c57ad85a99c0b52cdfa330afe6a83264724/docs/images/codex-inspector-dashboard.png)

## Analysis scope

### Inter-session analysis

Used to compare workflows and find sessions worth inspecting.

- Token usage by session, including median, P90, and token-heavy sessions
- Turn count and total recorded turn time
- Compaction frequency and repeated-compaction signals
- Tool-call volume and completed/incomplete outcomes
- Longest measured tool calls
- Root-agent versus subagent token usage
- Number and depth of generated subagents

### Intra-session analysis

Used to explain what happened inside one selected session.

- Session token breakdown: fresh input, cached input, output, and reasoning output
- Per-turn token usage
- Turn duration and time to first token
- Turn completion status and compactions
- Tool names, outcomes, and recorded duration
- Child-agent relationships and subagent token usage

“Longest tool calls” is based on recorded duration because the current logs do not provide reliable per-tool token cost.

## How the information is presented

Inter-session and intra-session analysis are conceptually different, but I did not want to separate them into two disconnected dashboards.

Instead, the UI follows a connected `compare → select → explain` structure:

1. The top section summarizes overall Codex usage.
2. Sessions can be ranked by tokens, turn time, tool calls, or subagents.
3. Selecting a session updates its Session Story on the same screen.
4. The Session Story explains the session through token, turn, tool, compaction, and agent evidence.
5. Individual turns are collapsed by default and can be expanded to inspect their tool calls.

This keeps the connection between an aggregate signal and its underlying evidence visible.

## Codex integration

The MVP is implemented as a Codex plugin containing:

- A session-analysis skill
- A local MCP server
- A read-only analysis tool
- An interactive MCP App

The MCP App requests Codex’s expanded display mode so it can appear as an adjacent artifact panel, similar to the Data Analytics experience. If the host does not support that mode, it falls back to an inline dashboard.

The analysis runs against local Codex session logs. No separate browser extension or external dashboard is required.

## Key product decisions

- The target user is an engineer or Codex power user.
- Compaction is one review signal, not the entire product.
- High token usage or long duration is not automatically treated as inefficiency.
- Aggregate comparisons must always lead to inspectable session evidence.
- The MVP prioritizes deterministic metrics before subjective scoring.
- CSAT, memory reuse, usage-limit analysis, and external analytics integrations are left for later iterations.

## Validation

- 16 automated tests passing
- Analyzer, MCP, CLI, and interactive UI covered
- Session selection and turn expand/collapse verified
- Tested against real local Codex session logs
- Plugin schema validation passed

## How to try it

```text
[@Codex Inspector] Analyze my Codex sessions from the last 30 days
```

## Summary

PickAllReady already knows every issue in its loop is Dispatchable —
it just read them off `ListIssues(Dispatchable)`. Routing each one
through `PickIssue` re-checked InProgress and Complete anyway (2
`ListIssues` round-trips per issue) even though dispatch labels are
mutually exclusive (#707), so those checks were guaranteed to return
false. That's 2N wasted network calls on a bulk pick.

- Split `PickIssue`'s promotion step into `transitionToDispatchable`;
  `PickAllReady` now calls that directly, skipping the redundant
  checks. The single `p <num>` pick path (tea.go) still goes through
  `PickIssue` with the checks intact.
- Documents the TOCTOU tradeoff this reopens in `PickAllReady`'s
  comment: an issue that flips to InProgress/Complete between the
  snapshot and its turn in the loop still gets relabeled Dispatchable.
  Accepted as the same single-snapshot race the bulk gesture already
  has against issues becoming ready after it returns.
- Adds `Fake.ListIssuesCalls` (same pattern as `TransitionStateCalls`)
  and a regression test asserting `PickAllReady` makes exactly 1
  `ListIssues` call (was 1+2N) while still queuing and transitioning
  every issue.

author: wesley-allen-01
body:
## Problem
Docs-only change. For a multi-day unattended training run, the deploy guide had two observability/uptime gaps:
1. The launch command was a bare `uv run python main.py` inside tmux — if the process dies (OOM, CUDA error, network hiccup), the pod sits idle **and keeps billing** until someone notices.
2. No mention that W&B can push crash notifications to your phone.

## Change
- **Section 4 (Launch detached):** the launch command is now an `until` retry loop that restarts training after any non-zero exit (with a 10s backoff) and stops when training completes normally. Added a note on why this is safe: on each restart `main.py` auto-loads `checkpoints/latest.pth` and appends to the same W&B run, so a crash costs at most the progress since the last checkpoint (every 100 episodes). A Ctrl-C still exits the loop cleanly because the `KeyboardInterrupt` handler checkpoints and exits 0.
- **Section 5 (Monitor from your phone):** added instructions to enable "Run crashed" / "Run finished" alerts in W&B settings (email + mobile push) — the charts show training is going well; the alert tells you when it stops.

No code changes.

Implemented by a Haiku subagent, reviewed before push.

author: hubert-marek
body:
## Summary

Rebased replacement for #2945, now targeting `main` after #3032 merged.

- Carry renderer-produced multimodal samples end to end through SFT, including image-safe truncation, `mm_token_type_ids`, multimodal processor outputs, and cat packing.
- Load the model processor, attach it to the renderer, and save it with weight checkpoints.
- Add the dense Qwen3.5 composite VLM body (HF vision encoder + custom PrimeRL text model) with MRoPE positions derived from renderer metadata.
- Require custom PrimeRL implementations for VLM training and keep vision collectives symmetric across text-only and multimodal microbatches.
- Freeze vision encoders for text-only VLM training and fail invalid LoRA configurations with no matching targets.
- Enforce the VLM dtype, micro-batch-size, LoRA, and no-CP constraints in SFT config validation.
- Update the multimodal nightly config and add dense and MoE VLM SFT examples.

The branch preserves #3032's explicit `seq_lens` contract: trailing padding is merged into the final sequence segment and no separate padding metadata is transported.

## Validation

- `23 passed` — existing SFT dataset suite after the image-safe truncation fix
- `32 passed, 5 deselected` — focused non-GPU VLM model/forward/SFT tests using an import-only `ring_flash_attn` shim; no attention kernels were exercised
- `41 passed, 80 deselected` — config unit tests excluding external-plugin config loading
- Ruff format/check and diff checks passed
- Historical multimodal KL run: [custom Qwen3.5 VLM](https://wandb.ai/primeintellect/pr2485/runs/11cf49aa353d456fb5892a1944b30260), mean mismatch KL `0.0138`, step-0 KL `0.0025`
- Historical HF control: [Qwen3-VL](https://wandb.ai/primeintellect/pr2485/runs/4902c84180644e8ba8d5416bbab5a3c3), mean mismatch KL `0.1145`

Post-rebase CI fixes: the exact `examples/vlm_sft_moe/sft.toml` config test and an `sft --dry-run` validation both pass. The nightly RL VLM config now sets `impl = "custom"` in `[trainer.model]`, and obsolete GPU tests for removed modeling-layer validation were dropped.

Latest main merge: merged `main` at `445392294`; the README overlap retains the current multimodal docs anchor and keeps VLM CP marked unsupported, while main's obsolete debug-config deletion is preserved.

Cleanup: multimodal CUDA transfer is inlined in the singleton SFT collate path; the single-use helper was removed.

API cleanup: `[model.vlm]` now requires `model.impl = "custom"`. The dense and MoE custom VLM bodies accept token IDs only, share embedding accessors with their text-only bodies, and no longer carry unsupported `inputs_embeds` fallbacks or redundant modeling-layer validation. Multimodal samples without `[model.vlm]` still fail at the lazy dataset boundary.

Truncation follow-up: multimodal samples are now causal-shifted before image-safe truncation, keeping placeholder ranges, modality IDs, targets, and processor sidecars on the same model-input boundary.

Review follow-up: the multimodal processor is now loaded from `model.name`, so overriding `tokenizer.name` does not discard model-specific image preprocessing. `configure_trainable_parameters` is limited to LoRA application and frozen-vision discovery; router transforms and EP remain explicit in `setup_model`. LoRA keeps its existing initial freeze and logging, while EP performs the same conditional re-freeze as `main` after replacing parameters with DTensors. The VLM-specific vision freeze runs afterward.

Weight-tying follow-up: Qwen3.5 honors the checkpoint's standard tied-weight mapping. Checkpoints that omit `lm_head.weight` load the shared language embedding through the existing tied-model path without custom loader handling.

LoRA documentation follow-up: `freeze_vision_encoder` now promises parameter freezing only. The docs explicitly note that the default Qwen3.5 LoRA targets do not match vision modules, without claiming that arbitrary user-supplied target patterns are filtered.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches core training paths (model setup, forward, checkpoints, packing) and distributed VLM collectives; misconfiguration is mostly caught by validators, but multimodal truncation and vision/LoRA interactions need careful review.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **end-to-end multimodal SFT** for Qwen3.5 dense and MoE when `[model.vlm]` is set with `model.impl = "custom"`.
> 
> The SFT pipeline now carries renderer-produced `mm_kwargs`, `mm_token_type_ids`, and image-safe truncation through packing and the training forward; it loads an `AutoProcessor` from `model.name`, wires it into the renderer, and saves it with HF weight checkpoints. Config validation enforces VLM bfloat16 dtypes, `micro_batch_size = 1`, no CP, and rejects `freeze_vision_encoder=false` with LoRA; the old blocker that forbade VLM in renderer-only SFT is removed.
> 
> **Modeling:** Registers dense `qwen3_5` in the custom VLM map and extends `Qwen3_5ForCausalLM` / MoE VLM bodies with HF vision + custom text, MRoPE from renderer metadata, and dummy vision passes on text-only steps for distributed collective symmetry. Trainability is centralized in `configure_trainable_parameters` (LoRA + optional vision freeze after EP).
> 
> Docs and CI shift the multimodal story to Qwen3.5 (CP marked unsupported for VLMs); new example TOMLs cover dense and MoE VLM SFT.

author: osamaali313
body:
## Problem

In `GPT._compute_window_sizes`, the docstring describes the short window as `S=short (quarter context)`, and the code computes:

```python
short_window = -(-long_window // 4 // 128) * 128  # ceil to FA3 tile size (2048 -> 768)
```

This is `ceil(long_window / 4)` rounded up to the FA3 tile size of 128. For the default `sequence_len = 2048` it evaluates to **512** — which correctly matches the docstring's "quarter context".

The inline comment's worked example `(2048 -> 768)` is wrong: 768 is 3/8 of 2048, not a quarter. (768 would be the result for `long_window = 3072`.) It contradicts both the code and the docstring.

## Fix

Correct the worked example to `(2048 -> 512)`. Comment-only change; no behavior difference.

author: damianpapadopoulos
body:
## Why

User directive (2026-07-16, stated twice, escalated): SDLC phases must not be skippable; the enforcing mechanism must manage transitions and handover; this must live at the plugin level, not in agent memory. The problem is directly observed: with the composition chain rendered on every prompt, an agent session still skipped `writing-plans` entirely and compressed brainstorming's approval gate (discovery brief, archived). Prior evidence shaped the design: CURRENT-step directives reach 16/16 uptake while hint-adjacent advisories reach 0/5; the only deny-family backtest ever run here (PR #114) measured 56–94% false-block — so every new deny predicate is backtest-gated with pre-registered thresholds.

## What

- **`hooks/skill-gate.sh` (new, PreToolUse `^Skill$`)** — the sequencing gate: invoking a chain member while a required predecessor lacks evidence → hard deny with remedy (invoke the step, `phase_attest` with reason, or human `!` bypass). Implementation-slot aliases (`executing-plans`/`subagent-driven-development`/`agent-team-execution`) and DESIGN-slot aliases (`brainstorming`/`design-debate`) close sibling bypasses. Deny only on positive violation evidence — no chain / non-member / malformed state / infra error all allow (deliberate inversion of the push gate's fail-closed posture). Modes `deny|warn|off` with enum guard; default deny only in this repo (plugin-manifest identity), warn for external consumers.
- **Evidence provenance split** — gates trust `hooks/lib/phase-evidence.sh`: the completion hook's **append-only invocation record** (written only on successful Skill returns, independent of composition state) ∪ **branch ledger** (now records ALL chain-step returns, surviving re-anchors and session boundaries) ∪ **explicit attestation**. The walker-writable `.completed` is never consulted — a prompt trigger match is anchoring, not invocation (extends audit F1's provenance rule to all steps).
- **`hooks/lib/phase-attest.sh` (new)** — logged, review-surfaced skip-attestation. `requesting-code-review` and `verification-before-completion` are excluded by two independent locks (writer refuses, readers refuse even forged file entries — regression-pinned incl. direct-file-write forgery). Active attestations render under the composition block on every prompt, sanitized (newline/tab flattening, 200-char cap, "agent-recorded, verify before trusting" framing — the injection surface is pinned red-first).
- **`hooks/openspec-guard.sh` C2 leg** — chain-covered pushes missing DESIGN/PLAN evidence: telemetry-only warn (one-JSON-object contract preserved, regression-pinned against the routing-governance deny path). Deny mode is config-gated behind the backtest: **decision = NOT flipped** (replay inconclusive: 28/28 flagged sessions were ledger-covered cross-session continuations the replay can't see) — revisit 2026-08-14 on live telemetry.
- **`scripts/phase-gate-backtest.sh`** — advisory-only replay instrument (bidirectional error documented); controller-classified results archived with the plan.
- **Step-text promotion** — trifecta conditional moved into `brainstorming`'s `precondition` (16/16-uptake placement; superseded always-on hint retired); uptake eval pack authored at `tests/fixtures/phase-enforcement/evals/behavioral.json` (execution key-blocked).
- **Telemetry** — every gate decision logs to `~/.claude/.phase-gate-events.log` (size-capped at session start). Kill criterion armed: >10% user-judged false-blocks in 4 weeks → that predicate demotes to warn.

## Governance

Strictly additive on enforcement: existing REVIEW/VERIFY push-gate legs byte-untouched; attestation can never satisfy them; new libs joined `_GATE_ENFORCE_LIBS` (both canaries) and `_EVALUATOR_SURFACES` (paired-list rules). Codex adversarial sparring at plan stage (9 findings adjudicated: 7 accepted, 2 rejected with recorded rationale) + per-task adversarial reviews (2 Criticals caught pre-merge: walker-`.completed` trust, impl-slot alias bypass) + final whole-branch review ("Ready to merge: Yes" after spec-format, injection-sanitization, and doc-sync fixes).

## Heads-up for existing branches

In-flight branches predate the invocation record/all-step ledger, so the first SHIP-phase Skill invocation on an old branch in this repo may deny until earlier steps are invoked or attested — expected migration behavior, remedy text explains the options. Not a bug (cf. the "unexplained live deny" history).

## Test plan

- `tests/test-skill-gate.sh` (new, 72 assertions): all four spec scenarios red-first — sequencing deny/remedy/post-evidence allow; attestation satisfies-and-surfaces (incl. sanitization injection pin); gating milestones never attestable (incl. forged-entry and push-gate regression); scoping/fail-open matrix. Provenance pins (walker `.completed` never satisfies), alias pins (both slots), config-enum guard, C2 one-object contract, backtest fixtures.
- Full suite 95/95 under `/bin/bash` 3.2; OpenSpec validator green; push-gate suites (failclosed/detection/ledger/verdict/canary) all green.

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

issue #25854

## What this PR does / why we need it:

Fixes #25854.

pSpool manages message slots and cached batches in two independent pools. The normal release path returned both objects but retained the old batch, error, and cache metadata in the released slot. When the cached batch was reused by another slot, Abort could clean the stale free slot and thereby clear a batch still owned by a receiver.

This PR restores the ownership boundary:

- Detach all message metadata before returning the batch to the cache or publishing the slot to the free pool.
- Reuse the same clear operation for direct cleanup so normal, aborted, and late-release paths have one invariant.
- Cover the free-slot invariant and the stale-alias sequence for both a single receiver and a two-receiver broadcast.
- Cover concurrent Abort and final broadcast releases over all lock orderings.
- Verify current data remains readable until the final ReleaseCurrent and all MPool memory is reclaimed afterward.

The release path adds no locks, goroutines, allocations, scans, atomic operations, or extra helper calls. It only clears a fixed-size slot at the existing final-reference release point.

body:
## Summary
Adds two end-to-end tests covering the double-box prevention guarantee
from #707: drive `PickIssue`'s rejection of an already-InProgress or
already-Complete issue through `teaModel.landPick`'s message wiring and
`Queue.Discover`/`RunContinuous`, instead of asserting only on
`PickIssue`'s own return value and `TransitionStateCalls` (the existing
`pick_adapter_test.go` unit tests).

Per the research verdict on #985: a `PickIssue`-rejected issue lands
`PickDissolved`, never `PickQueued`/`PickHeld`, so `claimable()`
(queue.go) structurally excludes it from `Discover`'s claim step —
there's no state-check branch inside `Discover` itself for this case.
The new tests prove the wiring end to end (adapter -> message handling
-> queue -> discoverer), not a branch that doesn't exist.

Both tests were checked against a real regression: temporarily
loosening `claimable()`'s filter alone still didn't let a dissolved
pick launch (`tryMarkClaiming` re-checks state as a second gate); only
loosening both gates together let a Box launch, which the tests then
caught (`RunCalls`/`TransitionStateCalls` go non-zero). Both mutations
were reverted before committing.

No production code changed — this is test-only, matching the issue's
scope.

Closes #985
