## Résumé

Première tranche de **skycode** — la plateforme de contrôle des process de revue de code multi-repo. Cette tranche pose la fondation web : authentification email/mot de passe et coquille applicative navigable. Pas encore de logique repo/revue (tranches suivantes).

Ce qu'un utilisateur peut faire : **créer un compte**, **se connecter**, **se déconnecter**, et atterrir dans une coquille sidebar avec une page « Repos » en état vide et un menu compte.

## Ce qui change

- **Stack** : Next.js 16 (App Router) + TypeScript, better-auth (email/password, sessions cookie httpOnly), PostgreSQL via Drizzle ORM + Docker Compose, Tailwind + shadcn/ui.
- **Auth** : instance better-auth serveur (`src/lib/auth.ts`), handler de route `api/auth/[...all]`, client React, schéma Drizzle (`user`/`session`/`account`/`verification`) + migration.
- **UI** : formulaire d'auth partagé (carte centrée, bascule connexion ⇄ inscription), pages `(public)/login` et `(public)/register`, coquille protégée `(app)` avec garde de session server-side, sidebar, menu compte (email + déconnexion), page repos en état vide.
- **Validation** : helper pur `validateCredentials` (email + mot de passe ≥ 8), aligné sur `minPasswordLength` serveur.
- **Docs** : README (but + setup), CLAUDE.md racine (stack + pointeurs), spec et plan sous `docs/superpowers/`.

## Périmètre exclu (par design, tranches suivantes)

Vérification d'email, mot de passe oublié, OIDC, invitations, gestion réelle des repos/revues. Les liens sidebar `Revues`/`Activité` pointent volontairement vers des pages à venir.

## Plan de test

- **Unit (Vitest)** : `validateCredentials` — 4 tests, 4 branches. `npm test`
- **E2E (Playwright)** : parcours complet inscription → `/repos` → déconnexion → connexion, garde d'accès sans session, rejet mot de passe trop court. `npm run test:e2e` (requiert `npm run db:up && npm run db:migrate`)
- Les deux suites passent en local (4/4 unit, 3/3 e2e).

## Notes pour le reviewer

- Le champ `name` requis par better-auth est dérivé de la partie locale de l'email (l'UI ne collecte qu'email + mot de passe).
- `.env` est gitignoré ; seul `.env.example` est committé. Configurer `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` avant de lancer.
- Revue de code interne passée : 0 problème critique/important.

Adds a playable mini-golf minigame at `/putt` ("🕹️ Arcade Putt" on Home).

**Gameplay** — two taps per shot: lock the sweeping aim arrow, then tap the oscillating power meter to fire. The ball rolls with friction, bounces off the rails and obstacle walls, and drops in the cup when it arrives slowly enough (near-misses get a gentle magnet nudge). Three holes, per-hole birdie/par scoring, a final scorecard, plus spacebar / tap-canvas shortcuts.

**Implementation** — `src/features/putt/PuttGolf.tsx`: a single `requestAnimationFrame` loop drives physics off a ref, so React only re-renders on phase changes. Circle-vs-AABB collision with sub-stepping prevents fast shots tunneling through thin walls. Entirely client-side — works offline, no API calls.

Validated the physics in a standalone Node simulation: hole 1 sinks across a wide power window (0.22–1.0), walls block rather than tunnel, and all three holes are provably sinkable.

author: aidanlsb
body: ## Problem `REF_NOT_FOUND` was used as **both** a fatal error (read/resolve failures, `ErrRefNotFound`) and a benign warning on permissive writes (`WarnRefNotFound`). Agents could not branch on the code alone — they had to combine `ok` + context, and a successful write with broken refs looked like clean success if warnings were ignored. Remediation was also CLI-string only (`create_command: "rvn new person ..."`), forcing MCP agents to shell-parse the string into an invoke payload. ## Changes 1. **Distinct warning code.** Added `REF_TARGET_MISSING` (`codes.WarnRefTargetMissing`, registered in `internal/codes`) for successful, permissive writes that introduce a reference to a missing target. `REF_NOT_FOUND` remains the fatal error code for read/resolve failures. The stale `WarnRefNotFound` warning code (and its `internal/cli` alias) is removed since it is no longer emitted, eliminating the dual meaning. 2. **Structured remediation.** Added `create_invoke: {command, args}` to the warning envelope (`commandexec.Warning.CreateInvoke` / new `commandexec.Invoke`), alongside the existing `create_command` string. For an inferred type it produces `{command:"new", args:{type, title, path}}`; otherwise it falls back to `{command:"check create-missing", args:{confirm:true}}`. The `create_command` string was also fixed to use `--path` (the previous form passed the full slashed path as the title, which `new` rejects). 3. **Docs / agent guides updated** to reference `REF_TARGET_MISSING` and the structured `create_invoke`: `docs/types-and-traits/references.md`, `internal/mcp/agent-guide/{write-patterns,response-contract}.md`, `internal/commands/registry.go` command long-descriptions, and `CHANGELOG.md`. 4. **Tests.** Write-path integration tests now assert the `REF_TARGET_MISSING` code plus structured `create_invoke` (type/title/path). Added `commandimpl` unit tests for both the inferred-type and unknown-type (fallback) branches. Read/resolve paths still use fatal `REF_NOT_FOUND` (unchanged). `internal/testutil` `CLIWarning` gained `suggested_type` / `create_command` / `create_invoke` fields so envelope parity (MCP vs CLI) continues to cover the new fields. ## Deliberately out of scope Opt-in strict mode (fail writes that introduce missing refs) was listed as optional. It would require intercepting the permissive-write result across ~7 call sites in `new`/`set`/`add`/`edit`/`upsert` plus a new config/flag surface, which is more invasive than "no large redesign" allows. Default permissive-write behavior is preserved; strict mode can be a focused follow-up. ## Validation - `make fmt` / `make fmt-check` — clean - `make lint` — 0 issues - `make test` — pass - `make test-integration` — pass - Manual smoke test confirmed the new envelope shape and that running the suggested `create_invoke` (`new --path people/ghost`) creates the page at the exact target, resolving the missing ref.

## Summary

This PR classifies those commands (`self version`, `tool dir`, `auth dir`, `help`, `cache dir`, `cache size`, and `python dir`) as synchronous, then polls the shared command future once without an executor. author: danribbens
body:
## What?

Upgrades `drizzle-orm` and `drizzle-kit` from `0.44.x` to **`1.0.0-rc.4`** across all Drizzle-backed database adapters (`db-postgres`, `db-sqlite`, `db-vercel-postgres`, `db-d1-sqlite`) and the shared `@payloadcms/drizzle` package.

Drizzle 1.0 ships **Relational Query Builder v2 (RQB v2)**, which changes how `db.query.<table>.findMany()` works internally — most notably it now **aliases the base table** and exposes a different internal adapter shape. This required reworking Payload's read path, schema build, and migration tooling to match the new API.

## Why?

- Keep Payload current with Drizzle's stable 1.0 line and its RQB v2 performance/feature improvements.
- The old `0.44.x` internals (`db.drizzle._.schema`, `column.table`, static `with` typing, non-aliased base table) no longer exist in 1.0, so staying on the old API is not viable going forward.

## How?

**Adapter + schema layer**

- Bumped `drizzle-orm`/`drizzle-kit` to `1.0.0-rc.4` and updated adapter `types.ts`, `connect.ts`, and `requireDrizzleKit.ts` for the new drizzle-kit entrypoints.
- Reworked `buildDrizzleRelations`, `buildDrizzleTable`, `geometryColumn`, `defaultSnapshot`, and `createSchemaGenerator` for RQB v2 relation/table definitions.
- Replaced removed internals: `getNameFromDrizzleTable`/`column.table` → `getTableName`/`getColumnTable`/`getTableNameFromColumn`.

**Read path (RQB v2 base-table aliasing)**

- `find/traverseFields.ts`: join/count `extras` are now **callbacks receiving the aliased parent table**, so correlated subqueries reference the alias instead of the real table name.
- `find/findMany.ts`: `where`/`orderBy` are wrapped in `{ RAW: (table) => … }` callbacks; ordered IDs are pre-resolved via a manual select (real table names) so the relational fetch filters by primary key.

**Test-suite fixes** (`fix: failing tests`)

- `resetDB` (test helper) read the now-`undefined` `db.drizzle._.schema` and silently cleared nothing → every suite's seed inherited stale rows. Switched to the adapter's `db.tables` registry + `getTableName`.
- `selectDistinct`: added a caller-controlled `disableDistinct` flag. `findMany` sets it when there are no joins (it selects the unique PK), avoiding an invalid `SELECT DISTINCT … ORDER BY <expr>` for the `near` geospatial operator while `findDistinct` keeps true DISTINCT semantics.
- `deleteOne`: `forceRun` routed all deletes through a bare `findFirst` without the `with` clause, dropping localized/relationship fields from the returned doc → now uses `buildFindManyArgs`.

## Known limitations / follow-ups

- **Per-find extra query**: RQB v2 base-table aliasing forces a separate ID-resolution query per find. This trips the DB-query-count guardrail tests (`access-control/postgres-logs`, `queues/postgres-logs`); **left as-is for now** pending a follow-up that maps `ORDER BY` onto the aliased `db.query` columns.
- **`migrate-to-blocks-as-json`**: blocked by an upstream drizzle-kit v1 `generateMigration` `HintsHandler` bug (see `drizzle-v1-generateMigration-hints-bug.md`).
- **`db-mssql`**: drizzle 1.0.0-rc.4 mssql lacks RQB v2 (`db.query`), so that adapter remains blocked. See issue: https://github.com/drizzle-team/drizzle-orm/issues/6052

The renderer's output is a CPU pixel buffer, so the app shell shouldn't be setting up a graphics API. ## Description

Adds a Playwright E2E suite for the staff app in `frontend/staff/e2e/`, mirroring the portal's harness. It reuses the fake-MSAL test auth over the **shared localStorage token contract** (`src/auth/testAuth.ts`), seeds a known baseline through the CLI seeder + public API (never direct DB writes), and uses **origin-scoped storage states** so one token-minting harness signs identities into either the staff app (`:5198`) or the portal (`:5199`) against a single API (`:5299`). Playwright serves **both frontends simultaneously** so the cross-app scenarios work.

### Scenarios covered

1. **Auth & role gate** — staff sign-in reaches the dashboard; admin-only nav hidden from plain staff and admin pages blocked; org admin sees them; expat and unprovisioned identities both hit the access gate.
2. **RFP lifecycle + cross-app** — create → Draft → Approve (bare confirm) → Publish (confirm-with-summary) in the staff UI; the portal shows the published RFP; an edit-after-publish reaches the portal without re-approval; delete removes it.
3. **Proposal review loop + cross-app** — Submitted → Under Review → Approved; the expat's portal *My Proposals* shows `Approved`; no reject affordance anywhere.
4. **Takedown cascade** — deleting a proposal removes its CFEOI + EOI (portal contributor's *My EOIs* no longer lists it; API confirms).
5. **Staff EOI management** — approve/reject Pending EOIs, see `Private` submissions + the email column, delete via the checkbox-gated modal.
6. **Administration** — org-tree CRUD incl. the bootstrap empty state and the **409 refusal** on deleting a non-empty org (server message rendered); user management with client guards and the **self-delete 403 / last-org-admin 409** server backstops.
7. **Visibility integrity** — a `Private` proposal is visible in the staff *All proposals* tab yet invisible to an anonymous portal session (UI + API).

- **CORS:** `appsettings.E2E.json` only allowed the portal origin, so the staff app's API calls were blocked — added `http://localhost:5198`.

gfargo-horizon-agent[bot]
body:
## What
Every commit-producing atom used inside a `withRemoteTracking` scope now continues the **parent repo's** deterministic commit clock, instead of restarting at the `2020-01-01T00:00:00Z` epoch for the scope's temporary clone.

## Why
Closes #96

Plane: [OSS-898](https://compass.tailb82ead.ts.net:3443/gfargo/browse/OSS-898/)

Only `commitAll` continued the parent's clock (`nextCommitDate(parentRepo.path)`). Every other commit atom used inside the scope — `commit`, `emptyCommit`, `bulkCommits`, conflict atoms — called `nextCommitDate(repo.path)`, which inside the scope resolves to the clone's own path: a brand-new clock key starting at the epoch. That let upstream commits reuse or overlap the parent's own commit timestamps, making `git log --graph --all` ordering non-deterministic between replays — the exact failure class the commit clock exists to prevent. This was masked because every documented `withRemoteTracking` example uses `addCommit`, which happens to route through `commitAll`.

## How
- Seed the clone's clock (`setCommitClockCount(clonePath, getCommitClockCount(parentRepo.path))`) right after `mkdtemp`, before any commits happen inside the scope — so a fresh `nextCommitDate(clonePath)` naturally continues the parent's sequence instead of restarting.
- Switch `commitAll` to read from `clonePath` (now seeded) instead of `parentRepo.path` directly, so it's consistent with every other atom, which already reads `repo.path` (== `clonePath` inside the scope).
- Propagate the clone's advanced counter back to the parent (`setCommitClockCount(parentRepo.path, getCommitClockCount(clonePath))`) and reset the clone's clock entry in the `finally`, so post-scope parent commits continue past everything the scope produced and the clock map doesn't leak `clonePath` keys.

## Testing
- [x] build passes
- [x] tests pass / added (new test in `src/atoms/upstream.test.ts` mixes `commit`/`emptyCommit`/`bulkCommits` inside the scope with parent commits, replays twice for identical SHAs, and asserts a strictly-increasing, non-tied chronological chain across the whole scenario)
- [x] lint clean
- CI: pending

author: kevin-lucifer
body:
## What

Fixes a race condition where Telegram startup notifications fail with `send_path_degraded` after planned gateway restarts.

## Root Cause

The Telegram adapter's `_send_path_degraded` flag is set during polling initialization and only cleared after the first successful `getUpdates`. On networks requiring fallback IPs (DoH discovery + retry), this can take >1 second. The gateway only waited `1.0s` before sending startup notifications, so the send was rejected.

## Fix

After the initial 1.0s settle wait, poll all adapters for the `_send_path_degraded` flag and wait until it clears (max 10s) before sending startup notifications.

## Testing

- 26/27 restart notification tests pass
- The 1 failing test (`test_restart_command_uses_detached_without_systemd`) is environment-related (systemd detection in containers) and fails both before and after this change

## Related Issues

- Fixes #66589
- Related: #65057 (same root cause, shutdown phase)

author: jdev-02
body:
Adds one class and its game-frame rules to the cybersecurity ontology under development/.

**AdversarialKnapsack (subclass of Contest).** A Contest between AutonomousAgents competing under resource constraints. Formalizes the Adversarial Knapsack game from arXiv:2403.10789. Scope of this PR is the game frame: participants and their budget hookup. The behavioral content of the game (exploit and patch action selection, zero-sum utility, per-vulnerability cost accounting) is out of scope here and will follow in subsequent Cyber.kif PRs.

**Two-participant structural rule.** Every AdversarialKnapsack has at least two distinct AutonomousAgent participants under contestParticipant.

**Participant-budget hookup.** Every contestParticipant of an AdversarialKnapsack has an operationalBudget. This is the wire from the game frame into the knapsack constraint machinery already in Cyber.kif (violatedKnapsack + aggregateCyberCost > operationalBudget).

**Witness.** An AdversarialKnapsack exists whose two participants have distinct budgets, since the two sides of the game are not required to be symmetric.

**Coverage.** Every claim in the documentation string is backed by an axiom in this file.

**Validation.** sigma-fullcheck reports "No errors found in Cyber.kif". All other errors in the run trace back to unrelated upstream modules (loadBearingRegion, PorousContainer, accreln1 modal encoding) and appear zero times in Cyber.kif.

author: justin-stanley
body:
## OSSF Scorecard SAST finding (score 9/10)

> "SAST tool detected but not run on all commits: 5 commits out of 7 are checked with a SAST tool."

### Grounded root cause

Scorecard's SAST check samples recent **merged PRs** and looks for a CodeQL / `github-code-scanning` check-run on each. Verified via `gh pr checks`:

| PR range | CodeQL check-run? |
|---|---|
| #26–#30 (merged 2026-07-14 onward) | ✅ present (`Analyze (javascript-typescript)` + `CodeQL`) |
| #20–#25 (merged before #26) | ❌ **none** |

The cause is **the trigger, not a path filter**. Until PR #26 (`4cd6f94`, merged 2026-07-14) the CodeQL workflow ran only on `push: [main]` + `schedule` — it had **no `pull_request` trigger**, so PRs merged before #26 never produced a CodeQL check-run in their PR context. Those pre-#26 PRs are the ones Scorecard counts as "unchecked." The current workflow already has **no `paths:`/`paths-ignore:` filter**, so config-only PRs (Cargo.toml, fly.toml, *.yml) already get a run — confirmed on #27/#28/#29.

So the **forward fix already landed in #26**: every PR now gets a CodeQL run. The current Scorecard finding is a lagging artifact of the pre-#26 PRs still in the sampling window; it clears on its own as newer PRs age in.

### What this PR does

Since the trigger is already correct, this PR **hardens and documents the guarantee so it can't silently regress**, and fixes stale docs:

- **`codeql.yml`** — adds a triggers/coverage comment block making explicit that **no `paths:`/`paths-ignore:` filter may be added** (a path filter would skip config-only PRs, drop the check-run, and regress the Scorecard SAST score). Triggers are unchanged: `pull_request` → `main` + `push` → `main` + weekly `schedule` + `workflow_dispatch`. All actions stay **SHA-pinned** (`# vX` comments preserved); no floating tags introduced, so Pinned-Dependencies is unaffected.
- **`README.md`** (workflows) — corrects the now-stale CodeQL row/notes, which still described the old "push + weekly cron only, not every PR" trigger and wrongly listed a `rust` CodeQL leg that was dropped. The stale text invited a contributor to "restore" the narrow trigger and regress Scorecard.

### How every future PR gets a SAST run

`on: pull_request: branches: [main]` with **no path filter** and a single always-on `javascript-typescript` matrix leg means every PR — including config-only ones — produces a `CodeQL` check-run that gates on `main` before merge.

### CI-cost note

The Rust CodeQL leg stays dropped (its public-beta extractor errored on all files here; Rust is covered by clippy `-D warnings` + cargo-deny + cargo-audit), so the per-PR CodeQL cost is just the ~1-minute JS/TS analysis of the OAuth sidecar. On the public repo, GitHub-hosted Actions + code scanning are free, so there is no marginal cost. No build-heavy Rust analysis is added.

### Validation
- `actionlint .github/workflows/codeql.yml` → clean.
- Triggers / permissions (`security-events: write` + `contents: read`) / matrix unchanged and correct.

Note: `main` is protected (strict/up-to-date) and moving fast; if this PR goes out-of-date, leave it open — no merge/deploy requested.

## Qué hace

Nueva sección **Biblioteca de materiales** (`AdminMateriales.tsx`) para alojar distintos tipos de material de capacitación — documentos, presentaciones, imágenes, enlaces de video — y adjuntarlos a las actividades obligatorias existentes (la única "asignación de cursos" que tiene la app).

- **Origen del material**: archivo subido (PDF, Word, PowerPoint/Excel o imagen, máx. 20 MB, bucket privado `materiales` en Supabase Storage) o enlace externo (video de YouTube/Vimeo/Drive, u otro enlace). Nunca ambos.
- **Privacidad**: bucket privado + `createSignedUrl` al momento de ver el archivo — la seguridad la da RLS, no una URL adivinable.

- El relator ve chips de los materiales adjuntos en cada actividad pendiente (`Actividades.tsx`), con ícono según tipo y apertura directa (signed URL o enlace externo).

## Por qué 20 MB y sin video subido

El plan gratuito de Supabase da 1 GB de Storage total — un solo video lo agotaría. El video vive siempre como enlace externo.

- Tabla `materiales` (con `check` de origen único: `storage_path` XOR `url`).
- Tabla puente `actividad_materiales` (N:N con `actividades`).

author: jasmine-nguyen
body:
## What & why

The batch-save + reconcile logic was **duplicated** across two writers in `src/context.tsx`:
- `applyCategory('all')` (the "All from this merchant" sweep)
- `applyCategoryToMany` (multi-select re-file)

Both did the same thing: chunk under `CATEGORY_BATCH_LIMIT` → `Promise.allSettled` the chunk saves → reconcile saved ids **by id** → compute failed ids. Two copies meant a future change (e.g. a new server result status) had to land in both — the "two repository copies" drift the AGENTS.md landmines warn about.

This extracts that common middle into one module-scope helper:

```ts
persistCategoryBatch(ids, categoryId) => Promise<{ savedIds, failedIds }>
```

Both writers call it and keep their **own** optimistic write, rollback strategy (blanket-null for the sweep vs `previousById`-restore for multi-select), and toasts.

## The one subtlety: concurrency in the `'all'` path

The `'all'` path creates a BankSync **rule** at the same time as the batch save — originally both shared a single `Promise.allSettled([createEnrichment(...), ...chunks])`, so they ran **concurrently**. The helper owns only the batch, so the rule call had to be restructured carefully. This is worth understanding, so here's the wrong way vs the right way:

```ts
// ❌ WRONG — serialises the rule after the batch, AND lets a rule rejection float
//    as an unhandled rejection during the await if it fails mid-batch:
const { failedIds } = await persistCategoryBatch(sameMerchantIds, categoryId);
const [ruleOutcome]  = await Promise.allSettled([createEnrichment(...)]);  // starts too late

// ✅ RIGHT — rule starts NOW (concurrent with the batch) and its rejection handler
//    is attached synchronously, so it can never float:
const ruleSettled       = Promise.allSettled([createEnrichment({ value: ruleValue, categoryId })]);
const { failedIds }     = await persistCategoryBatch(sameMerchantIds, categoryId);
const [ruleOutcome]     = await ruleSettled;
```

The right version preserves all three properties of the original: **concurrency** (rule + batch in flight together), **call order** (rule issued before the charges), and **rejection safety** (no unhandled rejection if the rule fails while the batch is awaited). A test locks the call order and asserts no unhandled rejection fires.

## Folded-in tweak: honest sweep toast (approved in review)

Separately, the `'all'` sweep toast now reflects what actually happened:
- files ≥1 charge → `"N transactions filed — future … charges file as …"` (names the count + the future rule)

author: nonokia
body:
Closes #38. Adds Gradle build graphs to the ADR-2 multi-language path as a subprocess reference plugin (ADR-7). This is the last of the five open extractor issues.

## The judgment the issue asked for first (recorded in dlog)

**The Gradle Tooling API is rejected; v1 is syntax-level.** The Tooling API is the official implementation, but it *evaluates the target build* — plugin resolution, dependency downloads, arbitrary script execution — which is non-deterministic across runs and environments, and the determinism invariant is what ADR-4's measurement discipline (and byte-identity checks like `selfindex:check`) rest on. The declarative subset that matters for the build graph (`include`, `project(":x")`, task declarations / `dependsOn`, plugin ids, catalog accessors, Maven coordinates) is **string-literal-level in both DSLs**, so a Go line/pattern scanner is deterministic, needs **no JVM to index a Gradle repo**, and everything dynamic (loops, computed coordinates, convention plugins) stays honestly `resolved=0`. `gradle/libs.versions.toml` **is** parsed exactly (BurntSushi/toml) — TOML has a real grammar.

## Design (recorded in dlog)

- **Symbols** (no new `SymbolKind`s): `project.<:path>` and `settings` as kind **`resource`** — the #39 Kustomization lesson repeated: module-kind anchors are invisible to retrieval's seed selection (the first cut with module-kind scored **42%** micro; resource-kind scores **100%** on the same golden — its own dlog record). `task.<name>` (explicit `tasks.register`/`create`/Groovy `task x {` only), `libs.<accessor>` / `libs.plugins.<accessor>` catalog entries (dash/underscore keys normalized to Gradle's dot accessor form).
- **Edges**: settings `include` → project symbols (imports); `implementation(project(":core"))` in Kotlin DSL and `implementation project(':core')` in Groovy DSL → project symbols; `libs.x` on dependency-configuration lines / `alias(libs.plugins.x)` → catalog entries; each catalog entry → its **version-dropped coordinate** (`group:artifact`, the same #35 specifier style as image tag-stripping — the `links.json` entry point for in-house libraries the issue anticipated); `dependsOn` → task symbols (attributed to the nearest task context — a line scanner has no brace tree, recorded simplification); plugin ids (`id()` / `kotlin("jvm")` → `org.jetbrains.kotlin.jvm` / `apply plugin:`) → imports `resolved=0`.
- **Routing** via `claims()` (#40 mechanism): `*.gradle` / `*.gradle.kts` / **exactly `gradle/libs.versions.toml`** — claiming all `.toml` would swallow `Cargo.toml` / `pyproject.toml` (tested).

## Evaluation (ADR-4)

Fixture `eval/fixtures/gradle-taskflow` (multi-project, Kotlin + Groovy DSL mixed, version catalog) and golden (5 cases). Baseline `docs/gradle-baseline.md`:

- **micro recall 100% (12/12), 5/5 perfect**, unresolved 11 (external coordinates / plugin ids / undeclared task — all by design)
- The catalog's value shows in `gr-002`: changing `libs.commons-text` reaches only `:app` (catalog consumer), not `:worker` (hardcoded coordinate) — a distinction plain grep cannot make.

## Verification

- `npm run build` + `npm test`: **180/180 pass** (8 new tests: both DSLs, catalog round-trip, specifier discipline, routing exclusions, degrade, capabilities)
- `go build` in `gradle-extractor/`
- `npm run selfindex:check`: `{"stale": false}`

author: philipfweiss
body:
Tracking: #2234 (step 2 follow-up in the RBAC enablement sequence).

Restrictive RBAC depends on an admin recovery path, but the server can start while the configured user has `is_admin=false`. That can lock every operator out, while bypass use is difficult to identify in ordinary authorization logs.

**Why this was missed initially:** #2232 manually promoted `dj` before testing the bypass, so it proved recovery only after a valid admin already existed. It did not exercise cold startup with a missing or invalid admin, or check for a machine-distinct audit event.

This PR makes the recovery path an activation prerequisite:

- **Startup verification**: restrictive RBAC, or `RBAC_REQUIRE_ADMIN=true`, requires every configured `RBAC_ADMIN_USERS` entry to exist as a human user with `is_admin=true`.
- **Local admin seed**: the Compose path seeds `dj` as an admin, updates existing local rows idempotently, and waits for `db-seed` before starting the server.
- **Distinct audit event**: admin bypasses emit one bounded WARNING event on `datajunction.audit.rbac` with `event=rbac_admin_bypass`, actor fields, request count, and `reason=admin_bypass`.

Permissive deployments remain unchanged when admin readiness is disabled. Restrictive deployments fail before serving requests when the configured admin set is missing or invalid. Admin promotion remains an operations and seed concern; this adds no public promotion API.

---
Verification:

1. Started this branch from a fresh slot 2 database. Compose ran `db-seed` before the server, the seeded `dj` row was an admin, and startup verified the configured admin.

```text
./dev.sh up -d
SELECT username, is_admin FROM users WHERE username='dj';
-> dj | t

server log:
rbac_admin_readiness_verified admins=dj

GET http://localhost:8200/health/
-> [{"name":"database","status":"ok"}] HTTP_STATUS:200
POST /basic/login/ username=dj password=dj
-> HTTP_STATUS:200
GET /whoami/
-> {"username":"dj","is_admin":true,...} HTTP_STATUS:200
```

2. Created a namespace and source node through the admin bypass, then checked the dedicated audit event.

```text
POST /namespaces/manual_admin_bypass
-> HTTP_STATUS:201

POST /nodes/source/ {name:"manual_admin_bypass.orders_admin", catalog:"default", schema_:"public", table:"orders_admin", columns:[{name:"id",type:"int"}]}
-> HTTP_STATUS:200

server log:
WARNING datajunction.audit.rbac:
event=rbac_admin_bypass reason=admin_bypass actor=dj actor_id=1 request_count=1 requests=write:namespace/manual_admin_bypass truncated=False
```

3. Removed the configured user's admin flag and restarted only the server. The application refused to start and the health request could not connect.

```text
UPDATE users SET is_admin=false WHERE username='dj';
docker restart dj-s2
GET http://localhost:8200/health/
-> connection reset, HTTP_STATUS:000

server log:
RuntimeError: RBAC break-glass admin verification failed: users without is_admin: dj
ERROR: Application startup failed. Exiting.
```

4. Restored the admin flag and restarted the server. Readiness passed and traffic resumed.

```text
UPDATE users SET is_admin=true WHERE username='dj';
docker restart dj-s2
GET http://localhost:8200/health/
-> [{"name":"database","status":"ok"}] HTTP_STATUS:200
```

body:
## Summary

Ports the five shader effects from the [krd-knt/threejs-graphics](https://github.com/krd-knt/threejs-graphics) reference repo into Scene Studio as fine-grained, independently reusable primitives (`ChannelShift`, `InvertBlend`, `Mosaic`, `GradientFlow`, `SignalNoise`), and adds a `shader-demo` composition that renders all five effects with captions as one demo video.

### What changed?

- Extracted the DepthGallery texture-loading gating (delayRender → load → advance → continueRender, cancelRender on error) into a shared `useImageTexture` hook with a `colorSpace` option; `ImagePlane` now consumes it (behavior-preserving — verified by the unchanged test suite and a byte-identical `primitive-depth-gallery` still).
- Added shared internals (not exported as primitives): `ScreenQuad` (fullscreen NDC quad + ShaderMaterial with pierced-prop uniform updates), `coverFit` (cover-fit UV math + shared vertex shader), `clampUnit`.
- Added the five effect primitives with inline template-string GLSL (no webpack change) and pure, node-tested motion/math modules.
- Registered five `primitive-*` Studio demos plus the `shader-demo` composition (5 scenes × 150 frames = 750 frames / 25 s) and a README table row.

### Why was this changed?

- The reference repo's effects were locked inside a window-global rAF harness; Scene Studio needs them as deterministic, per-frame-driven building blocks for future compositions (#392).

## Deliberate adaptations from the reference

- Cover-fit UV mapping replaces the window-aspect UV hack (correct for arbitrary image aspects on the 9:16 canvas).
- The noise shader gets a per-frame seed (the original was frozen at seed 1) and a fullscreen NDC quad (the original used an MVP-projected centered quad).
- Mosaic cells are quantized square in screen space via the canvas aspect.
- Dead uniforms (`uTime`/`uResolution` where unused) are dropped; GLSL magic scale factors moved to testable TypeScript constants.
- `GradientFlow` uses linear elapsed time (the reference wrapped accumulated time in `Math.sin`, slowly rocking the field back and forth instead of flowing).
- Image-effect textures load untagged (`NoColorSpace`) because `ShaderMaterial` has no output color transform — verified byte-faithful passthrough at `amount = 0` (background pixel exactly `#474a4d` at frame 0).

## Rendering note

Uniform values are routed through React Three Fiber pierced props (`uniforms-<name>-value`) instead of mutating the captured uniforms record during render: during sequential rendering (`frameloop='never'` + advance-per-frame), render-body mutations were not picked up after the initial mount — effects froze at their mount-time amount. Pierced props go through the reconciler's commit-phase applyProps, the same mechanism DepthGallery's animated props already rely on. Verified by a segment-range render showing the inversion peak mid-segment.

author: martyinspace
body:
## Why

Reopening a conversation re-read and re-decrypted the **entire** thread from SQLite every time (and again on every 3s poll). With the inverted list (#36) you no longer *see* it happen, but the cost is still there and grows with thread length. This makes it flat, the way WhatsApp does it.

## What

- `getMessages` accepts `{ limit }` and returns only the newest N messages (selected newest-first, flipped back to chronological — callers see the identical shape; the no-limit path is unchanged).
- The chat opens with a **50-message window**. Scrolling up to the oldest loaded message (`onEndReached` of the inverted list = the visual top) grows the window by another 50. If a load comes back short of the window, there's no older history and the grow is skipped. The window resets to one page on each (re)open.
- Poll ticks re-read only the current window, so background decrypt cost stays constant no matter how long the thread gets.

## Known edge

A reply-quote referencing a message older than the loaded window shows "Message not found" until the window grows to include it. Tap-to-jump already handled missing indices gracefully. Can be revisited if it bugs anyone in practice.

author: menno420
body:
## The assembled picture

**Idea.** `menno420/idea-engine` → `ideas/product-forge/bt-controller-plan-2026-07-17.md` (blob `970edbfc`): the phone as a *customizable Bluetooth-HID controller*. Android is viable but the HID **device** role sits behind an OEM compile-flag on `BluetoothHidDevice` (API 28+), so `registerApp()` must be **probed at runtime**, never assumed; iOS is walled off from the HID role at the OS level.

**Slice 1 (merged, PR #27).** A portable, dependency-free Python **verdict engine** — `products/phone-controller/src/capability.py` (`evaluate(ProbeInput) -> Verdict`, codes `SUPPORTED_CLASSIC_HID` / `BLE_HOGP_FALLBACK` / `OEM_DISABLED` / `OS_TOO_OLD` / `IOS_WALLED` / `UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM`) — plus the receiver-compat matrix, a CLI, and stdlib tests. The decision table is kept out of any UI so it stays unit-testable with no hardware.

**What this PR adds** — an Android module under `products/phone-controller/android/`:

- **`capability-core/`** — a pure-JVM **Kotlin port** of `capability.py`: the same verdict enum, the same `ProbeInput` fields, the same branch order, with JVM unit tests (13, all green) that prove it stays in **lockstep** with the Python core. SDK-free on purpose, so CI can build it green with no Android toolchain.
- **`app/`** — the **real** `BluetoothHidDeviceTransport`: it binds the profile proxy (`getProfileProxy(HID_DEVICE)`), calls `registerApp(...)` with a fixed media-remote SDP record + HID report descriptor (**this is the runtime OEM-flag probe** — an API-28+ phone rejected here is exactly the engine's `OEM_DISABLED` case), sends input reports on the interrupt channel (`sendReport(...)`), and **feeds the probe result into the shared `evaluate()`** so the phone reaches the same verdict as the portable core. A fixed Consumer-Control media remote (play/pause, next, prev, mute, vol ±, stop) is the skeleton HID device; customizable layouts are Slice 3+. This module is reviewable skeleton source and is **not** built by CI yet (it needs the Android SDK + AGP).

## Decide-and-flag choices

1. **CI target = pure-Kotlin verdict port, not `assembleDebug`.** A JVM unit-test lane needs no Android SDK download (far more reliable in CI) and tests the load-bearing decision model directly; the real `BluetoothHidDevice` transport can't be unit-tested without hardware, so `assembleDebug` would only prove compilation — lower value. Upgrade to `assembleDebug` in Slice 3 when there's a UI worth compiling. *(Reversible.)*
2. **Split into two PRs (this one carries no workflow file).** Recon of `.github/workflows/merge-on-green.yml` (lines 171–173: any PR whose diff touches `.github/workflows/**` is skipped as **owner-merge-only**) confirms a workflow file would park this whole PR. So this **code** PR auto-lands; a tiny companion **workflow** PR (`android-ci.yml` only) parks owner-gated with its blocker named.
3. **`app/` kept out of `settings.gradle.kts`.** So `gradle :capability-core:test` stays Android-toolchain-free; the transport + manifest + AGP config are skeleton source, wired into the build in Slice 3.
4. **No `control/status.md` / `control/inbox.md` edits** (one-writer rule — the coordinator's). **Did not** arm auto-merge or self-merge (per directive); opened READY and left the repo's own `merge-on-green.yml` to land it once green and the session card flips `complete`.

## Verification

- `cd products/phone-controller/android && gradle :capability-core:test` → **BUILD SUCCESSFUL**, 13 tests passed (run locally, Gradle 8.14.3 / JDK 21).
- The Slice-1 Python suite remains the canonical decision table; `CapabilityTest.demoScenariosMatchPythonCore` mirrors `capability.py`'s `DEMO_SCENARIOS`.

Born-red session card: `.sessions/2026-07-17-controller-android-transport.md` (flips to `complete` as the last commit).
